DOC:External-Theaters.selector: p, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, blockquote, pre, li, th, td

leaves.text: This page records the duty watches and handovers of goods that ran from Seoul out to the corridors beyond it.
Anguk, Gwanghwamun, Sinnae, and Guui jointly ran the gate quarantine and the repatriation registers along the Imjin River Gate corridor.
Linked states: S10 Anguk Order, S11 Seongha Group, S12 Sinnae Transport, S06 Republic of Korea Government, S14 Achasan Gate

At the temporary quarantine post below the Imjin levee, an Anguk Order guide held the return roll up to a flashlight beam. In northern Korea, communities around Kaesong and Hwanghae entrust family letters and replies to southbound columns from 2032. Some leave and others remain; part of this traffic later reaches the Imjin return window. In 2048 residents around Pyongyang repair ferries and parts of bridges over the Taedong to keep markets reachable. Each crossing asks a different price, and one agreement guarantees no safety at the next. This civilian history does not settle the survival of a central government or its military power throughout northern Korea.

The Seongha Group convoy wet its wheels on the muddy road outside the gate, and the Sinnae transfer window opened only the family queue first. In Gangwon, after columns vanish during the winter of 2028, guides and mountain residents place food and ropes on both sides of passes and agree when to withdraw. River posts and mountain routes support different communities. The Sluice’s 2097 contracts in Yangpyeong and Chuncheon and the rejection of the city-name petition in 2099 stand, but Chuncheon traders and boat crews keep using their city’s name in the market. The contractual title Second Sluice grants neither rule over all Gangwon nor control of residents’ daily language.
A Republic of Korea Government jusa clerk from Gwanghwamun traced the ink bleed on a forged kinship certificate, and the Achasan gateway post split the seal key into two pieces.
Verified geography: Only the public terrain anchors — the Imjin–Han confluence and the northern transfer and refugee corridor — were used.
Staging nodes: the roll cross-check window of Anguk and Gwanghwamun → Sinnae's neutral transfer window → Guui's double-seal window → the temporary quarantine post beneath the Imjin levee

Outbound boundary: Family journeys in Kaesong and Hwanghae and ferry life around Pyongyang are authored history. Detailed waypoints, crossing procedures, and travel times beyond the Imjin quarantine post remain unset.
Travel time: Not set. Movement cost and openness were judged by water level, quarantine waits, passage rights, and the state of the refugee columns.

Seasonal conditions: In the rainy season the flood level and the state of levee access changed whether the sluice stairs and the quarantine post stood open. / In the dry season and in winter, the ecological pressure that followed food traces could overlap the passage along the northwestern edge. / On days when the bird migration overlapped, the low-noise window and the slow-speed window of the bridge and depot lead tracks were adjusted together.

Suspension conditions: when the cross-check of the roll's original and its copies was unfinished / when custody of the two halves of the sealing key was unconfirmed / when the water-level warning and the evacuation leftovers occupied the same stairs
Recording rule: Closure was recorded not as deletion of the passage but as a state change carrying cause and reopening conditions.

Goods · nighttime detour boxes of grain and medicine: The sealing ledger of goods was kept separate from the family register, and at every hand-off the seal state and receipt signature were left together.
Power · the northern emergency battery relay: Even when the escort ran late, custody of the capacitors and the quarantine judgment of persons were never gathered into one hand.
Records · the return-roll hashes and the family-reunion queue: Reissue records never replaced the original; damage facts, issuer, and collation grounds were left on separate lines.

Separation rule: Medicine and food boxes, repatriation registers, and sealing keys passed through different hand-off procedures. One suspicion or delay never became grounds for the automatic refusal of another item.

XT01-CP-ANKUK-GWANGHWAMUN · the Anguk and Gwanghwamun roll cross-check window: cross-check of originals and copies of the return rolls and kinship certificates, and the record of reissue / whether the roll was damaged, grounds for reissue, discrepancy between certificate and ledger
XT01-CP-SINNAE · the Sinnae transfer window: splitting and joining of the family queue and the neutral convoys / the passage window, responsibility for receiving the convoy, need for medical priority

XT01-CP-GUI-IMJIN · the Guui seal window and the temporary Imjin quarantine post: dual custody of the sealing key and handover of the Seoul-side quarantine / the custody record of the two key halves, the state of the box seals, water-level safety of the passage window
Record language: The Seoul-side ledgers were kept in Korean.
Interpreter rule: Interpretation was connected to Seoul's existing interpretation corridor only when the party concerned requested it.
confirmed: Mutually independent registers or seal records collated, with responsible issuers and hand-off agents remaining.
withheld: Only a single escort record or damaged copy remained, needing re-collation.
hearsay: Only family contact or movement rumor existed, unconfirmed by register, seal, or receipt record.
Prohibited inference: From word-of-mouth alone, no outside polity's policy, a traveler's origin, kinship, or crimes were fixed.

S10 Anguk Order: It kept the continuity of return-roll reissue and of the family tablets and queue. It receives northern and Gangwon columns while distinguishing affiliation, lodging, and eligibility for instruction. Beggars’ Sect Dog-Beating Staff transmission remains separate from Shaolin transmission; visiting grants no martial art. / leverage: Anguk's custody of the rolls and its guide staff / red line: It did not fix a family relation on a damaged copy alone.

S11 Seongha Group: It kept the handover of convoys and emergency batteries unbroken. It exchanges information and parts with repair workers in places such as Daejeon, without a nationwide communications monopoly or an obligation for Min Ung-gi to return. / leverage: preparation of the Gangnam convoy and the surviving cooling and computing keys / red line: It did not turn custody of the batteries into a power to judge the rolls.

S12 Sinnae Transport: It kept the neutral transfer of the family queue and of the medical and goods convoys. It escorts contracted journeys as far as outside handoff posts, without running a scheduled train across the peninsula. / leverage: the Sinnae transfer slots and the emergency-convoy ledger / red line: It did not close the transfer window on one state's order alone.

S06 Republic of Korea Government: It screened the authenticity of kinship certificates and accreditation records by a public procedure. From the Gyeonggi post in Goyang it seeks recognition from outside envoys, but recognition does not entail obedience. / leverage: the Gwanghwamun seal and the grammar of record accreditation / red line: It did not judge a traveler an outside enemy on suspicion of forgery.

S14 Achasan Gate: It spread the safety responsibility for the gate seal and the departure window. It prioritizes existing gate safety and passage and has no direct diplomatic relationship with Tsushima or Jeju. / leverage: the sealing procedure of the Guui sluices and the Achasan outposts / red line: It did not leave the sealing key in the sole custody of one person or one house.

G01: When the evacuation column's food traces overlapped the flood level, the Wild Boar could occupy the sluice stairs. / response: The leftovers were diverted to a separate sealed collection, and the passage times were divided. / nonlethal constraint: A wholesale cull scattered the herd into the alleys, so it was kept only as a last resort.

G06: When the migratory birds' movement along the northern wind path overlapped the sluice inspection, access to the bridges and the depot narrowed. / response: The roosts and perches of each functional flock and the low-noise inspection window were adjusted. / nonlethal constraint: The choice of drying the water surface to drive the flock out left an ecological and water-quality cost.

Residents making handoffs around Hamhung and Chongjin and the Dokdo outpost’s people are described, but exact mineral and fuel types, quantities, and extractors remain unset. Outpost staffing, carrying capacity, resupply quantities, and sailing schedules are not fixed numerically.
The names and acts of outside governments, state enterprises, and armed groups were not set.
Outside languages and returning workers’ origins are not established solely by counseling interpretation requests.
XT04-SC1: The Eastern Command's Amsa watch disclosed the freight-car weight log, and Sinnae adjusted the transfer slots
XT04-SC2: The Changdong wheel works divides the winter fuel queue and Jegi-dong receives the frostbitten
XT04-SC3: The Achasan gate inspects the mineral-sample seals and scraps the forged origin tags
Yeouido, Yeongdeungpo, Gwanghwamun, City Hall, Yangjae, and Myeongdong entrusted residual satellite bands, aid manifests, and diaspora contact through the Incheon Trust gateway.
Linked states: S09 Yeouido Investment Federation, S01 The Sluice, S06 Republic of Korea Government, S16 Jeongdong Federation, S03 Taeuk Group, S15 Myeongdong Archdiocese

On the roof of the Yeouido Investment Federation hall, residual-band lottery numbers were circulated. On the capital outskirts in 2027, rail workers and refugees toward Incheon and Paju divide loads among backs and carts at the ends of maintainable tracks, creating temporary markets. Not all these markets later become Junction termini. Eastern Command’s 2098 guard districts in Hanam, Namyangju, Uijeongbu, and Yeoncheon, the Junction’s 2100 tolls at Incheon and Paju rail termini, Taeuk Group’s 2101 Seongnam and Suwon workplaces, the 2104 Yeongjong branch, and the 2106 Gyeonggi administrative post in Goyang remain. Outside those posts, residents evade call-ups and tolls or trade directly, bringing them into conflict with Seoul interests.

The Sluice's sluice watch matched the water-pump operating times to those numbers, and a Republic of Korea Government jusa clerk posted the delivery-list hash in the citizens' observation cell. Seoul’s sixteen states hold contracts, workplaces, and registers at gateways; they do not govern all seven regions of the peninsula. XT01–XT05 identify relationships and corridors, not new states. Arriving people and goods create consequences within Seoul’s existing opening territories and subway movement network.
A Jeongdong Federation branch chief opened a turnback line carrying only boxes of overseas remittance records, and a Taeuk Group deputy manager switched off the rail terminal's false-positive alarm.
The Myeongdong counseling window did not throw away the multilingual queue tickets however late the night grew.
Verified geography: Only the general concepts of satellite, aid, and disaster cooperation and the level of public international-organization names were used as fact anchors.

Staging nodes: Yeouido's remaining-bandwidth and ledger window → Yeongdeungpo's water-hour window → Gwanghwamun's citizen-observation hash window → City Hall's turnback record window → Yangjae's orbital-terminal correction window → Myeongdong's multilingual counseling window → the unnamed Incheon trust receipt window

Outbound boundary: Existing capital-outskirts contacts, including the Incheon and Paju rail termini and the Yeongjong branch, remain. The Incheon trust’s exact receiving site, detailed port and road routes, and overseas aid parties remain unset.
Travel time: Not set. Transmit bands, pump power, manifest hashes, terminal state, counseling consent, and receipt confirmation set waiting and movement cost.

Seasonal conditions: In weeks when frozen and deep-sea protein residue piled up, the burden on the transfer stevedore elevators and the sealing line could grow. / When the sea wind's direction overlapped the drainage burden, the cost of the choice to pass the water to the outskirts was recorded. / When the remaining bandwidth overlapped an old call format, the automatic relief equipment's false alarms were judged as a separate state.

Suspension conditions: when only a reception log existed, with no list hash and no physical receipt / when the citizen-observation record of the transmission key was missing / when an uncorrected false alarm on an orbital terminal left the recipient unclear
Recording rule: An unreceived orbital signal was not read as any outside party's command; it passed to the next stage only with reproducible logs and receipt records.

Delivery goods · the delivery-goods allocation list, medicine capsules, and frozen protein: Receive logs, manifest hashes, and physical receipts were recorded separately; ration order was never fixed on one alone.

Power and communications · the emergency transmission power quota and the reservation of the satellite's remaining bandwidth: Band lottery results were published together with pump running times, and the transmit key was never kept alone.

Families and records · the waiting list for reconnecting families abroad, multilingual counseling, and remittance records: Counseling consent and remittance records were separated from the receipt and isolation judgment of aid goods.

Separation rule: Aid promises, received signals, family contact, and interpretation requests had different evidentiary levels; one item's uncertainty never became grounds for another's automatic refusal.

XT05-CP-YEOUIDO-YEONGDEUNGPO · the Yeouido bandwidth window and the Yeongdeungpo water watch: It cross-checked the public drawing of lots for the remaining bandwidth against the pump running hours. / the bandwidth lottery record, the transmission power quota, the pump timetable

XT05-CP-GWANGHWAMUN-SICHEONG · the Gwanghwamun observation-hash window and the City Hall turnback record window: It confirmed separately the citizen observation of the delivery-list hash and the delivery turnback record. / the list hash, the observation signature, the turnback receipt record

XT05-CP-YANGJAE-MYEONGDONG · the Yangjae terminal-correction window and the Myeongdong counseling window: It handled separately the orbital terminals' false alarms and the counseling and interpretation requests. / the terminal false-alarm record, consent to counseling, the family-contact waiting list
Record language: The Seoul-side band, receipt, and counseling ledgers were kept in Korean.

Interpreter rule: Myeongdong's multilingual queue tickets were a tool for taking self-declarations and interpretation requests, and connected Seoul's existing interpretation resources only when requested.
confirmed: Independent grounds among receive logs, manifest hashes, and physical receipts were collated, and a receiving authority remained.
withheld: Only a receive log or manifest hash remained, with physical receipt or terminal calibration outstanding.
hearsay: Only talk of overseas family contact, aid promises, and orbital calls, without reproducible records.
Prohibited inference: From unreceived signals, interpretation requests, or remittance records alone, no outside authority's command, family's survival, or traveler's affiliation was fixed.

S09 Yeouido Investment Federation: It kept the public drawing of lots for the remaining bandwidth and the transmission ledger. Using the Yeongjong branch and currency exchange, it invests in ship and grain trades, but counterparties may reject its certificates. / leverage: the investment ledgers and transmission memory of the Yeouido hall / red line: It did not turn the bandwidth lottery into a private allocation or a sole transmission key.

S01 The Sluice: It kept the bandwidth and delivery schedule meshed with the safe running of the water pumps. It maintains Chuncheon waterway contracts and trades beyond the posts without demanding tribute from all Gangwon. / leverage: the Yeongdeungpo treatment and sluice watch / red line: A transmission demand did not cover over the water-safety record.

S06 Republic of Korea Government: It preserved the form of the delivery-list hash and the citizen-observation record. From the Gyeonggi post in Goyang it seeks recognition from outside envoys, but recognition does not entail obedience. / leverage: Gwanghwamun's record accreditation and seal / red line: It did not make an unobserved list into a ration right or grounds for quarantine.

S16 Jeongdong Federation: It published the carrying conditions of the delivery turnback and the remittance records. From its contacts with Seongnam and Siheung workers it engages in long-distance escort and ship-repair pay and return terms, without representing all outside workers. / leverage: the City Hall turnback line and the union ledgers / red line: It did not use the remittance records as a tool for judging passage rights or labor eligibility.

S03 Taeuk Group: It corrected the orbital terminals' false alarms, separating the recipient from the safety of the equipment. It maintains its Seongnam and Suwon workplaces and seeks parts and labor from Yeongnam dismantlers, but cannot order Busan shipowners to sail. / leverage: the Yangjae maintenance depot and the memory of field humanoid maintenance / red line: It did not bypass citizen observation and the receipt hash on the grounds of correcting a false alarm.

S15 Myeongdong Archdiocese: It did not discard the multilingual counseling and the family-contact waiting list, and kept the form of accreditation. It debates recognition of marriages and settlement established outside Seoul, without reducing the parties’ choices to a single return order. / leverage: the Myeongdong altar and the diocesan rolls / red line: It did not use the language of counseling or a family's story as a stigma for rations or quarantine.

G05: When frozen and deep-sea protein residue piled up, the Brown Rat could extend its branch nests as far as the stevedore elevator passages. / response: Leftover collection and a temporary double-sealing line were run first, and the stevedore hours were divided. / nonlethal constraint: Refugees were not sealed off by a contagion stigma or by wholesale toxic spraying.

G10: The choice to pass the water in the direction of the sea wind could leave one season's burden on the Flood-Mold Breath Cluster's corridor and the outer storage grounds. / response: Before the drainage choice, the residents' roll and the right to stop the pumps were confirmed, and the contamination burden was published. / nonlethal constraint: Passing the water to the outskirts so that only the center of Seoul shed its cost was not used as a costless solution.

G15: When a delivery-goods code was received, the Care Wheel could raise both the supply and the intensity of quarantine. / response: The roll, the consent hash, and the power to each bed were cross-checked, blocking over-supply and new confinement. / nonlethal constraint: The welfare block was not burned, and the locks of every bed were not cut at once.

G25: The medicine capsules on the XT05 delivery list could pile up with an old simulated recipient. / response: The recipient mark, the delivery table, and the loading bay were cross-checked against the field treatment record. / nonlethal constraint: Instead of destroying the main transmitter at once, the rescue double row and the citizen passage were assessed together.
Trigger: The Sangam transmission's public residual-band lottery and the Yeouido water watch's pump times overlapped in the same window.
Conflict: The demand to secure the band first and save communications collided with the demand to leave the citizen-observation hash first and keep the receipt ledgers trusted.
First decision: Choose whether to enter onto the ration list the medicine capsules that have only receive logs, or hold until observation, hash, and receipt confirmation.

XT05-ENTRY-BAND-LOTTERY · Yeouido's remaining-bandwidth lottery window: a citizen assistant cross-checking the lottery, the pump hours, and the observation signatures / first decision: It decided which condition to meet first, the speed of the bandwidth allocation or the completion of citizen observation.

XT05-ENTRY-MYEONGDONG-CONSENT · the Myeongdong counseling window: an assistant recording the family-contact waiting list and the consent to interpretation requests / first decision: It decided whether to withhold as hearsay a family contact with no receipt record, or to send it to the turnback record for the terminal to be checked again.

Existing capital-outskirts contacts, including the Incheon and Paju rail termini and the Yeongjong branch, remain. The Incheon trust’s exact receiving site, detailed port and road routes, and overseas aid parties remain unset.
Outside aid parties, the operators of orbital assets, and overseas families' whereabouts were not set.
The volumes of aid goods, frozen protein, and medicine capsules were not set.
Outside languages and communicating parties’ identities are not established solely by Seoul’s interpretation and logs.
XT05-SC1: Sangam transmission holds a public lottery on residual bands and Yeouido matches the water watch's times
XT05-SC2: The Seoul Station Records Bureau keeps the manifest hash and Suseo opens the delivery turn line
XT05-SC3: Magok corrects the orbital false positives and Garak extends the separated-family counseling window

leaves.text: The generation of 2126 placed the night of the Great Blackout at the start of events. The canon name was The Great Blackout, and the year 2026. The story's present was 2126. The institutional and religious changes of the century between were written year by year in the Seoul Subway States Timeline 2026–2126.

Faith did not arise because a stationmaster or a Moderator proclaimed it. It grew on the night the announcements went silent, on the morning the sluices opened, in the person who died before the platform's yellow line. Occupying a gu did not change temperament.

In the Korea of 2026 there had been no religious majority. Pew Research 2010 wrote 46% non-religious, 29% Christian, 23% Buddhist (Pew, viewed 2026-09-17). The lack of a majority vote did not mean the institutions were weak. The pulpits, altars, General Directorate, and chapels crossed the century on real estate, registers, relief, and calendars, and the watchkeepers' grandchild's grandchild was the head of the time. Living pastors, church logos, and presbytery arms were not carried onto opening-day persons. The state names Sermon Registry State, Cathedral Accreditation State, Sangha Relief State, and Won Buddhism were not erased.

The Seoul of 2026 was still the capital of one country. The Military Manpower Administration took volunteer intake selection; the conglomerate families controlled the affiliates with small stakes; the pulpits, altars, General Directorate, and chapels held real estate and registers. Water, rail, markets, medicine, and communications ran on one call mesh of institutional and family ledgers. The hands that later became states grew from that year's watch rosters.
B. The Night of the Great Blackout

On the night of the Great Blackout the fleet calls, GNSS, the mobile networks, and the licensing servers stopped waiting for one another. The grid SCADA, belonging to the same mesh, folded the lights. The Yeouido plant, the Yeonji-dong General Assembly, the Myeongdong altar, the Jogyesa General Directorate, the Heukseok chapel, and the Gwanghwamun complex exercised emergency powers to save their own jurisdictions. The joint command mesh broke that night. A century later the Yeouido hall had split off as a neighboring state, and the Yeongdeungpo Station sluice house sold the western water. When the powers were returned stayed the seed of a century of legitimacy disputes.

The clock on which manufacture died and the clock on which society changed ran separately. The fabs stopped within a few years, but for offices to become ranks, the generation that remembered the shell of the corporation that had turned the fabs had to die. The children who received the keys still used the words "company," "General Assembly," and "diocese"; their grandchildren read the keys as the family's signature. When the grandchild's grandchild sat in the head-of-state seat, the emergency committee had become the creation oral record and the watch roster a charter. That gap was the hundred years. The canon of the calendar was in the Scenario Timeline.

In the First Water Compact, those who read it as public rights split from those who read it as a protection contract. The military-household register dispute divided supporters of household service registration from those who refused it. The Sixteen Banners rose. The Merit Subjects' Winter scattered or hardened titles in different states, and the Second Water Compact set the minimum line, standards, and emergency convoys again.

On opening day, the central water-and-parts contract carried from earlier records expired. Moderator Im Hajun of the Sermon Registry State had disappeared before the opening. O Gyeongjae took the Moderator's seat through General Assembly accreditation, and the adopted heir Im Chowon remained in the teacher's seat holding half the hammer. The price of water rose, medical convoys ran late, and smaller states began overlapping contracts. The water contract, Assembly registers, and rites became entangled in the same dispute.

The main stage was the Seoul subway. The capitals were subway stations. Yeongdeungpo, Guro, and Yangjae were not state names but the stations of the capitals. The list and origins of the sixteen states were canon in the Sixteen States of Seoul.

Theocracy was the form of government of three of the sixteen states, not the state religion of all Seoul. The titles kept the words those institutions used in 2026, and the tiers followed the five layers of Offices and Ranks. No living pastor, sitting bishop, or order logo was moved onto an opening-day person. Those seated at the opening were the 2126 generation of the Characters.

In 2026 the General Assembly of the Sermon Registry State held registers, relief, and church real estate at the General Assembly Hall, 29 Daehak-ro 3-gil, Yeonji-dong, Jongno-gu. The 29% Christian of Pew 2010 was no majority, and the majority within it was Protestant. Weak at the ballot, the pulpits were strong in real estate.

On the night of the Great Blackout the General Assembly registers became the watch roster. When the announcements went silent, the churches' emergency lights became the watch's fire. A century later the surviving pulpit real estate lay in Gangnam, so the capital of the time was Samsung Station. The state name stood as the General Assembly's own name.

The Moderator of the time was O Gyeongjae. Im Hajun descended from the surety line of the Second Water Compact in the creation oral record but did not overlap that body. Before vanishing he left three wills and sealed the original chest of the pump-cleaning process. Im Chowon was the adopted heir who received half the hammer, and her rank was teacher. O Gyeongjae held the other half — General Assembly accreditation — and sat in the Moderator's seat. The trade aliases "pump-technology steward" and "treatment-principle transmitter" did not go into the ledger cells. The cell's title was Moderator.

The public faith was the Pump-Workshop Rite. It bound pump and workshop into one rite and read the hand that brought water as a blessing. When Han Jaemok, elected monarch of the Sluice, read the same tap as contract, the Samsung Station pulpit read that tap as blessing. The House-Secret Rite lay inside and traveled with the succession dispute. Ttukseom was not the capital; the drawings of the Ttukseom Heat-Source House remained only a house rite on unclaimed land.

What was not brought in: living pastors' real names, church logos, presbytery names, Yoido Full Gospel Church. Lineage names grown from subway wreckage stayed fiction, and the state name was not erased.

In 2026 the Cathedral Accreditation State held the altar and diocesan registers of Myeongdong Cathedral, 74 Myeongdong-gil, Jung-gu. Accreditation of marriage, adoption, and memorial rites came from that altar.

After the Great Blackout the altar moved memorial and marriage accreditation onto paper registers. A century on, the real estate and the order of relief remained. The diocese of the time was a state accrediting marriages and memorial rites at Myeongdong Station. The Bishops' Conference building on Myeonmok-ro, Gwangjin, remained only an outer warehouse of the diocese.

The archbishop of the time was Nam Yungyeong. The title was archbishop; the trade alias was auction mediator. The hand that had kept the scales of the Seoul Station Inventory House unbroken sat in that seat. Garak's price hub stood empty as unclaimed land, and the archdiocese could not feed that empty ledger.

The public faith was the Auction-Disclosure Rite. When the bell rang, that day's price was set. The bell of the distribution-and-consumption lineage overlapped here with the theocracy's altar. At a station that took down its altar, the event record broke off.
What was not brought in: sitting bishops' real names and diocesan arms.

In 2026 the Sangha Relief State held the memorial tablets, temple rolls, and rite calendar at Jogyesa and the General Directorate, 55 Ujeongguk-ro, Jongno-gu. The 23% Buddhist of Pew was not a 2126 vote. The reason the order's slot remained was the General Directorate's watch.

After the Great Blackout the General Directorate kept the tablets and the temple rolls. The capital of the time was Anguk Station. The state name stood as the order's own name. Other orders like Taego and Cheontae were not opened as a seventeenth state.

The abbot at the opening was Baek On. His title was abbot; the trade alias was refugee delegate. The hand that had kept the register chests of the Bukhansan Bogukmun Return Society unbroken sat in that seat. The Bukhansan refuge was not a Hu but a vacancy, used as no state name. The lodging rite remained in the register chests beside the Anguk tablets.

The public faith was the lodging oath. The habit of giving lodging to those crossing the mountain had hardened into the order's teaching. The tablets and relief were the Jogye Order's sovereignty. Medicine was sold by the Jegi-dong Medical Neutrality League. Though the windows overlapped, the state name was not divided.
What was not brought in: splitting particular head temples into other state names, and raising the refugee vacancy into one of the sixteen slots.

In 2026 Won Buddhism held the charter and the dharma-officer watch at the Seoul chapel and Sotaesan Memorial Hall, Heukseok-dong, Dongjak-gu. The Iksan headquarters lay outside the city and entered no Seoul slot.

After the Great Blackout the Heukseok dharma-officer watch transcribed the charter. A century later Heukseok Station was Won Buddhism's Seoul capital. Seats were not counted by Pew shares. Where the watch remained, there was the state.
C. Public Religion and the Facts in 2026

The Kyujeongwon head of the time was O Haerin. The title was Kyujeongwon head; the trade alias was cold-trade delegate. The hand that had kept the warehouse keys of the Noryangjin Delivery House unbroken sat in that seat. The Noryangjin market function was scrapped; the credit of ice and short-term stock remained only as a neighboring debt of the Heukseok chapel watch.

The public faith was the Settlement-Right Rite. Ice and short-term stock were credit. When the power cut, the beep died; the doctrine died with it. The main lineage was the ledger lineage. Numbers and charter lay in one ledger.
What was not brought in: bringing the Iksan headquarters in as a Seoul state, and reviving the scrapped Noryangjin market as a capital.
F. Summary of the Three Theocracies

The Sermon Registry State, the Cathedral Accreditation State, and the Sangha Relief State inherited Assembly registers, diocesan registers, and tablets respectively. The Central Technology Preservation Institute established a technology office at Heukseok Station.
Yeonji-dong Assembly Hall registers · church real estate
The Assembly registers become the watch roster. The surviving pulpits are in Gangnam
Paper registers of marriage, adoption, memorial accreditation
Jogyesa · General Directorate tablets · temple rolls
The tablets the General Directorate kept
The Heukseok Seoul chapel · Sotaesan Memorial Hall charter
Heukseok Station, Kyujeongwon head O Haerin
The Yangjae Machineworks Company used verification like doctrine but raised no chapel to a state faith. Even when a state forced public rites, the station crowds kept a mixed practice.
The Everyday That Grew in Stations

The units that collided on the map were not state names. In the Seoul of later days the routes, the gu, and the stations held identity power. The sixteen territory slots were kept. A slot was no flat partition but a living sphere binding treatment plants, depots, head offices, assemblies, dioceses, orders, transfers, and mountain-refuge corridors.

The station chapels remained as concourse notice boards, yellow lines, barrier gates, and ad frames; the gu chapels as government-complex entrances and ration windows. The route chapels stood as the milestones of depots and main-line tunnels. Injection from above failed. Even when Han Jaemok forced the Water-Compact Rite on the western lesser states, the Cheonwang depot's engineers held their bolt rites first. Even when Bae Ujin planted the Protected-Water Rite in the east, Jegi-dong applied the treatment principle to friend and foe alike.

The Sinjeong depot district lined up before the ration taps instead of reciting with the sluice guards. In the Cheonwang depot district the order of closing the barrier gates was the prayer. Within the same west, a different station saw different taboos. The southeast did not look like one lump. The Gangnam cooling key, the Samsung pulpit, the Yangjae depot, and the Heukseok charter were neighbors that touched different things before the meal.
Families in the same living area who worshipped the same ruins or symbols belonged to one lineage. A change in teaching rarely changed that lineage.

A faith was a named community with a meeting place and clergy. Moderators, archbishops, abbots, directors, stationmasters, priests, and guilds named such communities. A faith changed when communities merged or split.
Doctrine and teaching set taboos, rites, succession qualifications, and the words of oaths. Factions and heresy trials changed these terms.

Even within one route-map lineage, a faith that read transfer as salvation fought a faith that read only the terminal as rest. That was sectarianism. When one line of doctrine changed, marriage, adoption, vassal oath, ration priority, and grounds of legitimacy changed with it. The sixteen state slots were not increased. The faith slots grew.

Priests were a relation class of persons, powers, trades. Priest and apprentice belong to succession paths. The three theocracies have tier-one offices. Moderator, archbishop, and abbot are offices rather than trade bynames. The head of the Central Technology Preservation Institute also holds an office in a technology-preservation administration.
G. Main Lineages and Public Faith

The main lineage and the public faith need not match. The Yeouido Investment Union was ledger-lineage but its public rite was the On-Time-Broadcast Rite. Won Buddhism was ledger-lineage but its public rite was the Settlement-Right Rite. The Sermon Registry State was pulpit-lineage but its public rite was the Pump-Workshop Rite.

The pulpit, altar, and monastery lineages were left by institutions. The eight below were creative lineages grown from subway wreckage. The starting list was locked. They could later merge or split, but state names were not changed into wreckage-lineage names.
Wreckage Was Not a Manual but a Rite

Severed equipment was not a manual but a rite bowl. When power came, a blessing had been received; when the announcement sounded, the word was fact. A name in the military register meant one could still be mustered.
What was worshipped was facilities and parts. No living king was raised into godhead first. The ruler held the keys of the facility and borrowed legitimacy from it.

Acts of piety were three: retrieval that moved wreckage into chapels, pilgrimage that circled sealed zones on schedule, and offering that set mended parts on the altar. Recorded as plunder, chapel authority was shaved.
Route maps, rolling stock, platforms, barrier gates
Moving a stopped train again is a miracle
A module with charge left is a relic
Fingering what cannot be read from drawings
Drill belongs only to the one who opened the keys
Banknote portraits, ad frames, the checkout beep
When the numbers match, that day's trade is licensed
When water flows, the contract is true
The Government Complex Seoul entrance, empty council rooms
The accreditation seal is the old state's remaining mouth
Water overlapped transport and the military. In Seoul the treatment centers were large, so the sluice lineage stood apart.

The bodies and capacitor modules of sealed underground chassis were relics of Lost Technology. On the story's public face they were not explained as equipment lists. Lamps, roars, and flat underwater shells remained as chapel murals and taboo. The retrieval squad blocked passage on grounds of the rite calendar. Scavenged technology appeared only inside this relic-myth frame.

The default of the pilgrimage route was the depots and plants people kept. The Sinjeong, Cheonwang, Godeok, and Sinnae depots were tied to the capitals of the time. Banghwa, Gunja, Changdong, and Suseo were unclaimed or edge corridors. When forced rites ran two seasons, hidden chapels arose.

The night of the 2026 Great Blackout was the first line of the event record. The arms and marks of the country before it were not gods but faces left on empty pedestals. Later Seoul raised those faces again. What mounted the pedestal was never a person's name.
Government Complex Seoul main building, Gwanghwamun Station entrance
Take the plaque down for firewood and accreditation is void
The tower of empty council rooms
Force the hands and the oath's hour is false
No one rides in a cell whose mark was erased
Water without the mark is guest water, used in no rite
Memory of the old state seal
The empty seal pad of the Gwanghwamun notary window
Stamp only a new seal and deny the old pad, and the Records Bureau refuses
The Gwanghwamun ruin plaza. The Jamsil sculpture is the wall of unclaimed land
Use the space under the sculpture as a market and the auction bell curses the trade
No doctrine of raising a king into godhead existed at the opening. The ruler was the custodian of plaques and marks. When a custodian pasted his own face onto the pedestal, a heresy trial opened.

Old currency, distribution networks, and advertising became after the collapse not price tags but rites. The lineage name of this axis was the distribution-and-consumption lineage. It split from the ledger lineage. The ledger lineage was notarization and accreditation; the distribution-and-consumption lineage was banknotes, frames, and distribution paths. The five below were not the state-faith list of the time. They were factions within the distribution-and-consumption lineage.

The Banknote-Portrait Rite pasted the faces of old banknotes on chapel walls. There were stations that floated them on water to divine the ration order. They counted at Garak's empty windows and in the Noryangjin wreckage. Garak was not a state; Noryangjin was not a capital.

The Ad-Frame Rite held the platform advertisement as the portrait of a saint. Where the model's name was unknown, it was called only "the Honored Frame." The Euljiro concourse of Line 2 was the wall of the Yeouido Investment Union's retainer window. The Jamsil frame wall was the far end of the emptied sphere. Tear a frame out to light a fire, and that station's passage remained unclean for a season.

The Barcode Rite made the sound of the scan a license. There were priests who mimed the beep of dead terminals. It counted in the Dongdaemun night labor and the convenience-store wreckage. Dongdaemun was the Hu on the Medical Neutrality League's west. To take a thing without the sound was not theft but apostasy.

The Auction-Disclosure Rite was the Cathedral Accreditation State's public teaching. When the bell rang, that day's justice was set. It meshed with Nam Yungyeong's scales. Garak's empty ledger could not replace that bell.
The Settlement-Right Rite was Won Buddhism's. Ice and short-term stock were credit. When the power cut, the beep died; the doctrine died with it.

The hidden faction was the Dual-Price Rite. The dual ledgers of Daerim and Garibong attached here. Daerim was the Hu inside the Standards Alliance. A state that did not read the Korean-language price and the other-tongue price as one rite issued a seizure order.

The pilgrimage of the consumption rites was the distribution path — walked from wholesale to retail, from frame wall to checkout. When the path was blockaded, this lineage's chapel authority was shaved first. The open head temples were the Myeongdong altar and the Heukseok chapel. Suseo's empty depot was no priest to escort this rite; Jeong Yura merely leased the Suseo unclaimed zone's drawing chests.
The hand that mended machines was a rite before citizenship. This axis was no single lineage; the route-map, distribution, and fabrication lineages shared one piety.
The bodies counted as four that were touched into godhead.

The rolling-stock car body came first. The departure bell and the door-closing warning remained as prayers. The hand that greased the wheels remained as a remnant rite of the Changdong unclaimed zone, and the barrier-gate key was held by the Changdong Protection House of I Hongwon. Changdong was not a capital.
The substation room came second. The order of raising the breakers was read as a rite, and the distribution watch of the lamp-lighting rite stood as priest.

The lift machinery came third. When the elevator doors opened, passage was permitted, and the steps of the dead escalator remained a pilgrimage stair. It counted in the transfer stations where concourse heights differed.

The factory line came fourth. The conveyors and barrier gates of Guro and Geumcheon remained the body of the law; where the Open-Standards Rite spoke of the bolt, machine worship spoke of the machine the bit into.

When a repair succeeded, a restart ran, and a part was offered to the chapel, the maintenance house's mouth opened. When a restart failed, the maintenance house lost the standing to mend doctrine. Conversely, when a stopped train rolled again, that house could table a doctrine-revision bill for a season. That was this axis's path of reform.

The lamps, roars, and flat shells of the sealed underground lines were the extreme of machine worship. The chapel that saw them as saints and the chapel that saw them as plague split. No one wrote that the control code was deciphered.
The colors and dots of the route map were scripture. The rolling stock was a moving shrine. This lineage took the car-body cell of machine worship.

The Transfer Pact counted at the Neutral Convoy City and the Line Succession State. Whoever transferred, even an enemy, the blades stopped. Terminal Rest overlapped the Wheel-Mobility Rite of the Seocho Computing Group. There were hands that read forcing a train past its terminus as apostasy. That the Jeongdong Federation pushing trains beyond Suseo read as apostasy was a residual teaching left by the leased drawings over the emptied depot. Suseo was not a capital.

The hidden faction rode one color only. It was called the Route-Color Faction. The open station service held it a superstition, but the dispatch houses would not load freight into cars of another color.
The gate that gave water was the altar. The Arisu mark attached as an old-world symbol.

The Water Compact used the Water-Compact Rite close to official faith. Sluice ruler Han Jaemok's legitimacy was unbroken water. The trade alias Water Director-General was no cell of the ledger. The Sermon Registry State's Pump-Workshop Rite bound pump and workshop into one rite. The Escort Protection State held the Protected-Water Rite: water given in exchange for escort. The Gate Military Government had only Guui's limited supply and held on with the Emergency-Water Rite.
When the supply cut, doctrine cracked first. The rites collapsed faster than the state grades.
When the light came on, words carried; when it went out, oaths were void — so believed some stations. It took the substation cell of machine worship.

In the lamp-lighting rite the switchgear watch was priest. The Capacitor-Relic Faction touched modules with charge left. It was no public faith. The Yangjae Machineworks Company saw it as a verification subject, and the chapels saw it as bone not to be touched. The Taeuk Group recognizes Jeongtonghoe as its state religion.
The bolt standard was the law. It took the factory-line cell of machine worship.

The Open-Standards Rite of the Standards Alliance taught that parts anyone could use were citizenship. It meshed with Gang Minseo's repair-standard agenda. Ttukseom was unclaimed; the pumps and bolts had passed into the Standards Alliance's standards, and the House-Secret Rite of the Ttukseom Heat-Source House remained a house rite that posted no drawings to the council. The Seocho Computing Group held the Wheel-Mobility Rite: the hand that rolled a stopped train again was the rite.
The Guro dormitory remnants believed repair labor stood ahead of citizenship. They sat inside the fabrication lineage but took no council seal. The Daerim dormitories were the Hu inside this state.
They fought over whether the word from the speaker was fact.

The On-Time-Broadcast Rite of the Yeouido Investment Union held the programming schedule as prayer. When Chair Choi Jiwoo's cross-verification hardened into doctrine, official announcements waited on the Yeouido schedule. The Sangam transmission was an abandoned axis, not the capital of cross-verification. When trust broke once, the transmission towers became propaganda tools, and then the Silent Faction grew. It turned off the broadcast and trusted paper only.

The platform announcement was this lineage's terminal rite. A stop at which "this station" was never called remained a ghost stop. The wreckage of dead home-shopping voices mixed with the distribution-and-consumption lineage as a hidden rite.
The sanctuary was where the pre-collapse conscription ledgers lay split. It made no new state. It laid rites over conscription remnants and the military registers.

The Muster-Remnant Rite read names, service numbers, and the last muster date. It said the state could still muster. There was no such state. The Key-Drill Rite let only the armory watch touch the drill. Desertion was recorded as apostasy. A squad carrying issue firearms stood out — one reason doctrine kept them out of the drifter's starting gear.

When the Republic of Korea Government brought these registers into the Gwanghwamun archives, the ceremonial guard looked like a barracks. The Record-Accreditation Rite rose into heresy dispute, and the Records Bureau's legitimacy broke.
Numbers and seals were the oracle. This lineage kept the plaque, clock, and state-seal memory of the old-world symbols.

The Record-Accreditation Rite of the Republic of Korea Government saw succession and treaties as void without accreditation. It overlapped Yun Seorin's ambition. The Jeongdong Federation held the Contract-Mediation Rite; the hand that recorded breaches and compensated losses was priest. The Yeouido Investment Union and Won Buddhism were also ledger-lineage; only their public rites split into the programming schedule and the checkout beep.

The ledger lineage did not raise prices into godhead. Price was the distribution-and-consumption lineage's business. When the two lineages shared one window, both seal and bell had to ring for the trade to close.
The lineage of the consumption-rite axis. The Banknote-Portrait Rite, Ad-Frame Rite, Barcode Rite, Auction-Disclosure Rite, and Settlement-Right Rite belonged here.
Myeongdong and Heukseok remained the open head temples; the Euljiro frame wall and the Dongdaemun night labor stood at the far ends. Garak, Jamsil, and Suseo were emptied spheres.
Mixed, It Hid; Forced, It Split
The public faith was posted on the station notice board. Hidden faith sat in switchgear rooms, dormitories, the mouths of sealed galleries, behind frames, in the dual-ledger drawers.

Even when the state set one public rite, the station crowds kept a mixed practice. Hidden faith was a pressure valve. When a great power forced public rites, residents went down into the Capacitor-Relic Faction, the Silent Faction, the Dual-Price Rite, or the Route-Color Faction. On discovery, the grievance and reputation of Powers and Diplomacy moved. Isolation weakened only outside promises; it did not automatically shave the local chapel's legitimacy.

The hidden rites of the corridors brought in no foreign denomination proper names. The habit of taking the interpretation fee first, and the habit of not torquing a bolt without a Vietnamese-language token attached, became teachings. This ban did not mean erasing the state names Sermon Registry State, Cathedral Accreditation State, Sangha Relief State, and Won Buddhism.

Water split before the same tap. Han Jaemok read the lock gate as contract; O Gyeongjae read the pump as blessing. The Myeongdong Auction-Disclosure Rite, the Heukseok Settlement-Right Rite, and Garak's empty ledger fought over one price. The Gwanghwamun Record-Accreditation Rite and the Yeouido On-Time-Broadcast Rite fought over which mouth was fact. When the Amsa Protected-Water Rite tried to bind military rations, the Jegi-dong treatment principle placed the sickbed outside the state. The Guui Emergency-Water Rite and the Achasan ridge almost merged into one military government, but did not. It was no condominium. Bring the armory registers into the Gwanghwamun archives, and the mobilization-register lineage's heresy dispute opened.

When forced rites ran two seasons, a hidden cell grew beside the public one. When two stations of one line were severed for a month, even within one lineage the doctrine slot split in two. Mixing was when one person kept two lineages together — the sluice guards held the Water-Compact Rite in public and, with it, the platform taboo of never stepping on the yellow line. A heretic was the side that had changed doctrine inside the same lineage. The Open-Standards Rite called the House-Secret Rite heretical; the Ttukseom Heat-Source House called it the other way.

Culture was no state ID. The naming keys remained the spheres. The CultureKey of the heir, name-roster, and world ledger was a naming bundle. The state-key pairing of the 2126 opening kept the Sixteen States of Seoul as canon. Even when a state was annexed, the key remained.

The northern refugee key north-refuge folded its slot row for want of a capital. It only thickened the hidden cells of lodging, the Changdong wheel remnants, and the register chests; it became no seventeenth state. The matrix cells read as lineage × living culture. Cell values were four: public, minority, hidden, heresy-dispute.

The pulpit, altar, and monastery lineages belong to the main lineages of the sixteen states. Rites on notice boards are public, while rites kept only by guilds remain a minority practice. Rites in switchgear rooms, dormitories, and behind picture frames are hidden. A heresy dispute opens when doctrine splits within a lineage and awaits judgment. The mobilization-register lineage at the Gwanghwamun archives is in that state.
The culture kit bundled temperament, tradition, and service custom. Service custom was what the organizations keeping a facility held sacred.
Water ledgers, parts standards, the Yeouido schedule
Sluice guards, engineers, barrier-gate combat teams, fire brigades
Record accreditation, transshipment, tablets and altars, strike rolls
Archive defense, line blockade, pump defense
Water escort, transfer neutrality, medicine contracts
Waterworks escort, medical convoy, ridge defense
Cooling keys, pump registers, depots, ice credit
Warehouse guards, convoy bidding, barrier-gate leasing

Within one key, each station split again. The ration queues of Yeongdeungpo and the night shifts of Guro differed in collars, curses, and the order of rites. The Yeouido schedule was not the prayer of western water but of the investment ledgers. No unified culture was assumed.

The houses that kept generational names were those with ledgers — the Records Bureau, the sluice houses, the merchant houses. The rules were in clan seats and generational names. Drifters and dormitory labor hardly kept them.

The migrant corridors were no seventeenth state. They lay over the living spheres as in Diaspora Corridors. When the habit of refusing contracts without interpretation hardened into temperament, that alley's culture kit counted apart from the homeland key. Names were not changed. Corridor cells added no row to the matrix; they thickened the hidden cells of the spheres they lay upon.

Dynastic succession, vassal oaths, and disputes over titles involved Ambitions. Faith determined whose signatures and approvals counted in marriage, adoption, ritual participation, and treaty ratification.
Doctrine shaped succession, marriage, rationing, and treaty ratification.
Bloodline only, adoption allowed, priests only, technical examination only. Theocracies put laying-on-of-hands, General Assembly accreditation, and altar accreditation in front
Other lineages banned, same line only, corridor dual names allowed
Which announcement, seal, tap, or ad frame is cited
A heretic cannot be stationmaster. A hidden priest only deputizes. Theocratic tier 1 is a layer of the land
Rite-participating households first, or public auction only
Which of water, power, safety, legitimacy, technology, medicine, trade is locked or opened. The formula is written by Powers and Diplomacy
Which is mandatory — the Gwanghwamun seal, Yeouido schedule cross-verification, or City Hall contract mediation
Public turned hidden, minority turned heresy
A state without water cannot fulfill a water-supply promise when it claims the high priesthood of the Water-Compact Rite. Its local legitimacy declines.

When a successor changed, personal and institutional promises were separated. If an institutional promise carried doctrinal accreditation, the new successor had to hold that rite again. Without it, the vassals withheld their oaths.

A faction was a new faith slot under the same lineage. When two or more doctrines clashed, a priest named it, and the chapel split in two, a slot was born. At the opening, hidden-faith occupancy was a minority of the sphere's population. When forced rites ran two seasons, hidden occupancy grew.

At a station where sluice-lineage doctrine was strong, holding out an electricity ground alone won low approval. In a sphere where the distribution-and-consumption lineage was public, holding out a plaque alone without ringing the auction bell closed no trade.

When a lesser state became a great power, faith did not necessarily follow. Even if the Seocho Computing Group gripped the Changdong unclaimed zone's barrier gates tighter, the Wheel-Mobility Rite remained. Conversely, if the Water Compact lost its water, the Water-Compact Rite rose into heresy trial first. The Gangbuk treatment center lay outside the city in Namyangju, so northern bulk treatment did not exist at the opening. Northern water self-sufficiency was not a fact of the time but the story's counter-assumption.

The public faith of the time followed the sphere's trades. A great power monopolized no lineage. The capitals were subway stations. The titles were in Offices and Ranks; those seated were in the Characters.
Hidden: the Muster-Remnant Rite. Daerim's Dual-Price Rite
The Silent Faction. Sangam is no capital
Government of the Republic of Korea
Trains pushed beyond Suseo read as apostasy. Suseo is unclaimed
The Bukhansan register chests are ledgers over a vacancy
Itaewon's multilingual passage permits = hidden teaching
Dongdaemun night labor = the western Hu
Sluices and ridge never gather in one hand
Changdong unclaimed zone's Terminal Rest and barrier-gate leasing
The House-Secret Rite. Im Chowon's half transmission
The Capacitor-Relic Faction is a verification subject
Doctrine dies together with the power
B. Main lineages at the opening
At the opening, each state's main lineage had the most followers there. A doctrinal split left its state name and territory in place.
The relative paths of the documents read.
Conscription Remnants and the Military Registers
The heir, name-roster, and world ledger
The arms and technology of this era
