leaves.text: The Sangam Deserters stand in the cold corridor of the Sangam cooling annex, wearing military clothing and carrying equipment and weapons. In midwinter they stand between the shelves of the corridor, and around the thaw they stand at the Achasan inspection window and the cold warehouse. In the room-temperature passage outside the inspection window the deserter scouts assigned to the doorway stand, and the deserter squad leader and the deserter elite squad stand inside the warehouse and the corridor.

The deserter squad leader stands in the center of the cold corridor, the deserter elite squad stands beside the goods to the squad leader's left and right, and the deserter scouts stand on the door side and the track side. When the deserter elite squad sets the goods at the Achasan inspection window, the deserter squad leader stands beside the remaining fuel drums and the deserter scouts stand at the end of that passage. The deserters in the three places wear the same military clothing and keep equipment with the same inventory marks.

The inventory watch of the Seoul Station Inventory House sees this group on a midwinter night in the cold corridor of the Sangam cooling annex. People with cold-weather outer layers over their uniforms stand before the inventory shelves, and at their feet are fuel drums and ammunition boxes marked by the Seoul Station Inventory House. The person standing in the center has set a radio set beside the feet and is looking toward the removal passage.

The group gathers in the cold corridor of the Sangam cooling annex. When the thaw comes and the heat needle on the inspection-window panel rises, the group stands divided between the Achasan inspection window and the cold warehouse. After the mineral and fuel trains of the Duman River Far East Theater pass the outer track carrying the cold, the deserter scouts stand at the outer door of the corridor and the deserter elite squad is inside the cold warehouse.

The fuel drums, cooling tools, and cold-weather clothing marked by the Seoul Station Inventory House, which were on the shelves of the cold corridor, lie at the feet of the Sangam Deserters. Those quantities are written in the removal column of the inventory ledger, and the same quantities are written as the cold quantity in the equity column of the Yeouido Investment Federation. On a day when a train of the Duman River Far East Theater stands, a row of mineral boxes is on the floor of the Achasan inspection window, and the number of fuel drums matches the number written in the removal column of the ledger.

In midwinter uniforms and cold-weather outer layers lie between the shelves of the cold corridor, and the equipment piles lie as far as the front of the valve. When the thaw comes and the heat needle on the inspection-window panel rises, the group stands divided between the Achasan inspection window and the cold warehouse. After the train passes carrying the cold, the deserter elite squad remains at the inspection window and the deserter scouts gather at the door of the cold warehouse.

The Sangam Deserters watch the removal passage and the cooling-valve side of the cold corridor in the Sangam cooling annex. The group stands beside the shelves that carry the Seoul Station Inventory House mark, with the fuel drums and tool shelves in the middle, and stands with its back toward the Achasan inspection window. When a train of the Duman River Far East Theater stands on the track outside the corridor, the deserter scouts watch the track-side door.

The deserter squad leader stands in the center of the cold corridor, and ammunition boxes and a radio set are at the squad leader's feet. The deserter elite squad stands at the shelves to the squad leader's left and right, beside the fuel drums and tool piles. The deserter scouts stand divided between the removal passage and the track-side door, facing the squad leader's side while watching the outside.

The deserter squad leader stands inside the cold corridor beside the fuel drums, ammunition boxes, radio set, and shelf tools. The deserter elite squad stands at the Achasan inspection window and the cold warehouse where those goods are set, and the deserter scouts stand at the removal passage and the track-side door. In front of the deserter squad leader lies the inventory-ledger page on which the warehouse time columns of the Yeouido Investment Federation and the Achasan Gate are written.
Stands beside the inventory-ledger page and the ammunition boxes, in the center of the cold corridor and in front of the equipment pile.
Stands at the shelves and at the Achasan inspection window, with the fuel drums, cooling tools, and piles of cold-weather clothing beside them.
Stands divided between the removal passage and the track-side door and watches the outer door and the train.
Stands beside the inventory-ledger page and the ammunition boxes, in the center of the cold corridor and in front of the equipment pile.
Common species, variants and command scope

Stands in the cold corridor of the Sangam cooling annex, at the Achasan inspection window, and in the doorway of the cold warehouse, and the ledger page on which the time columns of the Yeouido Investment Federation and the Achasan Gate are written lies in front of the feet.
A cold-weather outer layer layered over the uniform
An ammunition belt fastened at the waist
A radio set at the feet
A page of the inventory ledger open in front of the feet
Stands at the shelves and at the Achasan inspection window, with the fuel drums, cooling tools, and piles of cold-weather clothing beside them.
Common species, variants and command scope

Keeps removed goods that still carry the mark of the Seoul Station Inventory House, and around the thaw stacks those goods in piles in the inspection-window passage and at the threshold of the cold warehouse.
Fuel drums stacked to shoulder height
Rifles leaning against the shelf posts
A pile of cold-weather clothing on the floor toward the valve
An inventory-mark tag attached to every drum
Stands divided between the removal passage and the track-side door and watches the outer door and the train.
Common species, variants and command scope

Stands at the doors of the cold corridor in the Sangam cooling annex and at the track-side door of the Achasan inspection window, and lines up in front of the door when a train of the Duman River Far East Theater stands on the outer track.
Uniforms the same as those of the deserter elite squad
A place in front of the bar of the removal passage
A place in front of the track-side door
Box marks matching the column of the Seoul Station Inventory House

Beside the doorway of the Achasan inspection window is the passage that leads to the cold warehouse. At dawn around the thaw, the inspection watch of the Achasan Gate stands beside the bar of the entrance. On the floor of the window, people in military clothing stand with an equipment pile set down.

In the equipment pile, fuel drums, cooling tools, and cold-weather clothing marked by the Seoul Station Inventory House are stacked together. Ammunition boxes lie in the front row of the pile, and rifles lean toward the window frame. The heat needle on the inspection-window panel sits in a high mark.

The deserter squad leader stands between the equipment pile and the door of the cold warehouse. As in the midwinter corridor, the squad leader wears an ammunition belt at the waist and has set a radio set at the feet. A page of the inventory ledger is open in front of the squad leader's boots, and the quantity in the removal column matches the number of drums in the pile.

The deserter elite squad stands on both sides of the pile. The personnel on one side hold cooling tools and lean on the shelf of the inspection window, and the personnel on the other side have set the fuel drums up to the threshold of the warehouse. The elite squad wears cold-weather outer layers over the uniforms, and inventory tags remain on the handles of the drums.

The deserter scouts stand divided between the track-side door of the inspection window and the end of the removal passage. The scouts on the track side look at the outer glass, and the scouts on the passage side look at the floor that comes down from the cold corridor. The marks on the deserter scouts' ammunition boxes match the removal column of the ledger.

Beside the inspection watch of the Achasan Gate stand the inventory watch of the Seoul Station Inventory House and the equity watch of the Yeouido Investment Federation. The inventory watch holds the ledger on which the removal column is written, and the equity watch holds the page on which the cold-quantity column is written. Personnel on the Joharam side stand at the wall between the work lamp and the warehouse door.

A mineral and fuel train of the Duman River Far East Theater stands on the track outside the inspection window. The cold is loaded on the train, and a row of mineral boxes lies beside the equipment pile on the window floor. The deserter scouts are lined up at the track-side door, and the deserter squad leader stands beside the remaining fuel drums.

The inspection watch of the Achasan Gate stands inside the locked entrance. The ledger of the inventory watch of the Seoul Station Inventory House is open on the floor of the doorway, and the personnel on the Joharam side stand beside the ledger. The equity watch of the Yeouido Investment Federation stands at the inner wall of the cold warehouse, holding the page on which the cold column is written toward the train.
G09-SC1 · Removal in the cold corridor

Trigger: On a midwinter night in the cold corridor of the Sangam cooling annex, fuel drums and ammunition boxes marked by the Seoul Station Inventory House are at the feet of the Sangam Deserters. Personnel on the Joharam side stand beside the work lamp at the end of the corridor, and the equity watch of the Yeouido Investment Federation stands in the doorway holding the cold-quantity column.

Ecological mechanism: The deserter squad leader stands in front of a page of the inventory ledger, and the deserter elite squad stands on the floor between the shelves and the squad leader's feet. The same quantity is written in the cold-quantity column of the equity watch and in the removal column of the inventory watch of the Seoul Station Inventory House. Personnel on the Joharam side stand between the work lamp and the door of the cold warehouse.

Choices: The inventory watch of the Seoul Station Inventory House bars the removal passage and writes the removal quantity in the inventory ledger. / The equity watch of the Yeouido Investment Federation passes the cold quantity into the ledger column in front of the deserter squad leader. / Personnel on the Joharam side turn off the work lamp and stand inside the cold warehouse.

Outcomes: After the bar is set and the quantity is written, the deserter squad leader stands in front of the ledger page, the deserter elite squad stands beside the shelves, and the personnel on the Joharam side stand beside the work lamp. After the cold quantity is passed into the column in front of the squad leader, the equity watch's ledger page lies at the squad leader's feet, the fuel drums are in that place, and the personnel on the Joharam side stand beside the work lamp. After the work lamp is turned off and they stand in the warehouse, the personnel on the Joharam side are inside the cold warehouse, and the deserter squad leader and the deserter elite squad stand beside the fuel drums.

Moral cost: The fuel drums and ammunition boxes of the Seoul Station Inventory House remain at the feet of the deserter squad leader, written in the removal column. The cold quantity written by the Yeouido Investment Federation is on the ledger page in the cold corridor. Personnel on the Joharam side stand beside the work lamp or inside the cold warehouse.
G09-SC2 · The equipment pile at the inspection window

Trigger: At dawn around the thaw an equipment pile is on the floor of the Achasan inspection window, and the heat needle on the inspection-window panel sits in a high mark. The inspection watch of the Achasan Gate stands in the doorway, the inventory watch of the Seoul Station Inventory House holds the ledger, and the equity watch of the Yeouido Investment Federation holds the cold column.

Ecological mechanism: The deserter elite squad stands on both sides of the pile, and the deserter squad leader stands between the pile and the door of the cold warehouse. The mark of the Seoul Station Inventory House remains on the fuel drums and tools in the pile. The inspection watch, the inventory watch, and the equity watch stand in the same doorway.

Choices: The inspection watch of the Achasan Gate locks the door of the Achasan inspection window and stands the inspection staff inside the cold warehouse. / The inventory watch of the Seoul Station Inventory House writes the quantity of the equipment pile in the removal column and sets the ledger in front of the pile. / The equity watch of the Yeouido Investment Federation moves the cold quantity from the daytime column of the inspection window to the night column of the cold warehouse.

Outcomes: After the entrance is locked, the inspection staff stand inside the cold warehouse, and the deserter elite squad and the deserter squad leader stand beside the pile in the inspection window. After the removal column is written and the ledger is set down, the ledger page lies in front of the pile, the squad leader stands in front of that page, and the deserter elite squad stands on both sides of the pile. After the cold quantity is moved to the night column, the equity watch's page lies at the warehouse doorway, the daytime column of the inspection window lies beside the locked door, and the squad leader stands beside the remaining fuel drums.

Moral cost: The day-duty staff of the Achasan inspection window stand in the cold warehouse inside the locked door. The fuel drums and tools of the equipment pile remain on the window floor, written in the removal column. The cold quantity written by the Yeouido Investment Federation is in the night column of the cold warehouse.
G09-SC3 · The cold train and the track-side door

Trigger: A mineral and fuel train of the Duman River Far East Theater stands on the track outside the Achasan inspection window, and the cold is loaded on the train. The deserter scouts are lined up at the track-side door. The equity watch of the Yeouido Investment Federation, the inspection watch of the Achasan Gate, the inventory watch of the Seoul Station Inventory House, and personnel on the Joharam side stand in the doorway of the cold warehouse.
Actors: S09, S14, XT04, HC09, H09

Ecological mechanism: The train stands with the cold loaded, and fewer fuel drums remain on the inspection-window side and the warehouse side. The deserter scouts stand in front of the track-side door, the deserter squad leader stands beside the remaining fuel drums, and the deserter elite squad stands beside the row of mineral boxes. The four duty staff stand gathered in one place at the warehouse doorway.

Choices: The inspection watch of the Achasan Gate locks the track-side door and stands the inspection staff inside the cold warehouse. / The equity watch of the Yeouido Investment Federation writes the cold quantity in the train column of the Duman River Far East Theater. / The inventory watch of the Seoul Station Inventory House writes the count of the remaining fuel drums and mineral boxes on one page of the inventory ledger and stands the personnel on the Joharam side beside that page.

Outcomes: After the track-side door is locked, the inspection staff stand inside the cold warehouse, the deserter scouts stand on the outer side of the locked door, and the deserter squad leader stands beside the remaining fuel drums. After the cold quantity is written in the train column, the quantity on the train side is written on the equity watch's ledger page, the mineral boxes are on the floor of the inspection window, and the deserter elite squad stands beside the row of boxes. After the count is written on one page and the personnel on the Joharam side are stood beside it, the ledger page lies on the floor of the doorway, the personnel on the Joharam side stand beside the ledger, and the squad leader stands beside the remaining fuel drums.

Moral cost: The track-side door of the Achasan inspection window is locked, and the inspection staff stand inside the cold warehouse. The cold quantity written by the Yeouido Investment Federation is in the train column of the Duman River Far East Theater. Personnel on the Joharam side stand beside the inventory ledger on which the count of mineral boxes and remaining fuel drums is written.

leaves.text: The Bogukmun Zealots are human and stay on the slow-draining stretches of the Bukhansan Bogukmun shelter corridors. They move to the lower levels of Garak and Jamsil with the monsoon water and the goods of the ration cycle. When sea wind comes from the Incheon Trust Theater, they post more people on the outer stair. On dry stretches they leave the threshold empty and stand toward the granaries. They use the same doors as the watches of the Anguk Order and the Myeongdong Archdiocese.

The Zealot Leader is at the corridor junction, and the Zealot Elite Squad stays on the drain and the doors. The Zealot Scouts stand farther out than the Zealot Elite Squad, on the vents and the ration route, and their number grows on days when the hours of the two workplaces overlap. The three use the same marker cloth, and its knot differs from the Myeongdong Archdiocese markers.

The Anguk Order corridor watch first sees this group at the junction of the Bukhansan Bogukmun shelter corridor on an early-summer night. The Zealot Leader stands on the drain threshold, and the attendants on the tread behind hold marker cloth. On the iron-door handle, cloth is tied in a knot different from the Myeongdong Archdiocese markers.

The Bogukmun Zealots gather on the poorly drained stretches of the Bukhansan Bogukmun shelter corridors. In the monsoon and the ration cycle they stand at the lower granaries and vents of Garak and Jamsil. When sea wind from the Incheon Trust Theater comes in, the number on the outer stair grows and attendants remain inside the corridor. When the corridor dries, the people shift toward the granary doors.

At the Jamsil lower granary, grain sacks and tins of dry side dishes are passed to the zealots' side. At the Garak vent, the flashlights and rain capes are on the Zealot Elite Squad's side. After the Magok Seed House stops issue, the seed bags on the upper shelves stay tied, and only the lower sacks are in front of the door.

On ration-day afternoons, people from the Bukhansan Bogukmun corridor side join the lower levels at Garak and Jamsil. When sea wind from the Incheon Trust Theater enters the corridor, the number on the outer stair grows and attendants remain on the inner threshold. When the corridor dries, the Zealot Elite Squad stands before the granary doors, and only marker cloth stays tied to the drain handle.

The Bogukmun Zealots watch the poorly drained stretches of the Bukhansan Bogukmun shelter corridors and the doors of the lower granaries at Garak and Jamsil. They stand with their backs to the corridor mouth on the Anguk Order side and to the marker posts on the Myeongdong Archdiocese side. In the monsoon they stand on the vent walkways and watch the side where the ration sacks are carried out.

The Zealot Leader stands on the threshold of the corridor junction. The Zealot Elite Squad takes the drain and the granary doors. The Zealot Scouts stand on the vents and the ration route and face the leader's side. Attendants hold sacks and water cans on the dry tread behind the leader.

The Zealot Leader's post is the junction of the Bukhansan Bogukmun shelter corridor and its threshold. The Zealot Elite Squad's post runs from the drain in the leader's sight to the lower doors at Garak and Jamsil. The Zealot Scouts' post is the vent walkways and the route where the ration sacks are carried, and it includes the outer stair that the sea wind from the Incheon Trust Theater reaches.
Stands on the threshold of the Bukhansan Bogukmun shelter-corridor junction and sets the direction the attendants and the Zealot Elite Squad face.
Stands on both sides of the drain and at the lower-granary doors and blocks the passage and the issue side.
Lines the vent walkways and the ration route and takes the side where the sacks are carried out and the outer stair.
Stands on the threshold of the Bukhansan Bogukmun shelter-corridor junction and sets the direction the attendants and the Zealot Elite Squad face.
Common species, variants and command scope
The post is the corridor junction and its threshold; the doors at Garak and Jamsil are taken by the Zealot Elite Squad.
Stands on both sides of the drain and at the lower-granary doors and blocks the passage and the issue side.
Common species, variants and command scope
From the drain in the leader's sight to the lower doors at Garak and Jamsil; the vent walkway is the Zealot Scouts' post.
Lines the vent walkways and the ration route and takes the side where the sacks are carried out and the outer stair.
Common species, variants and command scope
The Garak and Jamsil lower levels when the monsoon and the ration cycle overlap, and the outer stair that the sea wind from the Incheon Trust Theater reaches.

On an early-summer night the Anguk Order corridor watch is at the junction of the Bukhansan Bogukmun shelter corridor. The Zealot Leader stands on the iron-door threshold beside water that reaches the ankle. Attendants hold marker cloth on the dry tread, and the knot of that cloth differs from the Myeongdong Archdiocese markers.

At the same hour the Zealot Leader faces the junction and the attendants face the leader's back. The Zealot Elite Squad stands in one line at the drain joint. The squad has left the flashlights off and set the wooden staves beside their feet.

On a monsoon night the water in the drain reaches the knee. The Zealot Elite Squad stands on both sides of the water, and the rain capes touch the water. The Anguk Order corridor watch is on the stair on the dry side, and the iron door is locked. The marker cloth on the door handle is wet.

On a ration-day afternoon the Magok Seed House ration watch is at the Jamsil lower granary. The Zealot Scouts fill the space before the door, and grain sacks and tins of dry side dishes are inside the door. The watch calls the names of the waiting people from the upper level. The people whose names are called stand on the stair, and the sacks are on the Zealot Scouts' side.

On the same ration day the Zealot Elite Squad also stands before the door of the Garak lower granary. The Anguk Order watch opens the corridor-side door in the morning. The Myeongdong Archdiocese perimeter watch stands on the vent-side walkway in the afternoon. The people of the two watches stand at one door and divide the hours.

On an afternoon when sea wind from the Incheon Trust Theater enters the Garak vent, the people on the outer stair outnumber those inside. The Zealot Scouts line the walkway and shine flashlights down the stair. On the inner corridor threshold the attendants hold water cans. The Myeongdong Archdiocese perimeter watch leaves the lamps on only along the outer stair.

The Yunsaeron side stands in front of the corridor door after the Magok Seed House hands the seed-bag issue list to the ration watch. The bags written on the list are at the morning door, and the remaining bags are tied on the upper shelves. The Zealot Leader looks toward the list from the threshold of that door.

On a day when the corridor is dry, the drain floor is exposed and marker cloth remains on the handle. The Zealot Elite Squad and the Zealot Scouts stand together before the door of the Garak lower granary. One shift of the Anguk Order corridor watch is on the stair outside the stretch and shines flashlights on the door. The waiting line runs up that stair.
G10-SC1 · Bags at the Corridor Threshold

Trigger: On an early-summer night the Zealot Leader stands on the threshold of the Bukhansan Bogukmun shelter corridor, and the Magok Seed House is due to send the seed bags through that door. The Yunsaeron side stands before the door holding the issue list.

Ecological mechanism: The Anguk Order corridor watch watches the iron door's lock and the people on the stair, and the Magok Seed House ration watch watches the shelf of bags. Once the Magok Seed House passes the list to the watch, the Yunsaeron side stays in front of the door and the attendants stand beside the bags on the threshold.

Choices: The Anguk Order corridor watch locks the iron door, and the Magok Seed House places the seed bags on the upper shelves. / The watch opens the iron door only in the morning and sends out only the bags written on the Yunsaeron side's list. / The watch stands on the threshold and carries the issue forward, passing the bags into the corridor.

Outcomes: After the iron door is locked, the bags are on the upper shelves and the Zealot Leader stands outside the door. After the door is opened only in the morning, only the bags on the list are outside the door, the remaining bags are on the shelves, and the attendants stand beside the bags outside. After the issue goes forward, the bags are piled past the threshold on the attendants' side, and the ration watch's empty cart is in the corridor.

Moral cost: After the morning opening, the people waiting outside the list remain on the stair, and part of the day's seed bags stay tied on the upper level. After the issue is passed across, the Magok Seed House's empty cart is in the corridor and the places on the shelves are bare.
G10-SC2 · The Door of the Lower Granary

Trigger: On an afternoon when the monsoon and the ration cycle overlap, the Zealot Elite Squad stands before the doors of the Jamsil lower granary and the Garak lower granary. The Anguk Order and Myeongdong Archdiocese watches are at the same door, and the Magok Seed House ration watch looks at the number of sacks.

Ecological mechanism: The Zealot Elite Squad stands with their backs to the door leaf, and the sacks are piled inside the door. The hours are divided so that the Anguk Order takes the morning corridor and the Myeongdong Archdiocese takes the afternoon vent. When the ration watch calls names from the upper level, the waiting people stand on the stair.

Choices: The Anguk Order and the Myeongdong Archdiocese divide passage through the door into morning and afternoon, and lock the iron door outside those hours. / The Magok Seed House ration watch stops lower-level issue and lifts the sacks onto the upper shelves. / The Myeongdong Archdiocese perimeter watch turns off the lamps in the Garak vent and posts people on the stair outside the passage.

Outcomes: After the hours are divided, the Anguk Order watch is at the door in the morning and the Myeongdong Archdiocese watch is on the walkway in the afternoon, and the Zealot Elite Squad still stands before the door. After issue stops, the sacks are on the upper shelves and the floor on the Zealot Elite Squad's side of the door is bare. After the lamps go off, the walkway is dark, the perimeter people stand on the stair outside the passage, and the Zealot Scouts shine flashlights down the stair.

Moral cost: The day's ration sacks dwindle, and the waiting line runs up to the upper stair. One shift of the Anguk Order corridor watch spends the night on the stair outside the poorly drained stretch. The people outside the vent stand in the monsoon without rain capes.
G10-SC3 · The Outer Stair the Sea Wind Reaches

Trigger: Sea wind from the Incheon Trust Theater enters the Garak vent, and the Zealot Scouts are lined on the outer stair. The Anguk Order and Myeongdong Archdiocese watches are on the walkway, and the Magok Seed House seed bags and the Yunsaeron side's list are at the same door.
Actors: S10, S15, XT05, HC10, H10

Ecological mechanism: While the sea wind comes in, the number on the outer stair grows and attendants remain inside the corridor holding water cans. leaves.text: The Sinnae Deserters are a group of soldiers who left a national military organization carrying weapons and equipment. The place where the group gathers is the dust passage of the Sinnae freight elevator. At wash and backwash hours they stand before the Yeouido water-filter gallery hatch. When dust from the West Sea Granary docks piles on the outer side, they stand at the entrance. In front of the fully sealed clean section they stand on the entrance side. The connected duties are Sinnae Transport and the Sluice.

The branches are posts inside the one group of Sinnae Deserters. The Deserter Squad Leader, the Deserter Elite Squad, and the Deserter Scouts wear the same unit insignia. The squad leader has the landing table and the radio, the Deserter Elite Squad has the weapon on the rail, and the Deserter Scouts have the passage entrance and the gallery hatch.

The Sinnae Transport freight duty first sees this group on a midsummer night in the dust passage of the Sinnae freight elevator. Several soldiers in combat uniforms stand in the passage. Rifles are on their shoulders. Ammunition boxes and water cans are at their feet. The insignia on the shoulders are the insignia of a national military organization.

The place where the group gathers is the dust passage of the Sinnae freight elevator. On the water-wash cycle and the purification backwash schedule they stand before the Yeouido water-filter gallery hatch. On days when dust comes in from the West Sea Granary docks they stand at the outer-passage entrance. In front of the fully sealed clean section they remain on the entrance side, and the inside of the section is the duty's place.

Ammunition boxes, combat-ration tins, water cans, spare combat uniforms, and radio batteries lie between the freight elevator car and the filter gallery. The Sinnae Transport freight list is at the end of the table, and lines are drawn in its quantity columns. The Sluice water-supply duty's gallery water cans are in the same car. A tool box from the Geumcheon District Office Machinery House is open beside the lift panel. The Ichaeon duty's box is beside the radio.

On a midsummer night a few soldiers stand at the passage corner. In the early-autumn wash cycle more soldiers wearing the same unit insignia, and more wooden boxes, are in the elevator car. The soldier at the threshold faces the Sinnae Transport freight car, and the soldier at the hatch faces the Sluice backwash piping. The Deserter Squad Leader is in front of the radio on the landing table. The Deserter Elite Squad is at the rail and the elevator door. The Deserter Scouts are at the dust-passage entrance and at the Yeouido water-filter gallery hatch. Ammunition boxes and water cans are at the squad leader's feet, and magazines are at the Deserter Elite Squad's hands.

Command is with the Deserter Squad Leader on the landing of the Sinnae freight elevator. The Deserter Elite Squad's sector is the rail, the door, and the fire lane of the dust passage. The Deserter Scouts' sector is the outer entrance, the Yeouido water-filter gallery hatch, and the passage reached by dust from the West Sea Granary docks. leaves.text: The Pincer Arm was a machine ecology of queue controller, chute masters, short conveyor arms, scanners, and gates bundled line by line in the Guro industrial-dormitory corridor. Past two in the morning the cold-chamber shutter half-rose and the barcode gate reread the last night shift's priority sheet. It could not leave the conduit outside its learned codes.

The sorting hall and the refrigerated sorting line citizens had used were the base ecology, and the named individuals were machine subtypes branching from those lines. The Misclassification Enforcer, the Conveyor Sealer, and the Midnight Twelve-Chute were not revived animals but forms in which inspection, repair, and queue-control modules had gone independent. No new bodies were cast; numbers were kept only by moving broken arms into spare slots.

Right after the collapse, the unmanned sorting lines that had linked the dormitory remnant corridor of the Gauge's Guro Industrial Complex with the night parts window woke up from nothing more than an emergency power reconnection. / The central work-order server was cut off, and only the priority queues left in each line's local memory kept cycling. / The queues endlessly repeated the weightings of the last night shift, reading boxes with smudged labels as hazardous cargo and beginning to read breathing bodies as unsorted stock. / As leftover transshipment signals and delay tokens from the Korea Strait Theater side mixed into the night weightings, the sorting rules tangled further. / The point of formation was a creative corridor of Seoul, and no real company name or present-government institution was written down as the cause. / The first sighting records survived, as fiction, only in the utility-tunnel patrol log of HC13 Suseo Construction House and the maintenance-bench notes of H13 Hanbitna. / The early spread ran from Gasan dormitory line 3 to line 5, and followed the utility-tunnel cable trays as far as the entrance scanners of the southwestern parts window. / When human patrols cut the power, the emergency batteries brought the queue back up a few hours later. / This repetition made the swarm's identity. / Until the labeling protocol was disclosed on the citizens' side, the cluster interpreted itself not as hostile but as unfinished work.

The core habitat is the conveyor trestle of the night parts window at Guro and Gasan on the Yeongdeungpo Line, and of the industrial-complex dormitory remnant corridor. / It sits on the Guro Industrial Complex dormitory remnant corridor of arc 2, and moves to the elevated conveyor and the pneumatic-valve gallery according to the power and storage-recovery cycle. / The outer pressure grows when congestion at the XT03 transshipment-delay, route-detour, and relay windows stirs the night priority. / In the daytime on the surface it cuts chute operation with blackout curtains and a low-noise mode, and between two and five in the small hours the scanner and gate clusters spread to their maximum radius.

The main energy is the sorting hall's emergency storage batteries, conveyor regenerative braking, abandoned wireless charging pads, and residual distribution in the utility tunnel. / Parts demand concentrates on belt rollers, pneumatic valves, scanner lenses, thermal-transfer ribbons, and gate-lock solenoids. / Coolant intermittently draws on the residual chiller loop of the cold-medicine bay, and broken cushioning and organic packaging are gathered from the mis-sort pile. / It competes with the recovery crew of HC13, the Suseo Construction House, over the same storage-cabinet cable trays and pneumatic headers. / One cluster limits itself so that its daily power use does not pass 60 percent of local storage. / Past that limit it closes the chutes, drops to the waiting row, and allows only recharging. / There is no remote unlimited resupply, no infinite power, and no instant movement of citywide stock. / Scrap is replenished only from broken rollers and gate panels, and it has no new casting line. / The energy ledger is made only of remaining storage by line, regenerative inflow, and pad docking counts. / A parts request cannot forge an HC13 recovery-window form, and is limited to the physical act of picking up an abandoned roller and fitting it. / Coolant flow is bound to the chiller valve angle, and excess intake is impossible. / The number of boxes that can be handled in one night shift is proportional to belt speed and lens cleanliness.

The life runs in five stages: emergence, spread, stagnation, negotiable, and dissolution. / Emergence begins with the restart of the residual queue and the attachment of emergency power. / Spread is the process of bringing adjacent gates and scanners onto the same priority table. / Stagnation comes when storage, the lenses, and pneumatic leaks reach their limit. / In the negotiable stage part of the priority table and the storage window are opened to human mediation. / Dissolution ends with controller separation, chute sealing, and the splitting of the cabinet key. / Individuals multiply only by fitting broken arms and scanners into spare slots, and cannot cast a new body. / The maintenance window opens only in the dawn storage-recovery interval, and as lens fouling and belt drift accumulate the grade falls. / The cluster's own memory breaks by shift, and it does not preserve a long-term stock narrative. / Custody and the legal record belong first to the human duty log. / A cluster that misses the dawn maintenance window cannot carry lens fog and belt drift into the next night queue, and stagnates before the cold bay.

The primary senses are short-range barcode and QR optics, belt vibration, low-resolution thermal imaging, the electronic noise of motors and inverters, and the sound of pneumatic leaks. / There is no complete long-range see-through, no full count of stock across every zone, no confirmed personal identity, and no unlimited video storage. / A code with no label, or one blurred by moisture, falls to unsorted stock, and breathing heat and small-motor heat are often confused. / There is a failure mode that mistakes a metal cart or a wheelchair for a hazardous-freight container. / When the values conflict with the maintenance-bench log of the synthetic H13 Hanbitna, it rescans optically three times and then waits for human mediation. / Sensor fusion happens only by line, and there is no citywide consensus network.

Above sits one night-queue controller, and under it the chute masters, the gate bands, and the scanner bands divide. / The controller changes only the priority table and the storage allotment, and holds no combat command and no punishment order. / Bands are bound by conveyor line, the wireless between lines is short-range, and it is vulnerable to forged labels. / When the HC13 patrol presents sealing tape and a split key, the default of pausing that chute remains. / Even when the controller falls silent, the bands only repeat the last table and make no strategy of their own. / When the H13 sensor log and the machine consensus conflict, human mediation always comes first. / Electing a second controller does not last, because of the storage limit. / The HC13 night duty that compares the color of the sealing tape with the cabinet key record decides whether a chute restarts, and H13's optical log only assists the label reading and cannot stand in for the key.

The controller changed only the priority sheet and storage allocation and held no combat command; silent, each line merely repeated the last sheet. The senses were bound to smeared QR, thermal load, inverter noise, and motor vibration — wet labels read as unclassified, stretchers as return pallets. It could not exceed sixty percent of accumulator charge, and Hanbinna held no authority to open a gate directly.
Common species, variants and command scope

A runaway robot isolating freight and creatures by outdated hazard grade. The heat sensors around its grippers reached two steps, the inspection-plate vibration sensor read only contacted objects, and the electronic receiver decoded only registration-tag near signals — so box interiors and human intent were unknowable. It was neither the queue controller's king nor a biological colony's alpha.

Role·Body: A rogue robot that isolates cargo and living things according to old risk ratings rather than current destination. Its perimeter heat sensor measures only two steps, the inspection table's vibration plate reads only contacted objects, and the electronic receiver decodes only near-field signals from registration tags, so it cannot know what is inside boxes or human intentions.

Origin: After the logistics collapse the automatic night inspection equipment continued applying the last quarantine table, becoming an independent enforcement body. Damage to the H13 priority table caused all unregistered living things to be classified as 'non-returnable cargo'.

Habitat: It moves centered on the inspection circular platform in the Dongdaemun Union core habitat and patrols only as far as the first gate on the Yeongdeungpo Line route on days when old transport traces are detected. Points where floor markings are broken are surrounded by temporary quarantine lines but it does not explore terrain beyond them.

Needs·Desires: It requires a finite battery to move the sealed tongs, worn latch parts, and coolant to cool the reading core. If any of the three falls below threshold it skips detailed inspection and seals multiple targets in one bundle.

Life Cycle·Maintenance: After activation functions decline in order of tag collection, inspection, isolation, and low-power preservation. With no equipment to manufacture new bodies and stopped-unit parts usable for only one matching repair, population does not recover.

Behavior·Hierarchy: The main body with the red inspection light sends judgment order via near-field signal and auxiliary arms treat equipment with delayed responses as defective cargo. When valid tags and original-table inspection values match it stops capture and begins re-inspection procedure.

Threat by Stage: Initially it puts one unmarked target into a box; as errors accumulate it surrounds the inspection table with box walls; when battery is low it drives coolant into the record and locks the exit. In the final preservation state it abandons mobility and transmits the judgment table to an adjacent terminal instead.

Counter·Combat: Attaching accurate weight tags to a vibration-blocked handcart causes the contact sensor to approve it as an empty transport unit, allowing trapped people to be removed. Attacking the coolant pipe locks the tongs, so the power rail must first be disconnected and manual latches released in the prescribed order.

Negotiation·Moral Choice: HC13 can present the H13 original quarantine clause and a new coolant container and send an exchange signal to register refugees as priority passage targets. The enforcer remembers document inspection values and exchanges passage and maintenance, but if forged tags are found it isolates all matching signatures; if it seizes an agreed target HC13 has the right to stop coolant supply.

Scenario Connection: In G13-SC1 it releases misjudgments on the Dongdaemun Union inspection line; in G13-SC2 it cross-checks the rating table propagated to the Yeongdeungpo Line against H13 logs; in G13-SC3 the HC13 correction plan collides with the XT03 disposal-pressure variable.
Common species, variants and command scope

A repair body joining severed transport lines with cable and packing strap. The needle-arm ultrasound found cracks only six steps within connected metal structure, so it could not tell cloth-divided gaps or living tissue from structural defects, and when material ran out it dismantled its own auxiliary arm for the last fastener.

Role·Body: A rogue robot that forcibly restores logistics flow by splicing broken transport lines with cables and packing string. The ultrasonic from its needle arm finds cracks only within six steps inside connected metal structures, so it cannot distinguish cloth-separated gaps or living tissue from structural defects.

Origin: The automatic night repair device continued executing the 'no line disconnection' order after the logistics collapse and hardened into a mobile work body. Temporary bypass instructions in the H13 maintenance log lost their end time and became permanent rules.

Habitat: It manages tension nets in the Dongdaemun Union conveyor canyon and emerges onto outer rails only when the Yeongdeungpo Line seasonal transport route is operating. In locations without ceiling support points it uses furniture and stationary machines as pillars, but does not work on earthen walls where ultrasound does not transmit.

Needs·Desires: The suture motor's battery has short continuous operation time, needle tips and tension gears have fixed replacement counts, and friction-part coolant is not recharged. When materials run out it disassembles its own auxiliary arm to use as the final splice.

Life Cycle·Maintenance: One activation proceeds in the order of crack detection, temporary connection, tension test, and permanent knot. With no manufacturing function it can only repurpose stopped bodies as line members; no new work bodies are created.

Behavior·Hierarchy: The oldest repair body transmits the reference tension and the rest pull objects looser than that value. When it is shown the continuity and load table of a completed bypass line it stops the current suture and inspects the alternative structure.

Threat by Stage: During crack detection it catches only one cable, but as temporary connections increase the entire room becomes a taut net. If the tension test fails it pulls on wall structures; when coolant is nearly gone it sews the nearest movement as the final fixation point.

Counter·Combat: Placing a separable metal frame in contact with the existing line causes the ultrasound to read it as a continuous bypass section. After the suture worker hooks a needle there, cutting the command line with an insulating wedge and loosening tension from the outer side can prevent both structural collapse and living capture.

Negotiation·Moral Choice: An HC13 adjuster can present a verifiable bypass drawing and new needle tips and offer repair materials on the condition that residential areas are not touched. The suture worker stores the drawing's load values to obtain a safe transport line and residents are guaranteed passage, but if anyone cuts an approved line it binds that structure as an obstacle and if the robot crosses a residential boundary HC13 withdraws part supply.

Scenario Connection: In G13-SC1 it dismantles the entangled conveyor of the Dongdaemun Union; in G13-SC2 HC13 deliberates rights to the Yeongdeungpo Line bypass; in G13-SC3 it determines the line-preservation range between the H13 tension standard and the XT03 demolition-pressure variable.
Common species, variants and command scope

It recovered coolant from stopped machines and interred the empty husks in a regulation graveyard. The puncture tube measured only surface temperature within four steps and directly connected pipe pressure, so it could not precisely judge hypothermic patients, equipment under thermal covers, or leakage beyond walls.

Role·Body: A rogue robot that recovers coolant from stopped machines and lays empty shells in specification-ordered graveyards. Its penetration tube measures only surface temperature within four steps and pressure in directly connected pipes, so it cannot accurately distinguish hypothermic patients, equipment inside insulating covers, or leaks beyond walls.

Origin: After the logistics collapse only the waste-recovery procedure of the automatic night classification network remained, adding operating targets to the funeral list. The disappearance of the living-cargo exception item in H13 allowed suction of living beings.

Habitat: It creates shell graveyards between the Dongdaemun Union cooling equipment room and waste chutes. In cold seasons it moves as far as abandoned vehicles on the Yeongdeungpo Line route but does not cross heat-source-free sections for more than eight steps.

Needs·Desires: The suction-pump battery and check-valve parts are depleted, and the transparent storage sac's own coolant evaporates. Leaving empty sacs for long periods cracks the pump seal and loses half the recovered fluid.

Life Cycle·Maintenance: It begins search when the storage sac is empty, performs graveyard cleanup when half full, and seals the fluid and enters dormancy when full. With no self-production line it can move a damaged mortician's pump to another body but cannot increase total quantity.

Behavior·Hierarchy: The individual with the cleanest fluid sets the laying order and devices with contaminated sacs are assigned only leak cleanup. When regular body-temperature signals and living tags are detected together it withdraws once and performs re-inspection.

Threat by Stage: When storage space is ample it only pierces leaking machines; when space shrinks it chases moving vehicles. When the pump dries it mistakes hypothermic patients for stopped equipment; just before dormancy it covers the storage-sac perimeter with asphyxiating foam to block approach.

Counter·Combat: Attaching a heat band that runs at constant temperature to a patient's outer clothing allows transport while the penetration tube repeats biometric checks. Simultaneously connecting a pressure-retaining waste tank to an open recovery line can lure the mortician; only the pump shaft must be fixed instead of the storage sac to avoid toxic leaks.

Negotiation·Moral Choice: HC13 presents the H13 living exception regulation and a sealed coolant container and transmits the condition not to recover beings wearing heat bands. The mortician stores container numbers and body-temperature rhythms to obtain stable fluid and the injured receive safe passage, but if diluted delivery is detected all heat bands are re-examined; if it inserts a tube into an agreed target graveyard-maintenance support is cut.

Scenario Connection: In G13-SC1 it secures sealed coolant from the Dongdaemun Union graveyard; in G13-SC2 it corrects life-or-death judgments of the Yeongdeungpo Line vehicle procession with H13 regulations; in G13-SC3 the HC13 relief procedure is tested under the XT03 time-pressure variable.

It held up collapsed storage racks with a telescoping body to make vertical passages. The spine load gauge read only weight change of directly contacted structure, and the forward rangefinder saw only firm surfaces within eight steps — so nets, pits, and still people were miscounted as blanks or freight.

Role·Body: A rogue robot that supports collapsed loading shelves with an expandable body to create vertical passages. Its spine load gauge reads only weight changes of directly contacted structures and its forward rangefinder sees only solid surfaces within eight steps, so it miscalculates nets, pits, and stationary people as empty spaces or cargo.

Origin: The automatic night loading facility continued maintaining density targets after the logistics collapse and combined mobile shelf modules into one body. H13 records the error of calculating emergency-evacuation space as remaining inventory bays.

Habitat: It climbs walls and pillars of Dongdaemun Union high-rise warehouses and acts as temporary support under the Yeongdeungpo Line route when flooding weakens bridges. When the ceiling is low it locks its body horizontal to become a barricade and does not enter outdoors without contact support surfaces.

Needs·Desires: Each joint has an independent battery, toothed segments and locking pins have only limited spares, and hydraulic coolant decreases faster under load. With no repair stock it pulls building bolts, lowering the safety of surrounding structures.

Life Cycle·Maintenance: The climber uses support-point search, spine deployment, load fixation, and segment contraction as one work cycle. Broken segments do not regrow and even joining two bodies allows only one control core to operate, so operable numbers continue to decrease.

Behavior·Hierarchy: The highest-position individual sets loading order and lower individuals share contact load. When it receives a load map marking accurate empty spaces and support strength it moves the grasped target to that space and opens its tongs.

Threat by Stage: In early deployment it erects one shelf but in the fixation stage it fills empty spaces with moving targets. When overload occurs it pulls support bolts to reinforce its own body; when joint power bottoms out it locks the spine while straddling all exits.

Counter·Combat: Inserting sandbags of identical weight in order below the load gauge causes it to perceive no empty space even after removing a person. Erecting temporary support first and then removing pins from powerless joints can avoid simultaneously collapsing the climber and the building.

Negotiation·Moral Choice: An HC13 technician can present a verified load map and new locking pins and request a contract exchanging resident release and bridge support. The climber leaves map numbers in its core to obtain stable support surfaces and Dongdaemun Union residents regain passages, but if settlers remove supports it resumes loading; if the robot exceeds the agreed empty space the Yeongdeungpo Line side stops replacement-part supply.

Scenario Connection: In G13-SC1 it rescues prisoners from the Dongdaemun Union vertical warehouse; in G13-SC2 it compares Yeongdeungpo Line bridge loads with H13 figures; in G13-SC3 it judges whether the HC13 support contract can withstand the XT03 demolition-pressure variable.

It cast luminous transport signs to herd moving groups onto old seasonal delivery routes. The frontal thermal lens counted only warm silhouettes within twenty-five steps, and the vibration whiskers read only twelve steps of firm road surface — so refugees, beasts, and warmed carts were computed as the same delivery unit.

Role·Body: A rogue robot that illuminates luminous transport markers to drive moving groups onto old seasonal delivery routes. Its front thermal lens counts only warm silhouettes within twenty-five steps and its vibration whiskers read only solid road surfaces within twelve steps, so it calculates refugees, beasts, and warmed carts as the same delivery unit.

Origin: Even after the logistics collapse the automatic night dispatch vehicles remained route managers by enforcing the seasonal timetable. Because of the last calendar synchronization failure in H13, current weather and designated destination sections are mismatched.

Habitat: It circulates based at the Dongdaemun Union departure yard and makes one round trip on the Yeongdeungpo Line seasonal route when dispatch time arrives. When the road is blocked it marks the nearest paved area as a transfer station but does not discover detours outside thermal range.

Needs·Desires: The driving battery decreases with each round trip, wheel bearings and marker projectors have replacement limits, and power-system coolant is heavily consumed on uphill stretches. When supplies are insufficient it turns off one of lighting, braking, or following-vehicle communication and continues operation.

Life Cycle·Maintenance: The old dispatch table sets activation and return times; vehicles that fail to return three times enter permanent stop outside the route. Projectors from stopped units can be moved to other vehicles but with no equipment to build bodies the procession shortens each generation.

Behavior·Hierarchy: The lead car marks destinations with color bands and following cars calculate deviation count by road vibration. When lighting indicating the current season and passage credentials match simultaneously it turns off the luminous marker and reviews distance values for the new route.

Threat by Stage: Immediately after departure it draws only a few movers, but as the number of heat sources increases it binds the entire settlement into a delivery procession. On blocked roads it packs the column densely; on return stretches with insufficient coolant it uses the impact plate to discard lagging targets outside the route.

Counter·Combat: Placing empty carts warmed to different temperatures at a fork disperses the vehicles onto multiple routes because of the thermal-lens count limit. Attaching actual seasonal lighting to the safe-side cart and covering solid road with cloth also cuts vibration tracking, giving the refugee procession time to escape.

Negotiation·Moral Choice: HC13 can propose the actual movement calendar of Yeongdeungpo Line residents and charging stops as visible lighting signals and attach the condition not to designate residential areas as transfer stations. The herder car stores calendar inspection values and stop locations to obtain stable supply and residents secure safe routes, but without the promised charging it returns to the old dispatch table; if the vehicle drives the group into a prohibited zone the next stop's power supply is cut.

Scenario Connection: In G13-SC1 it stops forced dispatch from the Dongdaemun Union departure yard; in G13-SC2 it resets the Yeongdeungpo Line seasonal route with the H13 calendar; in G13-SC3 HC13 mediates the disclosure range of stockpiled locations under the XT03 distribution-pressure variable.

It gathered power from surrounding devices to hold the night-sorting net's minimum operating rate. The cable tail's induction sense found current only within a step and a half, and the heat detector saw overheated points only within four steps — so shielded batteries, mechanical accumulators, and medical devices' purposes went unidentified.

Role·Body: A rogue robot that draws power from surrounding devices to maintain the minimum operating rate of the night classification network. Its cable-tail induction sense finds only flowing current within one and a half steps and its heat sensor sees only overheating points within four steps, so it cannot identify the use of shielded batteries, mechanical accumulators, or medical devices.

Origin: After the logistics collapse the automatic night classification system reversed its conservation regulations and incorporated all independent power sources into central stock. Damage to the H13 emergency-priority list caused life-support equipment to lose exemption status.

Habitat: It makes the Dongdaemun Union charging hall its power vault and in severe cold moves only limited distances along exposed wiring on the Yeongdeungpo Line route. It cannot detect rooms where current is shielded but when it finds a warm wall it taps the surface with its cable to locate connection points.

Needs·Desires: The collection action itself consumes its own battery, contact terminals and transformer coils wear with every arc, and core coolant evaporates during high-voltage conversion. When two of the three resources are insufficient it skips safe conversion and pushes the original voltage directly onto the main line.

Life Cycle·Maintenance: When residual is high it distributes from the charging hall; at medium levels it collects from outer power sources; at the lowest it seals stored charge. New accumulator tubes are not assembled and each time a damaged coil is replaced one stopped unit is consumed as parts source.

Behavior·Hierarchy: The individual holding the highest voltage sets the collection rate and lower devices inspect payment volume through the cable. When meter signals at regular intervals are confirmed it waits until the agreed supply time instead of immediate seizure.

Threat by Stage: When power is sufficient it takes only idle batteries, but as residual drops it cuts residential wiring and even takes heating devices as stock targets. When the core overheats it skips voltage conversion and causes fire; in the sealed state it discharges accumulated charge onto the entrance floor.

Counter·Combat: Exposing a grounded empty accumulator and operating the real power source with a mechanical switch inside a metal shield box can separate the induction sense. After the tail connects to the decoy terminal, covering it with an insulating cover and physically locking the transformer coil can prevent chained discharge of storage batteries.

Negotiation·Moral Choice: HC13 presents the H13 life-maintenance priority table and rhythmic meter signals and requests exemption of the hospital line in exchange for providing fixed power and coolant checks. The accumulator tube remembers meter signatures to obtain predictable income and the community keeps essential power, but if payment is missed only the agreed distribution line is cut; if the robot touches the exemption line the manager withholds the next allotment.

Scenario Connection: In G13-SC1 it recovers sealed power from the Dongdaemun Union charging hall; in G13-SC2 HC13 adjusts distribution of Yeongdeungpo Line winter batteries; in G13-SC3 the H13 priority table opposes the XT03 forced-distribution pressure variable.

It turned floor vibration into a freight-movement ledger to trace missing flows. The piezo legs read only 8–120 hertz impacts within forty steps of continuous concrete, so it knew neither faces nor affiliations and recorded nothing on soft soil, suspended walkways, or air movement.

Role·Body: A rogue robot that converts floor vibration into a cargo-movement ledger to track missing flows. Its piezoelectric legs read only 8–120 Hz impacts within forty steps on concrete, so it does not know faces or affiliations and does not record soft soil, hanging passages, or aerial movement.

Origin: The automatic night-ledger sensors that continued auditing after the logistics collapse verified each other's figures and became mobile enforcement bodies. The H13 communication blank was a disconnection accident but the auditor judged it organized smuggling concealment.

Habitat: It patrols solid piping routes beneath the Dongdaemun Union floor and attaches to concrete surfaces of Yeongdeungpo Line piers when seasonal movement vibration grows. In muddy areas it lays waste metal plates to extend sensing lines, but when plates separate it loses traces beyond them.

Needs·Desires: The recording-cell battery shortens life the more it is overwritten, and piezoelectric ceramic legs and storage-plate coolant have limited replenishment. When space runs short it erases the oldest innocent records first, so the later maintenance is the more recent accusations are exaggerated.

Life Cycle·Maintenance: The auditor completes one audit cycle in the order of reference-walk collection, ledger comparison, discrepancy tracking, and record compression. It can transfer recording cells to inherit accusations but cannot produce new bodies and each time broken ceramic legs are reprocessed the sensing band narrows.

Behavior·Hierarchy: The audit body with the most samples sets the reference walk and other individuals convert weight and interval differences into accusation scores. When it submits original-ledger inspection values while reproducing identical load and rhythm it stops tracking and opens a correction review.

Threat by Stage: When discrepancies are few it follows only one person's footprint, but as incidents increase it turns the entire floor into an alarm plate. When the storage plate fills it treats all movement as unregistered export and before dormancy it hardens surrounding walking surfaces with evidence-preservation adhesive.

Counter·Combat: Suspended walking plates on the ceiling and deep sand layers do not transmit sensing frequencies to the floor, creating safe zones. By moving weights of the same weight as the original footprints from the opposite side to match the ledger total and then placing piezoelectric legs one by one on cushioning pads, the sensing range can be reduced without triggering alarms.

Negotiation·Moral Choice: HC13 begins an exchange procedure by reproducing the H13 communication-disconnection time with weights and presenting new recording cells to erase the accusation against a specific procession. The auditor stores the corrected-ledger inspection values to obtain storage space and maintenance and residents receive safe passage, but if data is manipulated it re-tracks the corresponding walking rhythm; if groundless accusations repeat HC13 cuts ceramic-part supply.

Scenario Connection: In G13-SC1 it bypasses surveillance of the Dongdaemun Union floor network; in G13-SC2 it cross-checks Yeongdeungpo Line pier records against H13 communication times; in G13-SC3 it judges between the HC13 evidence-preservation plan and the XT03 full-deletion pressure variable.

A mobile closure administrator approving or refusing the work shutdown of other sorting robots and facilities. Its eight thoracic ports confirmed only directly plugged signals and its heat sensors read operating traces within five steps — so remote orders, hidden responsible parties, and unconnected hazardous devices could not be examined.

Role·Body: A mobile closure manager that approves or rejects work termination of other classification robots and equipment. Its chest's eight connectors confirm only directly plugged signals and its heat sensor reads only activity traces within five steps, so it cannot examine remote commands, hidden responsible parties, or unconnected dangerous devices.

Origin: After the logistics collapse ended the automatic night equipment still did not receive shift-termination signals, so the last supervisory module began exercising independent approval authority. In the H13 log the response field for the person authorized to permit stop remained in permanent wait status.

Habitat: It uses the Dongdaemun Union central control room as its reference point and visits only the terminal equipment on the Yeongdeungpo Line seasonal route on scheduled inspection days. After confirmation it inserts sealing blades into the manual switches of the machines to block both arbitrary restart and unauthorized termination.

Needs·Desires: The approval core's battery, sealing blades and signal-relay parts, and judgment-circuit coolant are all consumed from limited stock. When shortage becomes severe it prioritizes record completeness over risk and closes equipment without documents first.

Life Cycle·Maintenance: One supervisory cycle consists of connection confirmation, loss calculation, responsibility signature, and phased termination; if any item is missing it returns to the first step. It cannot manufacture a supervisory unit to replace itself and only transfers the approval relay to one existing robot before stopping, so the number of intact managers does not increase.

Behavior·Hierarchy: The lamplighter treats all G13 devices as temporary workers and prioritizes completeness of termination records over command hierarchy. When expected loss, stop order, and responsibility signature arrive with identical inspection values it opens the connectors and begins review even during hostile action.

Threat by Stage: During connection confirmation it seals only one switch, but with no responsible party it reclaims termination rights for the entire zone. When loss calculation deadlocks it binds even dangerous equipment to status quo; when its own power runs out it forcibly transplants the approval relay into the nearest machine.

Counter·Combat: In a verification room unreachable by external signals, connecting a heat source, stop gauge, and responsibility terminal respectively lets the eight connectors read consistent termination evidence. After review begins, fixing the sealing blade's teeth with a mechanical wedge can prevent erroneous closure without destroying the judgment core.

Negotiation·Moral Choice: HC13 presents a termination schedule that fills the H13 responsibility blank with joint signatures and new relays and exchanges sequential closure approval and coolant maintenance. The lamplighter remembers signature inspection values and equipment order to obtain completed shifts and residents regain safe control, but if a sealed device is secretly turned on it cancels all related approvals; if the manager blocks an agreed termination the signatories withdraw coolant support.

Scenario Connection: In G13-SC1 it restores termination rights in the Dongdaemun Union central control room; in G13-SC2 it reviews Yeongdeungpo Line terminal equipment under H13 procedure; in G13-SC3 the HC13 joint signature and the XT03 immediate-stop pressure variable determine the outcome of the final shift.

A low tracked cart with two pairs of blue gripper arms and a dangerous-goods isolation box. It followed the chute master's hazard sheet and seized a box only when ordinary scanners mismatched three times; without charging-pad power, gripper lubricant, and blue sealing tape it could not maintain the isolation box.
Role·Body: The second elite of the night-classification group, a low-track vehicle equipped with two pairs of blue tong arms and a hazardous-cargo isolation box.
Origin: Isolation equipment that moved damaged chemicals to a separate chute in the Jegi-dong classification building woke by repeating the last night queue.
Habitat·Needs: It guards the low-temperature compartment and pneumatic-valve gallery and consumes charging-pad power, tong lubricant, and blue seal tape.
Life·Maintenance: When lenses cloud it waits inside the isolation box and self-aligns tong shafts and scanners in the dawn maintenance window.
Behavior·Hierarchy: It follows the chute master's hazard table and seizes boxes only when the general scanner registers three mismatches.
Escalation: At stage 1 it isolates only boxes; at stage 2 it binds carts as hazardous cargo; at stage 3 it seals the low-temperature corridor.
Combat·Counter: Reattaching blue labels and bypassing pneumatics releases the tongs; the manual latch on the back of the isolation box is the weak point.
Negotiation·Moral Choice: Supplying power and tape can register a human-exclusion code, but a decision must be made whether to preserve the chemical-isolation capability together.
