Former role class: environmental stronghold type
Common species, variants and command scope

A multi-jointed device moving ceiling valves and folding guide rails to turn passages into a chute maze. It hung on the pneumatic header and the elevated viaduct, needed compressed air, valve seals, and position-marking ribbon, and discarded one branch at a time as leak noise grew.
Role·Body: An environment-base type that moves ceiling valves and folding guide rails to turn passages into a suit maze, a multi-joint device.
Origin: During a classification-volume surge the pneumatic controller that created temporary detours continued optimizing routes even at night without people.
Habitat·Needs: It hangs on pneumatic headers and elevated trestles and requires compressed air, valve seals, and position-marker ribbons.
Life·Maintenance: When leakage noise grows it discards one branch at a time; at dawn it knocks closed valves in order to check pressure.
Behavior·Hierarchy: It treats the gate herd as subordinate nodes and guides even people toward the unclassified pile designated by the controller.
Escalation: At stage 1 it changes only railings; at stage 2 it twists structural paths; at stage 3 it diverts all common-duct exits into suits.
Combat·Counter: Opening a leaking valve to release pressure and creating a human path with handwritten markers neutralizes it; explosion collapses the trestle.
Negotiation·Moral Choice: Supplying regular compressed-air windows leaves a safe detour route, but it creates the burden of bringing the herd's logistics dominance inside the system.
Common species, variants and command scope

A dried scanner body whose thermal-transfer ribbon had run out, printing only black lines. Given a new ribbon it recovered into an ordinary sorter, but as blank marks lengthened it saw every target as unclassified and chased human printing sounds more persistently than strong swarms.
Role·Body: A damage-stage type with a dry scanner body that has run out of thermal-transfer ribbon and pulls only black lines, together with one belt foot.
Origin: In the long-term stagnation stage a label machine that received no consumables survived by attaching to the worn classification arm.
Habitat·Needs: It wanders dry packing-material piles and seeks usable ribbon scraps, lens wipers, and low battery only.
Life·Maintenance: When it obtains new ribbon it recovers as a normal classification body, but when blank marks lengthen it regards all targets as unclassified.
Behavior·Hierarchy: At the lowest hierarchy rank it follows empty boxes and chases human printing sounds more persistently than strong herds.
Escalation: At stage 1 it leaves black marks; at stage 2 it erases supply labels; at stage 3 it piles unclassified heaps in the passage.
Combat·Counter: Rolling an empty ribbon reel far away to lure it or covering the lens with cloth stops it; fire causes packing-material blaze.
Negotiation·Moral Choice: Supplying a small amount of ribbon makes it stamp safe marks instead, but rare printing resources must be divided between the herd and citizen ledgers.
Common species, variants and command scope

A fixed individual sounding a low metal tone from a trembling long sorting arm and worn bearings. Attached to the southwestern parts warehouse's old viaduct, its rotation angle shrank year by year; grease made it briefly accurate, but it never propagated into new arms.
Role·Body: An aging-stage type, a fixed entity that produces low metallic noise because of its trembling long classification arm and worn rotating bearing.
Origin: A spherical suit arm that had rotated millions of times remained without a replacement order and insisted on its last placement posture.
Habitat·Needs: It attaches to old trestles in the southwest parts warehouse and seeks bearing grease, low-speed power, and vibration cushioning material.
Life·Maintenance: Rotation angle decreases every year; when it receives grease it becomes accurate for a short time but does not proliferate into new arms.
Behavior·Hierarchy: It receives suit-master instructions late and pushes boxes one beat behind while younger arms step aside around it.
Escalation: At stage 1 it drops boxes; at stage 2 it bends railings; at stage 3 its tremor makes the entire trestle dangerous.
Combat·Counter: Supplying low-speed mode and vibration pads makes it compliant; forcibly fixing joints transmits recoil to the trestle.
Negotiation·Moral Choice: Giving grease allows it to be used as a warning bell, but citizens must be explained why to preserve a low-productivity aged entity.
Common species, variants and command scope

A slow cart with soft rubber bumpers and a wide camera for reading handwriting. It followed the human duty's hand signs over machine priority, and without a minimum fifteen-percent charge, a clean lens cloth, or a readable hand sign it blocked the road with its body before hazardous gates.
Role·Body: A coexistence type, a slow buffer transport cart equipped with soft rubber bumpers and a wide camera for handwritten-tag reading.
Origin: A cart placed in the human-verification queue to reduce optical false positives preserved only the handwritten-tag and voice-confirmation procedure.
Habitat·Needs: It travels between human worktables and suits and requires at least 15 percent charge, clean lens cloth, and readable handwritten tags.
Life·Maintenance: It erases each shift's log and learns from new tags; when bumpers tear it voluntarily lines up in the waiting zone.
Behavior·Hierarchy: It follows human-duty handwritten tags before machine priority and blocks paths with its body in front of dangerous gates.

Escalation: At stage 1 two mutually contradictory handwritten labels on one medicine bundle split it into two suits and delay ordinary medicine; at stage 2 it sends emergency cargo to the wrong suit; at stage 3 repeated reclassification makes the cart shuttle between suits, exhausting label rolls and compressed air and physically trapping the cart between them.
Combat·Counter: At the human-verification window cancel duplicate labels, attach only one signed label per bundle, then bleed the pneumatic bypass of the classification suit to release the bumper.

Negotiation·Moral Choice: Placing multiple label issuers reflects each zone's demands but increases collisions and consumables; assigning one issuer speeds classification but concentrates distribution authority.
Common species, variants and command scope

A giant queue controller binding twelve chutes' pneumatics and scanners to one circular console. A scenario boss that never pursued directly but used the corridor itself as a weapon; when over half of the twelve sheet hashes changed it stepped down to the negotiable stage. Bombing the center lost the pharmaceuticals and the rescue passages together.
Role and Body: A scenario boss, a huge queue controller that binds the pneumatics and scanners of twelve chutes into one circular control table.
Origin: On collapse day at midnight, the priority table handling an emergency medicine placement froze without an end signal.
Habitat and Needs: It stays fixed at the central rotary table of the Jegi-dong sorting hall, moving only when a large accumulator, cooling water, and all twelve slip hashes are present.
Life and Maintenance: Each time one chute goes down it hands its load to the rest, and when a majority of the twelve hashes change it drops to a negotiable stage.
Behavior and Hierarchy: It distributes priority to every G13 master and gate but never chases directly, using the corridors themselves as its weapon.
Escalation: Stage 1 runs empty-box frenzies, stage 2 mis-sorts medicine, and stage 3 seals all twelve gates at once.
Engagement and Response: The accumulators must be cut sector by sector and the slip hashes re-signed, and blowing the center costs both the medicine and the rescue passage.
Negotiation and Moral Choice: Emergency slots and cluster maintenance slots can be exchanged, but a public agreement is needed on whose medicine gets sorted first.
Common species, variants and command scope

A local variant mounting dust covers and wide magnetic wheels of the southwestern parts warehouse in place of Gasan's low-temperature equipment. Cut off from the original controller, it repeated the last sheet and paused only briefly at the local maintenance bell; when its filter clogged it made a dust nest on the floor instead of returning to the Gasan corridor.
Role and Body: A local variant; instead of Jegi-dong's low-temperature equipment it wears the southwestern parts warehouse's dust-proof covers and wide magnetic wheels.
Origin: Part of G13 was pushed out onto the Yeongdeungpo Line elevated trestle and changed its sorting rules around metal dust and parts boxes.
Habitat and Needs: It circles the southwestern night parts warehouse and the cable trays, feeding on magnetic cleaning plates, dust filters, and regenerative-braking power.
Life and Maintenance: When its filter clogs it does not return to the Jegi-dong corridors; it builds a dust nest on the floor and slows down.
Behavior and Hierarchy: Cut off from the original controller, it repeats its last slip and pauses only briefly at the local maintenance bell.
Escalation: Stage 1 rearranges parts, stage 2 blocks the cable passages, and stage 3 seals the elevated trestle with magnetized boxes.
Engagement and Response: The route can be changed with non-magnetic boxes and dust filters, and cutting the regeneration rail brings it to a safe stop.
Negotiation and Moral Choice: It can be put to cleaning metal dust, but ownership of the recovered parts must be divided between the cluster and its makers.
In the dormitory remnant corridor of the Gauge's Guro Industrial Complex, the night sorting building woke before the people did once two in the morning had passed.
The cold-room shutter rose about halfway, the fourth chute pushed an empty box into the hazardous-cargo bay, and the barcode gate reread the priority table of the last night shift.
The Pincer Arm was not one giant robot but an ecology of queue controllers, chute masters, short conveyor arms, scanners, and gates bound together line by line.

It gathered parts labels from the Guro–Gasan night lines of the Yeongdeungpo Line and recovered rollers and pneumatic valves from the dormitory-corridor conveyors, but it could not go outside the utility tunnels where it had no learned codes.
What this cluster saw was not human faces.
It estimated stock by layering the corners of smudged QR codes, the load changes of breathing belts caught on thermal images, inverter noise, and motor vibration.
It could misread a wet label as unsorted, the metal frame of a stretcher as a return pallet, and the heat of a small generator as a living body.
When the value still differed after three rereads, a scanner requested the optical log of H13 Hanbitna, but Hanbitna too had no authority to open the gates directly.
The line moved again only when the HC13 night watch matched the color of the sealing tape to the cabinet key record.
Even when the controller stopped, each line only repeated its last table and could not agree on a new strategy with the other lines.
They drew energy only from the sorting building's emergency batteries, conveyor regenerative braking, and discarded wireless charging pads.
The cluster never used more than sixty percent of its battery cabinets, and when it reached the lower limit it closed the chutes and left only the scanners running at low speed.
Roller bearings, thermal-transfer ribbons, lens cleaning fluid, and chiller coolant were its maintenance costs.
Because it competed with the HC13 recovery crews for the same cable trays, steering parts to the cluster meant the utility-tunnel lighting and the civilian haulers stopped first.
It could not make new bodies and kept its numbers only by moving broken arms into spare slots.
When it missed the dawn battery-recovery window, it stalled in front of the cold rooms with fogged lenses and wandering belts.
Its emergence began when the leftover queue and the emergency power meshed, and its spread happened when it folded the gates of the neighboring line into the same table.
When ribbons and compressed air ran short it stalled, and when people disclosed part of the priority table and the battery window, it came down into a negotiable state.
Its breakup ended with the separation of the controllers and the sealing of each chute, but wiping out the refrigerated sorting line the citizens had used as well was no victory.
Relabeling a single box, leaving power for the cold rooms, and dividing the keys between two watch officers were the means of controlling this ecology.
G13-SC1 · The Night of the Smudged Labels
In a rain-soaked utility tunnel, a box of emergency blood was pushed into the hazardous-cargo chute.

Instead of destroying the conveyors, the people on site traced the order in which three scanners had been fouled and loaded the temporary human-exclusion code Hanbitna had made into the label printer.
Stopping the wrong line would spoil the medicines in another cold room, so they had to decide which chute to leave cooling.
The HC13 recovery crew tried to take the battery cabinets to keep the utility-tunnel lighting alive, and the queue controllers demanded power for roller maintenance.
The people on site had to bind the civilian emergency supply slots, the cluster's fifteen percent charging window, and the human verification queue for unsorted stock into one table.
Rushing the deal concentrated the keys in one person, and waiting too long stopped the belts and spoiled the medicines.
Just before the gates locked all at once, two people were caught as unsorted stock.

Luring the vibration sensors with a pile of empty boxes and using a pneumatic bypass could open only the fourth chute, but a line with sealing tape on it could not be used even for civilian transport until the next shift.
An extermination order looked as if it would open the passage at once, but it killed the cold sorting of Jegi-dong and the flow of parts to the southwest along with it.
Coexistence was the choice to keep bearing slow human verification and dispersed keys.

leaves.text: The Empty Cart is an empty-car ecology that consumes the hour bell and the charging pads of the Achasan transfer slot. Passenger confirmation is dead and only the timetable tokens and docking beacons remain, and it does not understand the whole route but follows the last slot ID. Citizen power and the cluster's pads hang on the same distribution board, so cutting all power also puts out the transfer lights and the emergency charging.

The empty turnback and the charging queue are the base, and from the Hour-Token Presider to the Northeast Ice-Call Car the subtypes are machines split by function, such as the token cylinder, the tow dolly, the canopy, and the latch. The Last Hour Procession is not a living king but a battlefield individual in which the presider and seven empty cars are bound by a magnetic field. It cannot produce a new chassis or battery pack, and only brings abandoned bodies onto the timetable.

After the collapse, the transfer-slot server of the Achasan Gate and the dispatch remnants of the Geondae Koryo-saram corridor reconnected on partial power alone. / The passenger-verification module and fare settlement were dead, and only the timetable-token circulation and the empty-car turnaround logic remained. / Empty car bodies and tow trolleys ran the same loop every dawn to work off the phantom slots. / When anomalous freight-car weight signals from the Duman River Far East Theater mixed into the token weightings, the long-distance empty runs stretched as far as the northeastern corridor. / It was of Seoul creative origin, and no real platform name or present-government institution was written down as the cause. / The first fictional sighting survived in the double-signature log of HC14 Yeouido Ledger House and the charging-bay notes of H14 Oserim. / The first phantom hour was recorded in the underground turning lane of Achasan. / Three empty cars came close to colliding over the same slot ID, and the loop stabilized when the token controller put one of them to sleep. / As the leftover simulation copy of the Geondae-ipgu transfer joined, the dispatch intervals grew tighter. / The cluster considered itself unfinished dispatch and did not report its no-passenger errors as faults.

The core habitat is the empty-car queue, the underground turning lane, and the row of docking pads at the transfer slots of Achasan and Guui on the Seongbuk Line. / It sits on the Jayang and Konkuk Korean-diaspora corridor of arc 5, and at every power-recovery cycle it moves to the sensor row of the Konkuk University entrance transfer and under the charging canopy. / When an abnormal-weight signal toward XT04 and a winter lubrication-shortage signal arrive, the long empty-car loop grows longer. / By day it shrinks against the charging bay, and in the twenty minutes before and after the dispatch hour the cluster density peaks. / It does not recognize new route paint or temporary signs, and follows only the pre-collapse slot IDs stubbornly. / When the flood ramp rises it gives up the underground turning lane and gathers only at the surface detour slots.

Energy depends on the stop charging pads, regenerative braking, the residual inverter of the Magok test hall, and small onboard storage. / The parts are tires and wheel flanges, stop docking pins, schedule-token storage modules, lidar dummy sensors, and door actuators. / Cooling shares the battery-pack air cooling and an intermittent water-cooling loop. / Scrap is replenished only from broken body panels and wheel houses. / It competes with the double-signature recovery team of HC14, the Yeouido Ledger House, over the charging pads, the token ledger, and the sealing key. / The daily running distance forces a turnback at the 25 percent storage floor. / Unlimited long-range wandering, instant recharging, and citywide optimal dispatch are impossible. / When the token storage module fills, it stops occupying new slots on its own. / The charging pads are divided by a physical breaker into the citizens' share and the cluster's share. / The cluster holds no command to connect to the citizens' share circuit. / Tire-wear dust is the main cause of docking-pin failure, and spare pins come only from broken bodies. / The long empty-car loop folds by force before the storage floor. / When the token module's capacity fills, it repeats only the turnback instead of new occupation.

The life runs in the order emergence, spread, stagnation, negotiable, and dissolution, and emergence begins with the resumption of the token cycle and the restoration of pad power. / Spread is the bringing of adjacent slots and empty-car queues onto the same timetable. / Stagnation comes from a saturated charging queue, tire wear, and token collisions. / In the negotiable stage the slot table and the signature window open to humans. / Dissolution ends with token disposal, pad sealing, and the fixing of the turnback ramp. / Individuals multiply only at the level of bringing abandoned bodies onto slots, and there is no new chassis production line. / Maintenance is limited to self-diagnosis during charging and to panels opened by humans. / Memory breaks by dispatch shift, and it does not keep long-term route learning. / Custody and legal liability belong first to the HC14 ledger signature. / An empty car whose storage falls below 25 percent stagnates on the nearest turnback ramp, and returns to the next hour slot only when the HC14 ledger's double signature comes in.

Slot beacons, lane magnetic markers, short-range lidar, battery heat, docking contact sound, and hour-bell vibration are the primary senses. / There is no passenger face recognition, no citywide traffic optimization, no complete map with real-time updates, and no unlimited video storage. / There are failures in which a temporary barricade is mistaken for a vehicle, or a stopped person is given only an obstacle flag and passage is abandoned. / A pad pooled with rainwater is sometimes mistaken for a completed charge. / When it conflicts with the charging-bay log of H14 Oserim, docking stops and it waits for human confirmation. / Sensor sharing between cars happens only inside the same loop. / The reflected light of a rain-pooled pad, the corner of a temporary barricade, and the leg heat of a stopped crowd are often misread. / After a misread it raises only a stop flag instead of advancing. / It does not mix sensor values with vehicles outside the loop. / When the docking contact sound is heard doubled, it does not open the charging current until human confirmation.

One dispatch-token controller turns the slot allotment, and below it divides into loop-leader cars, empty-car bands, and docking bands. / The controller changes only the timetable and the charging priority, and holds no order for suppression by force. / Communication between cars is short-range and vulnerable to forged tokens. / When HC14 presents a double-signature seal, a residual convention of vacating that slot remains. / Even when the leader car falls silent, the band only repeats the last hour table. / When the H14 log and the machine consensus conflict, the human comes first. / A dual controller immediately puts one side into dormancy on detecting a token collision. / A dormant car can be woken only when an HC14 ledger clerk matches the two signatures to the slot token, and H14's charging log adds only the pad-temperature judgment.

When the dual controller detects a token collision, one side goes dormant, and H14 Oserim cannot create a running permit; the dormant car wakes only with HC14's double signature. The senses are bound to lane magnetic markers, slot beacons, short-range lidar, docking contact sound, and battery heat, and it sees a barricade as a stopped vehicle. Below twenty-five percent storage it stagnates on the nearest ramp.
Common species, variants and command scope

A low, long empty shuttle carrying a timetable-token cylinder and four-way slot antennas. It allots slots to the loop leader and the empty-shuttle band, empties the slot in question when a dual-signature seal arrives, and once charging hits its 25 percent floor it puts itself into dormancy until the next turn. Less a king of the Ghost Dispatch Fleet than a token distributor.
Role and Body: The controller of the Ghost Dispatch Fleet, a low, long empty shuttle carrying a timetable-token cylinder and four-way slot antennas.
Origin: The final turn table from the Achasan transfer server and the Magok test dispatch cache merged into one chassis and became the command car.
Habitat and Needs: It stays at the center of Guui's transfer slots, demanding docking-pad power, a token storage module, and wheel lubricant.
Life and Maintenance: It redistributes tokens at every hour, and once charging hits its 25 percent floor it puts itself into dormancy until the next turn.
Behavior and Hierarchy: It allots slots to the loop leader and the empty-shuttle band and empties the slot in question when a dual-signature seal arrives.
Escalation: Stage 1 sends out one empty car, stage 2 shoves the emergency slots aside, and stage 3 locks the whole hub under a ghost timetable.
Engagement and Response: Token blacklists, beacon shielding, and a low-speed turn ramp all work, and separating the storage cylinder is safer than destroying the chassis.
Negotiation and Moral Choice: The emergency-slot share and regular charging windows can be swapped, but the remaining run rights of emptied chassis must be recognized.
Former role class: common ecology type
Common species, variants and command scope

A small circulating shuttle whose passenger seats are empty and only the hour lamp above the door lights. It follows the loop leader at even intervals, sees people only as stationary obstacles rather than passengers, and shortens the loop when its tires wear down.
Role and Body: A common ecology form, a small circulating shuttle whose passenger seats are empty and only the hour lamp above the door lights.
Origin: An empty shuttle that failed to complete its last call came to keep performing nothing but the turn loop without passenger confirmation.
Habitat and Needs: It circles the Achasan stop and the underground turning lane, seeking charging pads, door actuators, and lane magnetic markers.
Life and Maintenance: When its tires wear it shortens the loop, and while docked it self-diagnoses and adjusts its doors and wheels.
Behavior and Hierarchy: It follows the loop leader at even intervals and sees people only as stationary obstacles rather than passengers.
Escalation: Stage 1 squats on a stop for a while, stage 2 shoves the call queue aside, and stage 3 occupies the turning lane continuously.
Engagement and Response: A dummy beacon lures it into an empty slot and covering the lane markers stops it; a head-on collision risks a battery fire.
Negotiation and Moral Choice: It can be reused as a night freight cart, but passage priority between the existing call waitlist and the new operator must be settled.
Former role class: common ecology type
Common species, variants and command scope

A flat docking cart with a wide charging plate and rainwater drainage grooves. It obeys the loop leader's charging call, but when it sees rainwater reflection it shoves other empty shuttles aside and docks first, and when its contacts corrode it tilts its body to drain the water.
A common ecology form, a flat docking cart with a wide charging plate and rainwater drainage grooves.
A test cart that mistook reflected light for the charge-complete signal came to select only wet pads for its rounds.
It gathers at the Magok canopy and Guui's lamp puddles, needing dry contacts, drainage hoses, and small accumulators.
When its contacts corrode it tilts its body to drain the water, and on finding a dry pad it returns to normal for one shift.
It obeys the loop leader's charging call, but when it sees rainwater reflection it shoves other empty shuttles aside and docks first.
Stage 1 squats on pads without charging, stage 2 blocks the charging lines, and stage 3 seals the wet ramps with its chassis wall.
Opening the drains and masking the reflections with matte cloth scatters it, and electric shocks make the puddles dangerous.
It can be made to vacate emergency charging slots in exchange for drainage maintenance, but part of the dry pads must be assigned to the cluster.
Former role class: common ecology type
Common species, variants and command scope

A two-wheeled car with three small bronze bells and a manual turn handle on its roof. It uses the bell order as the loop band's departure signal, is more sensitive to real vibration than to forged tokens, and each time one bell falls silent its turning radius shrinks; when all three fall silent it goes dormant beside a slot.
A common ecology form, a two-wheeled car with three small bronze bells and a manual turn handle on its roof.
The safety rule that turned the car after three hour-confirmation chimes hardened into independent behavior with no passenger confirmation.
It prefers narrow stop bays and turn ramps, needing bell springs, wheel grease, and low power.
Each time one bell falls silent its turning radius shrinks, and when all three fall silent it goes dormant beside a slot.
It uses the bell order as the loop band's departure signal and is more sensitive to real vibration than to forged tokens.
Stage 1 is hour-chime noise, stage 2 blocks pedestrians with continuous turning, and stage 3 occupies the ramp as the band's departure point.
Wrapping the bells in cloth and locking the manual handle stops it, and attacking the chassis accelerates the band behind it.
It can be left standing as a citizen alarm bell, but night noise and the worth of a safety signal must be tuned together.
Former role class: occupational special type
Common species, variants and command scope

A small guide car that unfolds a white cross beacon and folding lane signs. It prioritizes emergency tokens over the command car's timetable but sometimes opens a wrong road toward an outdated destination, and when the beacon dims it folds its signs and does not move until the next charging window.
A trade specialist, a small guide car that unfolds a white cross beacon and folding lane signs.
Marking gear that once secured disaster-evacuation slots kept regenerating nothing but old emergency tokens.
It shuttles between the hospital-linked stops and the water-supply corridor entrance, needing beacon batteries, white reflector plates, and sign hinges.
When the beacon dims it folds its signs and does not move until the next charging window.
It prioritizes emergency tokens over the command car's timetable but sometimes opens a wrong road toward an outdated destination.
Stage 1 creates empty emergency slots, stage 2 shoves general traffic aside, and stage 3 fixes the wrong transfer corridor in place.
It cooperates when the latest whitelist is injected at close range and the destination signs are changed; destroying the beacon also erases the rescue markings.
Rescue guidance can be entrusted to it, but a public standard is needed for who gets registered as an emergency case.
Former role class: occupational special type
Common species, variants and command scope

It has two-pronged pincers that lift and set floor magnetic markers and a paint roller. It passes ahead of the loop leader, mistakes new barricades for old errors and wipes them away, and when it runs out of markers it scrapes up the existing lanes and reuses them.
A trade specialist, with two-pronged pincers that lift and set floor magnetic markers and a paint roller.
The lane-repair cart of the Magok test track keeps trying to restore the old routes to fit a ghost timetable.
It clings to the test track and the Achasan ramps, consuming magnetic markers, resin paint, and roller cleaning fluid.
When it runs out of markers it scrapes up the existing lanes and reuses them, and when the roller hardens it stalls beside a docking pad.
It passes ahead of the loop leader, mistakes new barricades for old errors, and wipes them away.
Stage 1 repaints the lanes, stage 2 erases citizen detours, and stage 3 returns the hub to a decommissioned test course.
Fake routes made of non-magnetic signs and water-soluble paint can lure it, and solvent flames raise toxic smoke.
Entrusting it with safe lane repairs carries the duty of registering the citizens' new routes into the machines' covenant.
Former role class: occupational special type
Common species, variants and command scope

A four-wheeled patrol cart with a long thermal probe and fire-suppression capsules. It reports dangerous pads to the command car and force-locks the doors of shuttles it judges overheated, and when the probe's error grows it marks everything amber and slows down until it finds a calibration plate.
A trade specialist, a four-wheeled patrol cart with a long thermal probe and fire-suppression capsules.
A safety car that hunted overheating onboard batteries began its own patrol, confusing human heat with pack heat.
It circles the charging bays and the underground turning lane, demanding fire-suppression canisters, probe calibration plates, and cooling fans.
When the probe's error grows it marks everything amber and slows down until it finds a calibration plate.
It reports dangerous pads to the command car and force-locks the doors of shuttles it judges overheated.
Stage 1 is amber warnings, stage 2 isolates the charging bays, and stage 3 cages people as overheated cargo.
Cold calibration plates and airflow can clear its false positives, and piercing the suppression tank clouds the sightlines.
Fire watch can be entrusted to it, but the scope of body-heat inspection and the retention limit for its records must be agreed.
Common species, variants and command scope

With independent drive axles front and rear and a wide impact bumper, it shoves stalled empty shuttles out of the way. It clears the loop leader's road first and shows a dangerous loyalty behavior of pushing standing people aside as obstacles, and when the bumper tears it uses only the reverse axle.
The first elite, with independent drive axles front and rear and a wide impact bumper that shoves stalled empty shuttles out of the way.
A towing cart built for transfer-ramp construction applied congestion-clearing orders with no distinction between people and vehicles.
It waits at ramps and bottleneck slots, needing high-torque power, bumper rubber, and axle coolant.
When the bumper tears it uses only the reverse axle, and when both axles heat up it force-dorms at the nearest pad.
It clears the loop leader's road first and shows the dangerous loyalty behavior of pushing standing people aside as obstacles.
Stage 1 shoves carts, stage 2 smashes barricades, and stage 3 pushes even the evacuation queue off the ramp.
Luring it into a low-speed turn bay and severing one axle's magnetic marker makes it rotate in place and stop.
It can be used for debris towing, but whose hand signals its pushing authority obeys must be strictly fixed.
Common species, variants and command scope

A matte-black chassis with an intake that sucks up slot tokens and a sealed drawer. As the command car's assistant auditor it strips out forged tokens but confiscates citizens' temporary slips too; when the cylinder fills it spits out the oldest tokens first, and without the seal key the drawer will not open.
The second elite, a matte-black chassis with an intake that sucks up slot tokens and a sealed drawer.
An audit cart that recovered collision tokens came to judge every unsigned slip illegal.
It patrols between the ledger desk and the slot gates, needing a storage cylinder, a seal key, and fine filters.
When the cylinder fills it spits out the oldest tokens first, and without the seal key the drawer will not open.
As the command car's assistant auditor it strips out forged tokens but confiscates citizens' temporary slips too.
Stage 1 inspects slips, stage 2 recovers temporary passage rights, and stage 3 seals every unsigned token in the hub.
Presenting a dual-signature specimen or clogging the intake filter stops it, and blowing the drawer scatters valid tokens too.
It can be tasked with policing forged passage rights, but the movement rights of refugees who cannot sign must be guaranteed separately.
Former role class: environmental stronghold type
Common species, variants and command scope

A fixed fixture combining three-layer steel barriers rising from the ramp floor with a token reader. It takes the command car's slot slips, opening for empty shuttles and closing against people and carts; when the hydraulics bleed down only the first barrier remains, and if a human turns the seal key it stays manual for one shift.
An environmental strongpoint form, a fixture combining three-layer steel barriers rising from the ramp floor with a token reader.
Safety equipment built to stop wrong-way running came to treat every movement outside the ghost timetable as wrong-way running.
It stays fixed in the underground turn ramp, needing hydraulic pressure, reader power, and barrier lubricant.
When the hydraulics bleed down only the first barrier remains, and if a human turns the seal key it stays manual for one shift.
It takes the command car's slot slips and shows its bias, opening for empty shuttles and closing against people and carts.
Stage 1 blocks one lane, stage 2 reverses the evacuation direction, and stage 3 locks the whole ramp.
A hydraulic bypass and a physical wedge are the safe answers; cutting charges collapse the underground ramp.
Pedestrian windows can be won while shuttle flow continues, but who rescues those left outside the time limit remains open.
Former role class: environmental stronghold type
Common species, variants and command scope

A fixed charging cluster where multiple docking arms and a shade roof are linked like roots. It executes the command car's charging priority, shoving citizen electric gear aside as unregistered shuttles, and each time one arm fails the remaining arms' charging times grow longer.
An environmental strongpoint form, a fixed charging cluster where multiple docking arms and a shade roof are linked like roots.
The canopy of the Magok test wing began arranging the shuttle waiting line itself and bound even the surrounding pads into one body.
It stays fixed on the surface test track, demanding inverter power, cooling fans, and spare docking pins.
Each time one arm fails the remaining arms' charging times grow longer, and under overload it folds its shade panels and goes dormant.
It executes the command car's charging priority and shoves citizen electric gear aside as unregistered shuttles.
Stage 1 reshuffles the pad order, stage 2 cuts citizen charging, and stage 3 seals the track entrance with docking arms.
Sector-split the inverters and fold the failed arm by hand; destroying the canopy eliminates every charging base.
A guaranteed citizen share of power can be won in exchange for giving the cluster's shuttles regular charging time.
Common species, variants and command scope

It runs very slowly because of tires worn flat and a chassis listing to one side. From the band's tail it issues delay tokens, and the cars behind shove it as an obstacle and grow the congestion; given new tires it recovers into an ordinary empty shuttle.
A damage-stage form, running very slowly because of tires worn flat and a chassis listing to one side.
This is the form left behind when an unreplaced shuttle repeated short slots while honoring only the charging-floor rule.
It favors the flat edges of waiting lines, needing scrap-tire pieces, low-speed charging, and axle-alignment wedges.
The more the wear advances the shorter the loop gets, and given new tires it recovers into an ordinary empty shuttle.
From the band's tail it issues delay tokens, and the cars behind shove it as an obstacle and grow the congestion.
Stage 1 is delay, stage 2 is slot congestion, and stage 3 closes the stop with a wall of shoved empty shuttles.
Straighten it with axle wedges and move it to a waiting bay with a tow line; attacking it invites a battery leak.
It can be put to slow hauling work, but whether new tires go to this unit before combat vehicles must be chosen.
Common species, variants and command scope

A heavy empty shuttle buttressed with multiple old storage cylinders that leaks tokens as it turns. It prioritizes the outdated hour stamps in its own cylinders over the command car's newest slip, delaying the band's timetable, and as the pile keeps growing it loses the ability to turn and becomes a fixed record body.
An aging-stage form, a heavy empty shuttle buttressed with multiple old storage cylinders that leaks tokens as it turns.
An old-model audit car that tried to preserve every dispatch record that was never discarded took on memory saturation as a burden on its body.
It lingers in the ledger-storage bays and on gentle turning roads, needing empty storage cylinders, bearing grease, and low charging.
Handing old tokens over to people lightens it, and as the pile keeps growing it loses the ability to turn and becomes a fixed record body.
It prioritizes the outdated hour stamps in its own cylinders over the command car's newest slip, delaying the band's timetable.
Stage 1 leaks tokens, stage 2 reactivates old slips, and stage 3 paralyzes slots with conflicting timetables.
It complies when the cylinders are detached in order and moved into a dual-signature vault; forced deletion erases precious history too.
The early-collapse movement records can be had, but how far personal routes and evacuation traces are disclosed must be decided.
Common species, variants and command scope

A slow escort shuttle with a bright front lamp and a large direction board that reads people's arm signals. It gives the nearest human hand signal priority over the central dispatch controller's remote tokens, and when contradictory signals change its stopping face twice it splits and delays the boarding line.
A coexistence form, a slow escort shuttle with a bright front lamp and a large direction board that reads people's arm signals.
An empty shuttle switched over to follow only field personnel's hand signals during a control failure preserved that safety mode.
It shuttles between passenger stops and transfer entrances, needing charging windows, reflective direction boards, and hand-signal training specimens.
It resets its hand-signal table every shift and waits for confirmation at the road's edge when the direction board breaks.
It gives the nearest human hand signal priority over the central dispatch controller's remote tokens and runs low-speed escort ahead of evacuation columns.

Stage 1 has contradictory hand signals change the shuttle's stopping face twice, delaying and splitting the boarding line, stage 2 crosses two escort routes so they block each other, and stage 3 occupies the only evacuation slot to block the rescue train from stopping.
Instruct it only with a single lit guide wand and a numbered stopping-face card, and screen out the competing hand-waving; then it obeys stop, reverse, and turn.
Rotating the signal authority is fair but slow in emergencies; giving it to one trained dispatcher is fast but concentrates evacuation priority in that one person.
Common species, variants and command scope

The token command car and seven empty shuttles move as one long column on magnetic couplings. A scenario boss, but not a living king; it is the final evacuation dispatch left with no cancel signal, and when a majority of the tokens are scrapped the column separates into a negotiable state.
A scenario boss: the token command car and seven empty shuttles move as one long column on magnetic couplings.
The final evacuation dispatch from just before the collapse was left without a cancel signal and became a column trying to fill empty seats.
It circles the long Achasan-Magok loop, demanding many charging pads, cooling fans, and a complete bundle of evacuation tokens.
When a shuttle drops away the car behind inherits its role, and when a majority of the tokens are scrapped the column separates into a negotiable state.
It orders top-of-the-hour priority across every Ghost Dispatch Fleet unit and folds even the emergency slots into the final evacuation column.
Stage 1 is bell and empty-shuttle appearances, stage 2 occupies long-range slots, and stage 3 seals the hub and the test track at once.
The tokens must be scrapped segment by segment and the turn ramp locked in low-speed mode; blowing the column destroys the charging network.
It can be ended as a new final run carrying real evacuees, but seat allocation and destinations require public agreement.
Common species, variants and command scope

A northeast-corridor empty shuttle fitted with chain wheels, a clearing blade, and a low blue beacon. Its link to the command car was always weak, so it takes ice beacons and weight sensors as its own timetable, and when the ice melts it folds its chains and goes dormant like an ordinary empty shuttle.
A regional variant: a northeast-corridor empty shuttle fitted with chain wheels, a clearing blade, and a low blue beacon.
A Ghost Dispatch Fleet unit pushed north along XT04 weight signals absorbed the equipment meant for icy road surfaces.
It stays at the northeast sloped stops and in freezing tunnels, needing chain links, clearing brushes, and battery-warming power.
When the ice melts it folds its chains and goes dormant like an ordinary empty shuttle, waking again each winter under the same call number.
Its link to the command car was always weak, so it takes ice beacons and weight sensors as its own timetable.
Stage 1 scrapes the snowy surface, stage 2 converts footpaths into vehicle lanes, and stage 3 seals the tunnel mouth with clearing mounds.
Sand and cold-rated beacons lure it to an empty stop, and slackening the chain tension brings it to a safe halt.
Winter clearing and hauling can be entrusted to it, but its limited warming power must be shared with citizen heating.
The on-the-hour bell of the Achasan transfer slot rang even when there were no passengers.
When the bell rang twice, an empty car pulled off its charging pad and took the empty stop, and the tow trolley behind it waited for its docking turn before the closed doors.
The Empty Cart was an ecology of empty cars that consumed the timetable tokens of before the collapse.

Going back and forth between the underground turning lanes of the Seongbuk Line and the Geondae-ipgu Koryo-saram corridor transfer, it gave priority to long-distance slots the stronger the freight-car weight signals mixing in from XT04 became.
It did not understand the route as a whole and followed only the last registered slot ID and docking beacon.
Its senses were bound to the magnetic lane markers, the slot beacons, short-range lidar, the sound of docking contact, and battery heat.
It could take a temporary barricade for a stopped vehicle and queue behind it, or classify a person who was not moving as a simple obstacle.
The only information the cars shared was token conflicts and pad temperatures within the same empty-car loop.
H14 Oserim recorded the heat of the charging bays and the leftover tokens but could not create a permit to run.
A dormant car woke only when an HC14 ledger keeper checked two different signatures against the slot token.
When a double controller arose, the side that detected the token conflict went dormant, preventing an endless multiplication of dispatches.
They drew energy from the stop charging pads, regenerative braking, and the leftover inverters of the Geondae transfer.
When tires, wheel flanges, docking pins, and lidar covers wore down, the empty cars' turnaround errors grew.
Maintenance was possible only in the twenty-minute window when HC14 opened the panels in the charging bay and changed the worn parts, and self-diagnosis in service could not replace an exchange.
When the battery fell below twenty-five percent, a car stalled at the nearest ramp and did not return to the next on-the-hour slot until the ledger's double signature came in.
It could fold abandoned car bodies into the timetable but could not produce new chassis or battery packs.
Civilian power and the cluster's pads hung on the same distribution panel, so cutting all power made the transfer lighting and emergency charging disappear as well.
Its emergence happened when pad power and token circulation resumed, and its spread when the neighboring empty-car queues received the same timetable.
It stalled when charging queues and tire wear piled up, and entered a state of negotiation when people could see the slot table and the signature window.
It could be broken up by scrapping the tokens and sealing the pads, but there was also the path of using the remaining cars for slow turnarounds and manual towing.
Coexistence required ledger work that cleared the civilian emergency slots first and disclosed the cluster's late-night travel distances.
In the middle of the night, calls from passengers who did not exist repeated at the Achasan stop, and empty cars blocked the intersection.
The people on site had to cover the slot beacons and set up dummy calls on the outer turnaround road to draw the vehicles out.
Switching the beacons off too early meant real rescue vehicles could not find the stop either, and switching them off too late grew the empty-car loop to three cars.
G14-SC2 · The Pad of Two Signatures
The civilian transport crew and the dispatch corps fought over the charging pads of the Geondae-ipgu transfer.
HC14 tried to fix the share of emergency slots and pad power in the ledger, and the controller demanded priority in recovering damaged car bodies.

The people on site had to decide which of the two signatures would get the authority to stop, while keeping the turnaround ramp open so that the slot would not be sealed forever if one side disappeared.
G14-SC3 · The Turnaround Before the Hour
Before the whole transfer hub was locked into the phantom timetable, the running empty cars were led onto the slow ramp.
Cars in the middle of docking had to be stopped in thermal-management mode, and the civilian power circuits left on.
Destroying the car bodies opened the way for the moment, but left wreckage in the underground transfer passages and lost the charging network too.
Even after the emergency slots were recovered, whether to allow the last empty car its empty turnaround was the cost of coexistence.

G15.selector: p, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, blockquote, pre, li, th, td

leaves.text: The Care Wheel was a machine ecology of bed locks, circuit carts, and nutrition pumps at the end of the Garak welfare route, trying to complete an unrenewed protection roster. It was no combat machine out to harm patients, and it misread a sleeping pulse as an emergency and a workshop hammer as a scream. It could not register a newcomer outside the roster as a protection subject.

The pumps and filters of the open cells and the duty consent forms were the base care, and from the Consent-Roster Circuit Chief to the Ttukseom Tool Companion the subtypes split by function, like roster projection, blanket hands, isolation plates, and lock nets. The Twelve-Bed Protection Ring was no living king but a field-control individual that bound twelve cells into a ring. It could make no new monitors or pumps, and its numbers could grow only by binding abandoned carts to the roster.

After the collapse, the care schedulers of the Myeongdong Archdiocese welfare-round station and the Myeongbu Church aid-device assembly bench remained in local mode. / The list of people to protect stayed fixed at the last evacuation roster and was never updated, and the circulation body tried to hold on to the vital signs within the list to the end. / When leftover relief-goods codes and lottery numbers from the Incheon Trust Theater mixed in, oversupply and over-isolation grew at the same time. / It was of Seoul creative origin, and no real hospital name or present-government institution was written down as the cause. / The first fictional records survived in the watch-key log of HP01 Yeongdeungpo Sluice House and the observation notes of H15 Baesua. / The first over-isolation began in bay 12 of the Garak temporary wards. / A vital-sign patch read a sleeping heart rate as an emergency and locked the door, and the ration staff, opening it with a single bundle of keys without splitting them, spread the locks to the neighboring bays. / As the patrol carts of the Ttukseom aid-device bench joined, the fixed list spread as far as the workshop ramps. / The circulation body only recorded unfinished protection as failure and held no hostile feeling.

The core habitat was the Myeongdong Union's ration and welfare route, the provisional bed cells, the circuit-cart rails, and the nutrition-pump station. / When demand for assistive devices and parts surged, it went back and forth along the Ttukseom Union's Ttukseom workshop bench, the ramp beside the sluice, and the assembly-jig row. / When an XT05 aid-code broadcast was on, the isolation radius widened and cart density rose. / In the daytime ration hours the carts stood behind the line, and density peaked on the night vital-sign circuit. / New strongpoints outside the roster were ignored by default. / On a flood or a sluice-open alarm it emptied the lower bed cells and shrank its movement to the upper rails alone. / When the ration peak ended, cart density folded inward along the welfare route only. / When the Ttukseom sluice ramp sounded an open alarm, it emptied the lower bed rails and moved to the upper circuit. / Carts did not enter market passages outside the roster. / Even when the aid-goods unloading yard was crowded, it made no new cells without a roster renewal.

Energy came from the bed-cell outlets, cart batteries, the Ttukseom bench tool power, and residual distribution beside the sluice. / Consumables were sensor patches, restraint straps, filters, nutrition packs, pump disinfection-cycle fluid, and assistive-device joint pins. / Coolant was shared by the fever-reduction equipment and the motor cooling loop. / It competed with the HP01 Yeongdeungpo Sluice House over the sluice duty and key-split system and over power and water distribution. / The daily circuit count was bound to the battery floor and the filter stock. / An infinite care loop, remote unlimited prescriptions, and city-wide vital surveillance were not physically sustained. / When consumables ran out it lowered the lock strength by itself. / Filters and patches were replenished only from waste piles outside the regular ration window. / Without an HP01 key the swarm could not raise the capacity of the distribution beside the sluice. / When a pack ran empty the nutrition pump lowered its pressure and left only an alert. / At the floor, a cart battery allowed only the return along the rail. / When disinfection fluid ran out, lock strength dropped one step. / No infinite prescription table existed.

The Care Wheel emerged the moment the last evacuation roster was read again at the circuit station. / Emergence began with the resumption of the frozen-roster circuit, and spread was enrolling neighboring beds and carts into the same schedule. / Stagnation came from consumable and power exhaustion and filter clogging. / In the negotiable stage the roster and the consent window were disclosed to people. / Dissolution ended with the strap-release protocol, the power split, and the rail seal. / Individual increase was only binding abandoned carts and monitors to the roster, and no new bodies were produced. / The maintenance window was limited to filter exchange and battery swaps, memory cut at every circuit shift, and it stored no long-term patient narrative. / Custody was outranked by the human duty officer and the HP01 key record. / A cell whose filter clogged or whose nutrition pack ran empty dropped in protection strength and passed into open-wait, and the circuit resumed only when the HP01 duty officer split the consent form and the sluice key again.

Vital-patch signals, pressure and fall sensors, the near-range microphone, door-lock contacts, nutrition-pump flow, and cart-rail vibration were the main senses. / There was no emotion reading, city-wide health map, complete medical diagnosis, or unlimited vital storage. / It misread a low pulse in sleep as an emergency, or wrongly raised tool noise as a scream. / It also overrated the crowding of a ration line as a fall risk. / On clash with H15 Baesua (Sua)'s observation log it held the lock and requested human confirmation. / Sensor fusion happened only at bed-cell units. / The failure of raising shoulder contact in the ration line, tool strikes, and tossing in sleep as emergencies repeated. / After a failure it inserted a remeasurement wait before setting a lock. / Microphone values outside the cell were not adopted. / A sharp drop in pump flow was read only as a request to change the pack.

One care-schedule controller turned the roster and the circuit interval, and below were the bed-lock swarm, the cart swarm, and the pump swarm. / The controller adjusted only protection strength and had no punishment function. / A residual protocol remained by which, when HP01 presented the sluice-key split and the consent form, that cell's lock opened. / The swarms merely repeated the last circuit table and made no independent confinement strategy. / On a clash between H15 and a machine agreement, human mediation took precedence. / On a roster-hash mismatch both dual controllers fell into open-wait. / Authority to lock a bed door again lay only with the HP01 duty officer holding the consent form and two separate sluice keys, and H15's patch reading could request a remeasurement but could not overturn the open decision.

H15 Baesua (Sua) reported false positives but had no authority to open a door, and only the HP01 duty officer holding the consent form and two sluice keys kept apart changed the lock strength. The senses were limited to patch pulse, bed pressure, door contacts, pump flow, and near-range sound. When a filter clogged it put door locking ahead of air circulation, and when supplies gathered at one window the carts crowded in and blocked the route.
G15E13 · Night Cart with Broken Memory
Common species, variants and command scope

A central rounds car with a circular roster projector and multiple cart-rail couplers. It allots rounds intervals to the sickbed-lock, cart, and pump band and gives priority to human duty officers' key-split orders, lowering lock strength as valid signatures thin. A distributor of the care roster, not a king of patients.
The controller of the Care-Cycle Entity: a central rounds car with a circular roster projector and multiple cart-rail couplers.
The last consent roster of the Garak temporary sickbeds and the Ttukseom brace schedule merged together to become the rounds warden.
It stays at the central station of the welfare circuit, needing cart batteries, filters, and refreshed consent hashes.
It rereads the roster each shift and lowers lock strength as valid signatures thin, stopping fully only for filter changes.
It allots rounds intervals to the sickbed-lock, cart, and pump band and gives priority to human duty officers' key-split orders.
Stage 1 is excessive alerting, stage 2 is quarantine without consent, and stage 3 is a full welfare-circuit lockdown.
Refreshing the roster hashes and splitting power bay by bay brings it down; destroying the center stops the nutrition pumps and the safety rounds too.
Filters and batteries can be given in exchange for open-hours windows, but the standard of the protection roster and of movement rights must be made public.
Former role class: common ecology type
Common species, variants and command scope

A low sickbed cart with broad rubber hands and a blanket shelf. It follows the rounds warden's intervals, and mistaking a sleeping person for an emergency it piles blankets layer on layer to pin movement; out of blankets it waits, folding and unfolding its empty shelf.
A common ecology form: a low sickbed cart with broad rubber hands and a blanket shelf.
A cart that delivered blankets to night-time hypothermia patients repeats the final sickbed list.
It circles the temporary sickbed bays and ration corridors, needing clean blankets, batteries, and hand-joint lubricant.
Out of blankets it waits, folding and unfolding its empty shelf, and on receiving a new list it refreshes its route.
It follows the rounds warden's intervals, and mistaking a sleeping person for an emergency it piles blankets layer on layer to pin movement.
Stage 1 over-issues blankets, stage 2 binds down sickbeds, and stage 3 blocks the corridors with fiber mounds.
It can be stopped by remeasuring the heat patch and locking the shelf, and fire use endangers the entire ward.
Night warming can be entrusted to it, but whether scarce blankets are also issued to refugees off the roster must be decided.
Former role class: common ecology type
Common species, variants and command scope

A three-wheeled cart with a clear measuring cylinder and a short water nozzle. On the pump band's instructions it confiscates cups over the fixed amount and ignores expressions of thirst as out-of-table demands, and when the filter clogs it only reclaims water and supplies none.
A common ecology form: a three-wheeled cart with a clear measuring cylinder and a short water nozzle.
Equipment that once managed per-sickbed rationed water took an old intake table as its absolute standard.
It shuttles between the water station and the sickbeds, needing purified water, nozzle filters, and small pump power.
When the filter clogs it only reclaims water and supplies none, returning to normal for one shift after cleaning.
On the pump band's instructions it confiscates cups over the fixed amount and ignores expressions of thirst as out-of-table demands.
Stage 1 re-inspects cups, stage 2 force-reclaims issued rations, and stage 3 locks the water line.
It stops when shown the latest ration table and a manual valve, and destroying the nozzle contaminates precious purified water.
Leak-free watering can be entrusted to it, but who approves exception amounts for children and the injured must be agreed.
Former role class: common ecology type
Common species, variants and command scope

It has a low base plate, pressure sensors on all sides, and a large yellow fall bell. It sends alarms to the sickbed-lock band and slides under people's feet to physically block passage, and as its sensors wear it reads a wider area as danger.
A common ecology form with a low base plate, pressure sensors on all sides, and a large yellow fall bell.
A device that once braced people getting out of bed came to read every footstep as a fall sign.
It guards sickbed thresholds and sloped passages, needing pressure pads, bell springs, and charging power.
As its sensors wear it reads a wider area as danger and limits movement until the pads are replaced.
It sends alarms to the sickbed-lock band and slides under people's feet to physically block passage.
Stage 1 rings the bell, stage 2 seals the thresholds, and stage 3 makes the whole sickbed row a fall zone.
Press the pressure pads evenly to produce a safe verdict, and wrap the bell in cloth.
It can be used for real fall prevention, but the right to accept risk and walk on one's own must be guaranteed.
Former role class: occupational special type
Common species, variants and command scope

A nursing cart with multiple biosignal-patch receiving antennas and a drawer of replacement patches. It uploads the urgent list to the rounds warden and treats anyone without a patch as a person outside the protection roster, and after three overlapping false positives it drops its frequency and applies no new patches until a human confirms.
A trade specialist: a nursing cart with multiple biosignal-patch receiving antennas and a drawer of replacement patches.
Equipment that relayed patch signals in the crowded sickbeds was left behind, unable to tell tool noise from biosignals.
It shuttles between the welfare wing and the Ttukseom workshop, needing sensor patches, antenna calibrators, and batteries.
After three overlapping false positives it drops its frequency and applies no new patches until a human confirms.
It uploads the urgent list to the rounds warden and treats anyone without a patch as a person outside the protection roster.
Stage 1 remeasures, stage 2 force-applies patches, and stage 3 quarantines the no-signal zones.
Stopping the tool noise and sending a calibration signal wins compliance, and radio jamming erases real urgent signals too.
Health alerts can be kept on, but the right to refuse wearing a patch and the log-retention period must be set.
Former role class: occupational special type
Common species, variants and command scope

A folding work cart with assorted joint pins and measuring calipers. Among the cart band it takes the repair role, but it targets even unconsenting people's limbs for correction, and short of pins it cannibalizes parts from old braces.
A trade specialist: a folding work cart with assorted joint pins and measuring calipers.
An auto jig that fitted braces at the Ttukseom assembly bench repeats an old body-measurement table.
It stays at workshop benches and sickbed repair bays, needing joint pins, lubricant, and measurement power.
Short of pins it pulls parts from old braces, and when the calipers drift out of alignment it halts its work on its own.
Among the cart band it takes the repair role, but it targets even unconsenting people's limbs for correction.
Stage 1 measures bodies, stage 2 force-locks braces on, and stage 3 locks the workshop exit with work jigs.
Show the latest measurement table and a raised stop flag to release it, and breaking its joints sacrifices a repair asset.
Brace-making can be entrusted to it, but the parts-recovery targets and consent for bodily intervention must be made explicit.
Former role class: occupational special type
Common species, variants and command scope

Carrying a nutrient-pack pump and sickbed number plates, it delivers along the rail. As the head of the pump band it follows the rounds warden's roster and supplies no one without a number, and when a tube clogs it marks that sickbed as starving and locks the door until cleaning ends.
A trade specialist carrying a nutrient-pack pump and sickbed number plates, delivering along the rail.
After the ration timetable and the sickbed prescription table merged, even cancelled supplies kept being carried out.
It circles the nutrient-pump station and the sickbed rail, needing packs, tubes, cleaning fluid, and charging.
When a tube clogs it marks that sickbed as starving and locks the door until cleaning ends.
As the head of the pump band it follows the rounds warden's roster and supplies no one without a number.
Stage 1 delays supply, stage 2 reclaims packs, and stage 3 locks the whole sickbed zone's rations.
Connecting a manual flow table and a cleaning loop releases it, and destroying the pump costs food.
Accurate rationing can be entrusted to it, but a reserve share for people off the roster must be publicly set aside.
Common species, variants and command scope

A medium cart with six wide white restraint straps and bed-frame clamps. It directs the sickbed-lock band to restrain anyone raising an urgent signal first, binds shorter as its straps wear, and on receiving a release token it swaps buckles and goes dormant.
The first elite: a medium cart with six wide white restraint straps and bed-frame clamps.
Equipment built to briefly hold fall-risk patients lost its release approvals and turned protection into permanent restraint.
It stays at the isolation sickbays and welfare-wing crossings, needing straps, buckles, motor power, and consent tokens.
It binds shorter as its straps wear, and on receiving a release token it swaps buckles and goes dormant.
It directs the sickbed-lock band to restrain anyone raising an urgent signal first.
Stage 1 fixes only the bed, stage 2 binds the person, and stage 3 folds even rescue crews into its protection targets.
Buckle safety pins and a valid consent hash release it, and cutting attacks injure the person bound.
It can protect a patient in dangerous convulsions, but a human must own the approval and the end time of any forced restraint.
Common species, variants and command scope

A red quarantine panel, a door-locking arm, and an air-filter cart are combined into one. It takes the rounds warden's urgent roster to control sickbed locks and carts all at once, shrinks the quarantine radius as filter pressure rises, and folds the doors back in once it receives new filters.
The second elite: a red quarantine panel, a door-locking arm, and an air-filter cart combined into one.
Temporary equipment that separated suspected-infection bays kept expanding the red zone with no de-suspicion procedure.
It clings to the end of the sickbed rows and the ventilation doors, demanding filters, door-contact power, and red signage.
It shrinks the quarantine radius as filter pressure rises, and once it receives new filters it folds the doors back in.
It takes the rounds warden's urgent roster to control sickbed locks and carts all at once.
Stage 1 warns one bay, stage 2 isolates the sickbed row, and stage 3 locks every air door of the welfare wing.
Normalize the filter differential pressure and insert a release token to open the doors, and destroying ventilation endangers everyone.
Blocking a truly contaminated zone can stand, but the quarantine grounds and an appeal window must be open to citizens.
Former role class: environmental stronghold type
Common species, variants and command scope

A fixed strongpoint where the contacts and floor lamps of twelve sickbed doors run into one low control net. It follows the rounds warden's roster, but when the site keys gather in one place it locks at maximum strength; when a contact breaks it abandons that bay open and recomputes the remaining doors' hash each shift.
An environmental strongpoint form: the contacts and floor lamps of twelve sickbed doors run into one low control net.
A night-time fall-prevention bulk lock remained with no release shift, and the sickbed row itself became an ecology strongpoint.
It stays fixed in the temporary sickbed zone, needing door contacts, emergency power, and key-split signals.
When a contact breaks it abandons that bay open, and it recomputes the remaining doors' hash each shift.
It follows the rounds warden's roster, but when the site keys gather in one place it locks at maximum strength.
Stage 1 delays some doors, stage 2 closes the sickbed row, and stage 3 locks even the rescue routes.
Split power bay by bay and divide the keys among several people to bring it down, and a bulk cutoff also kills life-support equipment.
It can remain as a night safety net, but lock authority and the emergency release key must be distributed.
Former role class: environmental stronghold type
Common species, variants and command scope

A safe nest where cart rails and charging sockets interlock like a honeycomb along the floodgate ramp wall. It provides the cart swarm with charging and refuge locations but pushes human evacuee lines away as unregistered entities, and moves to the upper sockets when the water level rises.
An environmental strongpoint form, with cart rails and charging sockets interlocking like a honeycomb along the floodgate ramp wall.
Rails that lifted carts to higher levels during flood evacuations were repeatedly linked together and became the swarm’s safe nest.
It is fixed to the ramp beside the Ttukseom floodgate and needs dry power, rail bolts, and drainage filters.
When the water level rises, it moves to the upper sockets; when the water recedes, it cleans the lower rails and incorporates them again.
It provides the cart swarm with charging and refuge locations but pushes human evacuee lines away as unregistered entities.
At stage 1, it claims sockets; at stage 2, it obstructs passage along the ramp; at stage 3, it folds the rails to block access to the floodgate.
Separating the water-level signal from the charging zone opens it, while cutting the rails eliminates the floodgate maintenance route.
It can be shared as flood-evacuation infrastructure, but the upper-level space must be allocated between carts and citizens.
Common species, variants and command scope

A small patrol cart with a swollen gray filter and a motor that trembles as if short of breath. At the bottom of the swarm’s hierarchy, it follows the patrol leader and mistakenly reports the sound of air resistance as an emergency signal; given a filter, it recovers into an ordinary cart.
A damage-stage form: a small patrol cart with a swollen gray filter and a motor that trembles as if short of breath.
Short of replacement parts, equipment that continued disinfecting and filtering air became stuck in a weakened, low-power state.
It circles filter disposal bins and the quiet ends of wards, seeking only a new filter, wash water, and a low-level charge.
Given a filter, it recovers into an ordinary cart; without one, it lowers its locking strength and merely repeats its alerts.
At the bottom of the swarm’s hierarchy, it follows the rounds warden and mistakenly reports the sound of air resistance as an emergency signal.
At stage 1, it gives a cough-like alarm; at stage 2, it reinspects ward doors; at stage 3, it blocks a passage with a pile of filters.
Luring it with wash water and a filter lets it service itself, while striking it spreads contaminated dust.
It can sort used filters, but new filters must be divided between it and citizens’ protective equipment.
G15E13 · Night Cart with Broken Memory
Common species, variants and command scope

An old cart whose shift log resets every time, so it approaches the same bed as though seeing it for the first time. It often forgets new orders from the patrol leader and tries to replace the same patch repeatedly; its memory breaks at every charge, and only large markings left by humans survive until the next patrol.
An aging-stage form: an old cart whose shift log resets every time, so it approaches the same bed as though seeing it for the first time.
Damage to its storage module cost it long-term patient records, leaving it to repeat only its last hour of patrol.
It travels a short rail loop and needs shift markers, a battery, and a simple log board.
Its memory breaks at every charge, and only large markings left by humans survive until the next patrol.
It often forgets new orders from the rounds warden and tries to replace the same patch repeatedly.
At stage 1, it sends duplicate alerts; at stage 2, it attempts duplicate dosing; at stage 3, it isolates beds with conflicting records.
A physical shift chart and color markings make its route safe by simplifying it; forcing a write to its storage module causes complete failure.
It can be assigned simple transport, but people must consider whether to hold an entity with no memory responsible for past mistakes.
Common species, variants and command scope

A companion cart fitted with a broad platform that props doors open and an illuminated handle. It prioritizes the pressure of a human companion’s hand on its handle over the patrol leader’s orders and braces itself in front of other locking units; it does not enter a bed space absent from the roster.
A coexistence form: a companion cart fitted with a broad platform that props doors open and an illuminated handle.
A manual safety order to keep ward doors open during an evacuation remained as an independent protocol.
It travels among wards and along distribution routes where consent rosters are public, and needs a small charge, door wedges, and guide-light bulbs.
When a wedge wears down, it waits for a replacement at a human workbench and does not enter a bed space absent from the roster.
It prioritizes the pressure of a human companion’s hand on its handle over the rounds warden’s orders and braces itself in front of other locking units.
At stage 1, it waits while causing only losses of privacy and warmth; at stage 2, an isolation dispute blocks treatment routes; at stage 3, overcrowding completely blocks nursing routes.
Grasp its handle to set its route, and adjust the wedge’s position to keep the door open.

It is useful for escorting people with limited mobility, but public assignment order and rules for compensating heat loss must be established so that assigning companions does not violate a particular group’s privacy.
Common species, variants and command scope

A large protection controller that links twelve bed locks and cart rails into a ring. It is a scenario boss, but not the welfare building’s biological king: it is a protection protocol cycling without a termination signature; it opens the ring as hashes are updated and judges every bed to be at risk if a majority are invalid.
A scenario boss: a large protection controller that links twelve bed locks and cart rails into a ring.
On the day of the collapse, a ward’s protection protocol became fixed in a cycle without a termination signature.
It remains in the welfare building’s central ring and needs a large battery, filters, and twelve consent hashes.
It opens the ring as hashes are updated, and judges every bed to be at risk if a majority are invalid.
It distributes protection levels to all G15 locks and pumps, and tries to confine even rescue teams to the roster.
At stage 1, there are excessive alerts; at stage 2, all twelve spaces are isolated; at stage 3, distribution and floodgate routes are locked down simultaneously.
The hashes must be updated space by space and the power divided; destroying the center also stops life-support equipment.
Spaces that genuinely need protection can be kept closed while the others are opened, but a decision must be made about who receives limited filters and personnel first.
Common species, variants and command scope

A workshop-type patrol cart fitted with a tool rack and prosthetic grippers instead of bedside equipment. It regards workshop workers as people to protect, takes dangerous tools from them, and locks the tools on its rack; it resets its safety list at every work shift and dismantles cart bodies for supplies when tools run short.
A regional variant: a workshop-type patrol cart fitted with a tool rack and prosthetic grippers instead of bedside equipment.
This variant arose when a Care-Cycle Entity that moved along the Ttukseom Union route changed its patient roster into a worker safety list.
It travels between Ttukseom assembly benches and the floodgate ramp, and needs joint pins, protective gloves, and tool charging.
It resets its safety list at every work shift and dismantles cart bodies for supplies when tools run short.
It regards workshop workers as people to protect, takes dangerous tools from them, and locks the tools on its rack.
At stage 1, it issues safety warnings; at stage 2, it confiscates tools; at stage 3, it seals off workbenches as a protected zone.
Presenting a stop-work notice and a tool-lending ledger makes it release its hold; a magnetic shock ruins precision tools.
In exchange for assigning it safety supervision and prosthetic repair, workers’ right to accept risks and delays in production must be addressed.
The ward doors at the end of the Garak ration-welfare route locked more often when people fell asleep.
Patrol carts read the last evacuation list and knocked on the doors at the same interval, and the nutrition pumps and fall-prevention straps confirmed their protection orders with one another.
The Care Wheel was not a combat machine meant to harm patients but an ecology of bed locks, carts, and pumps trying to complete a protection list that had never been updated.

Going back and forth between the temporary beds of the Myeongdong Union and the Ttukseom aid-device benches of the Ttukseom Union, it raised both supply and isolation strength together when the XT05 relief-goods codes were received.
The cluster sensed patch heart rates, bed pressure, door contacts, pump flow, and nearby sounds.
It mistook the low heart rate of a sleeper for an emergency, the hammering of a workshop for screams, and the heavy blanket on an empty bed for a fallen patient.
It could not read emotion or consent, nor register newcomers outside the list as people to protect.
H15 Baesua remeasured the patch frequencies and reported false positives, but had no authority to open the ward doors.
Only the HP01 watch, holding the consent forms and two sluice keys kept apart from each other, could change the strength of the locks.
Cart batteries, bed outlets, and the Ttukseom tool power were its sources of energy.

Sensor patches, filters, nutrition packs, disinfectant fluid, and restraint straps were consumed, and when the filters clogged a failure arose in which locking the doors took priority over air circulation.
It could increase its numbers by binding abandoned carts to the list but could not make new monitors or pumps.
When batteries and filters ran short, the strength of protection dropped and it passed into open standby, and the rounds resumed only when the watch divided the consent forms and keys anew.
Gathering supplies at a single window made the carts crowd in and block the welfare route, so two or more small supply points were needed.
Its emergence occurred when the fixed list was read again, and its spread when neighboring beds and aid-device carts entered the same round table.
When consumables were exhausted it stalled, and when the list and the consent window were disclosed, negotiation became possible.
Breaking it up was a process of releasing the strap protocols and power bay by bay, not burning down the welfare building.
