leaves.text: In Seoul in 2026, people worked shifts and made their living at the Yeongdeungpo treatment plant's sluices, the Sinjeong, Cheonwang, and Godeok depots, church pulpits, guard posts, and deed record rooms. People continued that work after the call mesh failed. In 2126, Changdong is an empty depot without a state; its watch duties survive in oral accounts. Over the past century, people have passed the skills learned in their work on to apprentices. Martial masters oversee that transmission and its taboos.

Training lay close to continuing the work. Being struck hardened the body; mending grew the hands. When a limb went, the trade changed, and a prosthesis went on only after the cut. After it went on, the numbers spoke. The place and timing before it went on were decided by unit commands.
Names were given by the oral record and the martial masters.

When abandoned station audio, radio noise and vehicle vibration overlap, Shin Jun recalls an old call rhythm and points to a route on the map. Shin Jongmok compares it with field records. Guardians confirm his consent and rest and rotate relay duty.

Training from water plants, depots, pulpits, guard posts, and archives divides into nine martial categories. Each category is a real 2026 Seoul martial art, sport, or military training that survived 100 years and changed.
What was not left as numbers
Bare-hand striking and grappling. Taekwondo, boxing, and special forces arts survived 100 years and changed.
Attack. Strongest at halt. In narrow passages the fist arrives first.
Sword arts. Kendo, bonguk geombeop, and iaido bamboo swords and footwork survived.
Attack. A trail of light remains where the blade passed in darkness.
Blade arts. Recovered weapons and maintenance tools became weapons.
Attack. Practiced cutting tile, walls, and equipment.
Polearms. Derived from bayonet, rebar, and fire axes.
Attack and halt. Pierces forward in narrow tunnels.
Kick arts. Taekwondo kicks and taekkyeon footwork were rediscovered.
Attack and movement. The next kick launches as the foot lands.
Bows and crossbows. Olympic archery and traditional Korean archery survived.
Ranged attack. Shot from tunnels and stations. Requires power for sights.
Thrown weapons. Bolts, nuts, debris, and shuriken.
Ranged attack and disruption. All metal parts from the subway become weapons.
Lightness skills. Derived from parkour, climbing, and gymnastics.
Movement. Runs on rails, catwalks, stairs, and ruins.
Footwork and balance. Dance, kendo steps, and taekwondo footwork became combat footwork.
Movement and evasion. Balance on wet floors, rails, and narrow passages.

Breath and endurance is inner-practice training that governs breathing, stamina, focus, and the tension and release of the body. Those who have learned it tire less in a fight and keep their breath and focus longer. Maintenance and support covers equipment, registers, and morale. Treating waterborne disease and repairing a hammer are different tasks.

The martial arts of 2126 are forms that the real martial arts, sports, and military training of 2026 Seoul survived and changed over a hundred years. There are thirty-eight arts across nine categories, each with a basic and ascended form.

A school was not the state-name cell. The heads of the sixteen states did not represent their state's hands; title, trade, and martial path remained three layers. A president could be a maintenance hand; a chairman could also manage records. A trade alias like the Water Director-General was never raised to a school-elder title. Only the five offices of Offices and Ranks went into the ledger cells.
The rivers and lakes were read by appearance, not as an owned cell.

At the Water Compact the Cold Current Art ran thick, and Iron Forging Art practitioners lived together on the Sinjeong depot side. Han Jaemok's hand was the Cold Current Art. Hiding turbid water cut that transmission, and in a state with wide water duty that cut shook the rations. At the Standards Alliance the Iron Forging Art overlapped the bolt rites. Gang Minseo's hand was the Iron Forging Art, and off-standard modification was cast out. At the Line Succession State the Iron Forging Art sat thick on the transshipment watches. Park Taegyeom's hand was that, and escorting was borrowed from the Yongsan garrison memory and convoy contracts. At the Escort Protection State the Guarding Wall Art and the Amsa Cold Current Art stood in tension under one emergency superintendence. Bae Ujin's hand was the Guarding Wall Art. The commander did not double as the Amsa treatment watch's Cold Current Art. Taewook Group chair Jeong Seoon announced her succession in April 2112 using her father's share documents and shareholders' minutes.

Among the lesser and theocratic states too, the hand did not follow the state. Yun Seorin of the Republic of Korea Government managed the Gwanghwamun seal chest. This was an accreditation duty, not martial training. On the Yeouido transmission watch the Thunder Call grew. The taboo against raising a living pastor's name onto the school remained at the Yeouido microphone stand as well. On the General Assembly register line of the Sermon Registry State there were hands of completed Iron Forging Art transmission. The Thunder Call and pulpit-lineage faith were not read as one line; the Thunder Call was a school and the pulpit lineage a line of Faith. The Presbyterians did not monopolize the Thunder Call.

The hand of Baek On of the Sangha Relief State had no martial path. The rivers-and-lakes branch was the Open Hand inside the order. The hand of Jang Sehwa of the Neutral Convoy City was the Iron Forging Art; she borrowed the Guarding Wall Art only when convoying. Borrowing was order-of-battle, not dual practice. The hand of Go Seojun of the Gate Military Government was the Guarding Wall Art. The Guui Cold Current Art could live inside the same state, but the commander did not double as it. I Hongwon of the Seocho Computing Group managed the cooling keys and barrier-gate ledgers as work, not martial training, and the rail cavalry was facility military, not a school. The heads of the Medical Neutrality League, the Cathedral Accreditation State, and the Central Technology Preservation Office had no martial path. Medicine, the altar, and technical inspection remained trades.

The Cold Current Art lived together at the lock-gate watches of Yeongdeungpo, Amsa, and Guui. The Water Compact did not monopolize the transmission. Even if the Iron Forging Art's oral record remembered the Changdong depot, that place was unclaimed-territory training, not a state seal. Suseo, Banghwa, Ttukseom, and Garak were not capitals either, and so were not written as school head temples.
The Water-Compact Rite is not raised to school doctrine. That water flowing proves the contract true is a sentence of faith
The bolt rite of the Open-Standards Rite does not replace the elder hand's edge
Pulpit lineage, occasionally the ledger-lineage transmissions
No living pastor's real name, church logo, or presbytery name goes onto the pedigree
The Protected-Water Rite of the sluice lineage and the drill of military remnants
The Muster-Remnant Rite is not merged into school taboo

The militaries of the sixteen states were organization names keeping facilities, like the sluice guards, the engineers, the barrier-gate combat teams, and the rail cavalry. Not guards, shock troops, or archers — and not other names for the schools. The Sinjeong–Bupyeong mobilization remnants, the Yongsan garrison memory, the Capital Defense Command remnants, and the northern home-front corridor of the conscription remnants operated overlapping those organizations. The Guarding Wall Art grew out of those remnants, but the four organizations were not read as schools. When the storage-track run and a rail-cavalry dispatch fought over the same rail, that was an organizational conflict, not a school matchup.

School transmission passes from person to person. Books alone do not admit anyone to a school, and when a master dies the transmission survives as oral record. Someone who learns two schools is injured when their training movements, equipment, and transmission conditions collide. When breath and endurance collides with body conditioning, cough and joint injury follow, with the same symptoms written in the waterborne-disease, asbestos, and cooling-water records.
A master was one kind of relation in the ledger. Not the same title as the priests of a faith chapel. Where this chapter spoke of transmission, it wrote martial master.
The five tiers of office and the martial ranks are separate. A president can be an apprentice, while a jusa clerk can be an elder.
A pre-entry relationship status. The person does the work but has not yet entered the school
Separate from martial ownership and proficiency, and independent of office tier
Has begun learning from a martial master
Can teach the tradition they have learned to others
Kept the taboo. Declared expulsion and casting-out
Being a head of state did not make one an elder

Whether dual practice holds is settled, regardless of office tier, by the clash of training movements, the compatibility of equipment, the practitioner’s health, and both schools’ transmission conditions. Someone who learns the combat arts, inner practice, and footwork of one school has learned that one school.

A dual-practice review is where a school teacher and the practitioner check the actual conditions of conflict together. Injuries from dual practice remain differently in each person. The review belongs to the school and sits apart from state accreditation, office, and criminal review.

An Guarding Wall Art squad attached under a convoy contract enters the unit’s organization. The shields and ranks Jang Sehwa borrows are that squad’s equipment and organization. Commanding units of different schools is separate from the commander’s own training.

Anguk Chongnim carries the Gaebang arts Hangryong Sip-pal Jang and Tagu Bongbeop as well as Shaolin martial arts. The Gaebang and Shaolin teachings pass through different lines within the order. Baek On supervises the order's records and shelter; the martial training belongs to its practitioners and teachers.
The following register, shelter and ration customs are not moves of Hangryong Sip-pal Jang or Tagu Bongbeop. They describe other work done in the same station corridors.
What it does not do in combat
The Anguk tablets, the register chests of the Bukhansan vacancy
Carries refugee names over and writes them in
Does not replace the Thunder Call's roll-call restraint
Concourses where the lodging oath lived
Divides the lines and holds the places open
Does not make the Guarding Wall Art's interval
Silence that raises no living name onto a school register
It is not the Thunder Call's line-up
Shares the remaining rations. Begging is not a weapon
It is not a combat tool

Silent remembrance before memorial tablets does not enter living people's names in the register. The Thunder Call's 'Halting on roll-call' acts on registered names. If 'Dividing evacuation lines' occupies a catwalk, the Cold Current Art cannot use that route. Neither interaction establishes a special matchup for the Open Hand's martial arts.

The Transfer Circle was not a school. Nor an organization gathered only from the addressless or the homeless. A mobile mutual-aid net in which station veterans, porters, repair hands, interpreters, care workers, traders, and lost travelers, each with a home and an affiliation, exchanged needed work.

Its members tied safe roads between stations, resting places, job leads, water and medicine, storage chests, and the last sightings of missing persons through ledgers and oral record. A record of kept promises became credit, and debts were repaid not only in goods but in labor, information, and care. No state or religion owned the Transfer Circle whole. Local circles could take different decisions on neutrality, taxes, and protection contracts.

Pickpocketing and smuggling were livelihoods that became disputes even inside the Transfer Circle. Even if some members touched them, not all members were called thieves. A member who monopolized a road or sold the weak's lodging lost their surety and was turned away at other stations. The player, rather than trusting rumor and stigma at face value, checked witnesses, hand-off ledgers, and the flow of goods.

Resonant-Aiming Method was not a school teaching only realistic firearms doctrine. When rare physical-AI lenses and sensors and drive assists attached, the master's movement looked faster than a person could follow. Threats in view were read in layers; recoil and body sway were assisted; and for short spans, engagements in several directions were held together. This effect was an exaggerated martial-arts feel made by equipment, and was not recorded as supernatural magic.

The price was plain. When power fell or the lenses clouded, the body returned to that of an ordinary marksman. Without ammunition or maintenance half the school vanished, and a wrong sensor classification could read a comrade as a threat. Left long to let the module judge in the user's place, it repeated the memory of loss of control. The elders of Resonant-Aiming Method set first not the strong but those who knew when to switch off the equipment and withdraw.

A severed arm folded that school's transmission in half. With a prosthesis the trade remained, and the martial path became a different line. Fitting an artificial hand did not bring back the Cold Current Art's transmission. As an efficacy-less stockpiled medicine does not fool a fever, medicine did not give the dead hand back.
That school's transmission folds in half
The trade may remain. The martial path is a different line
Movement and footwork is impaired first
The artificial leg leaves walking. The catwalk step and the storage-track run do not return
The axle echo and the roll-call die
The Iron Forging Art's inner breath, the Thunder Call's roll-call fold
The hearing aid leaves trade communication
A prosthesis went on only after the cut. The numbers spoke after it went on, and this chapter did not write them.

Individual shield art and staff methods serve in close fighting, while the shared ranks of the Guarding Wall Art and the Landing Escort Formation move by their commander’s organization. The Cold Current Art’s inner practice shows in fatigue, breathing, and focus during a fight. The Iron Forging Art’s hammer strike is maintenance work that tests repaired equipment.

A technique was the way the hand showed when that order matched the battlefield archetype, the order of battle, and the taboo. Whether water stood, whether equipment had been mended, whether the register was a true copy, whether the unit had halted — those were the premises. The same battle and the same order did not end in a different hand.
Where water stood, the Cold Current Art's breath ran long
Carrying hammer and shield was slow
Main hand-form. Floor changes, catwalks, storage tracks
Hydraulics and heavy weapons are stronghold gear. No personal carry begins
Restraint does not form while moving
A Cold Current Art hiding turbidity strikes with the transmission already cut
Main hand-form. The Iron Forging Art lives only on mended gear
Only what sat in the order of battle among the four layers
The side that cuts the number landing at once
Equipment is not mended by attacking
The face of roll-call and seal
The face of muzzle and staff. Model counts are not written
Regrouping is not a card; it connects only to maintenance and support after a halt
Movement and footwork is inactive during a halt
Main hand-form. The capture cord comes only after a halt
Main hand-form. Repair, the turbid-water confession, triple-copy collation

The aptitude of a battlefield archetype was quality. It was not counted by adding numbers. The Han crossing was the Cold Current Art's; the depot approach was the Iron Forging Art's; the short fronts of transfer-station floors and small station houses were the Thunder Call's; the single file of a tunnel was the Guarding Wall Art's; the surface ruins were where Guarding Wall Art mobility met the Thunder Call's roll-call. At a terminal's blocked end, Restraint was strong.

Sumentson is taught at waterworks and sluice posts. On October 14, 2026, Yeongdeungpo waterworks staff operated valves manually after remote control failed. Han Jeonghun entered 21:47 and the failure in the first line of the operations log.

Water was the wreckage of the system that had purified raw Han water and sent it on. After pumps, chlorine injection, and turbidity testing came down to human watches, this hand grew. When the tank-farming cells and the drinking-water cells used one surface, that day's cloudy water became the evening soup. Cooling water did not go onto the drinking ledger. When turbidity reading read cooling-water admixture as clear, the next waterborne disease opened on that watch's signature. Cutting the raw water was a watch bound to taboo, not a technique of the table. The Medical Neutrality League saw the dysentery and fever; the Cold Current Art cut the cause above the water's surface.
Walks only the wet iron grating
The different width of the archive aisle disrupts their stride.
Move. Crosses restricted links without breaking the file
Slipping. Risk of mixing farming and drinking cells
When the Open Hand's refugee line holds the rim, there is no road
Sharing one water surface between drinking water and aquaculture defeats maintenance and support
Grips the key like a staff but never aims it like a gun
The Guarding Wall Art's issue staff wins in length and interval
The key is not put on the armory register

Iron Forging Art is a martial path passed down through depot maintenance. Transmission passed person to person at the Sinjeong, Cheonwang, Godeok, and Sinnae depots. Changdong, Suseo, and Banghwa were unclaimed, so transmission there was dangerous and the standards elders came rarely. Skill grew through continued maintenance, and off-standard modification was cast out by the martial masters.

Neural-net weights could not be mended. Hoses, terminals, and lenses could. Recovered lostech was no personal universal weapon, and the seal bolt kept that boundary. Hydraulic structural equipment was the stronghold's gear. No one carried it without power.
Rests the hammer's beat to the standard count
The Cold Current Art's lock-gate breath differs in beat; dual practice injures the body
When the rail-cavalry dispatch crosses the same line, the military organization and the school fight
When the Guarding Wall Art's interval lock blocks the entrance, one cannot come out
Uses the spanner as a staff
Shorter than the issue staff. The standard hammer is the true hand
Modifying a lostech actuator onto a spanner — the elders cast it out

Thunder Call is a martial path taught by church elders and deacons through registers and roll-call. Transmission opened in the church aisles, the General Assembly registers, and the Yeouido transmission watches. No living pastor's real name or church logo went onto the school pedigree. The pulpit-lineage faith's right to preach and this school's roll-call could share a place but were not one line.
Uses roll-call as a signal while stepping to change position and interval
The Escort shield shoulder blocks the feet
Walking while avoiding the yellow line
Moves the front rank without stepping on the yellow line

leaves.text: The titles of Seoul in 2126 were not game terms. They were seats people in Korea understood in 2026, or seats Joseon had used before that. For a hand to open water and stamp the registers after the call mesh died, it had to hold rank.
The sixteen states used five office tiers, with titles differing by institution.

There was no emperor tier. Seoul had no son of heaven. The heads of the sixteen states did not call one another king. What they called each other was the tier-1 title of that nation; only the layer the ledgers assigned was of king rank.

The baron, count, duke, king, and court figures of Crusader Kings were layers of land. The opening fixed those layers as tiers 1 through 5 and wrote the names apart only by form of government and institutional rank. The feudal operating houses read from stationmaster down to jusa clerk; the military governments from commander down to byeongjang; the theocracies from Moderator, archbishop, and spiritual director down to gyosa, gyowoo, and sindo; the commercial states from chairman, guild head, presiding chair, company president, or order head down to jikwon, johapwon, hosongwon, and hoewon.
The great matters within a state — water, escort, registers, repair
One gu, the living sphere of a great station
One station, one sluice, one market
No land. Signature and watch only
B. Mapping to the existing classification
Rulers held tier one, while facility staff held lower tiers. States used different titles for the same five levels.

Real ranks were laid over the tiers. Feudal heredity, emergency superintendence, and laying-on-of-hands remained in the prose, while the titles themselves kept the words those institutions had used in 2026.
Government of the Republic of Korea
A. Republic of Korea Government offices

President—Minister—Vice Minister—Director General—jusa clerk. The ranks the Government Complex Seoul main building had used. The president at tier 1 was elected by the duty houses. Only the civil-service houses that had inherited the duty, generation after generation, held a vote. It was an aristocratic election that kept only the form of democracy. In 2126, Ministers, Vice Ministers, and Directors General divided the records, distribution, and approvals at Cheong Wa Dae and the affairs of districts and stations. The Government Complex Seoul main building handled security and passage at Gwanghwamun, Jongno 3-ga, and Euljiro 1-ga. The jusa clerk held no land. The government ruled Jongno and Jung-gu directly, and the duty houses fought over control of the city center and over the factions among themselves.

The president, ministers, vice ministers, directors and jusa clerks exercise executive duties. Legislative deliberation and judicial review are separate authorities; registering a bill or judgment does not make a minister its legislator or judge. The five tiers compare the sixteen states' offices, not hereditary lordships or military command.

The Sluice's tier 1 was an elected monarch, and the other four layers kept the watch grammar of the Yeongdeungpo Arisu Water Treatment Center. The representatives of the houses bound by water contracts elected the monarch in the contract council. The sluice house was the house that had produced the monarch most often, but the seat was not hereditary. The Bureau Head approved the great matters of treatment and dispatch, the District Head fed the gu, and the Watch Chief opened one sluice. The Junction's Stationmaster—Bureau Head—District Head—Watch Chief—jusa clerk were the watch grammar of the Yongsan rail transshipment. The stationmaster's seat remained primogeniture inside the track house. The Yongsan Station track house passed its keys to its grandson, the Bureau Head approved the great matters of dispatch, the District Head fed the gu, and the Watch Chief opened one storage track.

Commander—Chief of Staff—Battalion Commander—Company Commander—byeongjang sergeant. The military ranks where the conscription remnants and the treatment watch were bound together. The Amsa Station commander read waterworks protection as emergency superintendence, and the Guui Station commander had still not gathered sluices and the Achasan outposts into one hand. The Chief of Staff bore the great matters within the state, the Battalion Commander the gu, the Company Commander one bridge or ridge, and the byeongjang the watch that carried a signature alone.

Moderator—Elder—Gwonsa—Deacon—gyosa teacher. The session ranks left by the Yeonji-dong General Assembly Hall; the opening capital was Samsung Station. The Moderator read the General Assembly registers through hereditary laying-on-of-hands, the Elder held the great relief within the state, the Gwonsa the living sphere, the Deacon one church, and the gyosa the landless signature.

Archbishop—Priest—Brother—Deacon—gyowu fellow. The ranks of the Myeongdong Cathedral curia. The Archbishop kept the altar of marriage, adoption, and memorial accreditation; the Priest held the diocese's great matters, the Brother the district, the Deacon one altar, and the gyowu the landless signature. The Bishops' Conference building on Myeonmok-ro, Gwangjin, remained only an outer warehouse.

Spiritual Director—Head of the General Directorate—Abbot—Monk—sindo lay believer. The order's ranks of Jogyesa and the General Directorate at 55 Ujeongguk-ro. The mountain assembly elevated the Spiritual Director. The contest of votes among the lineage factions was the politics of that elevation. The Spiritual Director read the tablets and temple rolls with the capital's hand, the Head of the General Directorate held the order's great matters, the Abbot the temple's living sphere, the Monk one chapel, and the sindo the landless signature. Anguk Station was that capital.

Kyujeongwon Head—Senior Dharma Teacher—Dharma Teacher—Dharma Student—gyodo adherent. The charter ranks of the Heukseok-dong Seoul chapel and the Sotaesan Memorial Hall. The Iksan headquarters lay outside the city and entered no slot; the Heukseok Station Kyujeongwon head kept the transcribed charter. The Senior Dharma Teacher held the great matters, the Dharma Teacher the district, the Dharma Student one chapel, and the gyodo the landless signature.

Presiding Chair—Vice Chairman—Executive Managing Director—Department Head—jikwon staff. The corporate ranks of the former FKI Hall at 24 Yeouido-ro. The bloodline houses that held shares of the vault formed the investors' council, and they elected the Presiding Chair from among themselves. The Presiding Chair read the investment ledgers as the cooling key and closed Yeouido Station, the Vice Chairman held the affiliates' great matters, the Executive Managing Director the district, the Department Head one window, and the jikwon the landless signature. Lotte, SK, and LG were this corporation's retainers and opened no separate ranks.

Chairman—President—Executive Managing Director—Department Head—daeri deputy. The stock-company ranks of Samsung Town at Seocho-daero 74-gil and the Yangjae head office at 12 Heolleung-ro. The Chairman was the tier 1 to which the I-family operating house and the maintenance houses leased the keys; the President held the great matters of cooling and car bodies, the Executive Managing Director the Gangnam and Yangjae living spheres, the Department Head one intersection or depot, and the daeri the landless signature. Gangnam Station and Yangjae Station were each capital.

Chairwoman—Vice Chairwoman—Bureau Head—Branch Head—johapwon unionist. The federation ranks of the Kyunghyang Shinmun site at 3 Jeongdong-gil. The Chairwoman read the City Hall Station strike rolls as passage right, the Vice Chairwoman held the great matters of the gatherings, the Bureau Head the district, the Branch Head one window, and the johapwon the landless signature. Party names were not used as state names.

Guild Head—Standing Director—Director—Auditor—johapwon unionist. The guild ranks of the Guro and Geumcheon complexes and the Cheonwang depot. The Guild Head kept the bolt rites as a state, the Standing Director held the great matters of the standards, the Director the complex's living sphere, the Auditor one barrier gate, and the johapwon the landless signature. Guro Station was the capital.

Company President—Dispatch Chief—Squad Head—Scribe—hosongwon escort hand. The transport-contract ranks of the Sinnae depot. The company president's seat was hereditary in the founding house. The route licenses were the house's property. The Company President read the terminal transfers and the medical trains as neutral, the Dispatch Chief held the great matters of dispatch, the Squad Head the transfer living sphere, the Scribe one platform, and the hosongwon the landless signature. Sinnae Station was the capital.

Order Head—Attending Physician—Resident Physician—Orderly—hoewon member. The physician-seniority ranks of the Jegi-dong medicinal-herb market (Gyeongdong) and the eastern medical network. The Order Head supervised the attending physicians' clinical judgment and confirmed the succession of the resident the attending physician had named. The seat was apprenticeship, a master naming a successor pupil, not bloodline. The Order Head kept the treatment vow that did not distinguish friend from foe; the Attending Physician held the great matters of the Jegi-dong medicine market, the Resident Physician the district, the Orderly one sickbed, and the hoewon the landless signature. Jegi-dong Station was the capital.
The Table of Offices by State
A. Titles of the sixteen states
Government of the Republic of Korea
Company Commander / guard captain / site lead
A. Traces of Joseon official titles
In 2126 the ruler of the Sluice was a lord, the ruler of the Government a president, and the ruler of the Junction a stationmaster.
The chief of a county. The head-of-state cell of one of the sixteen states. Substituted by each nation's tier-1 title
The chief of a Six Boards office and the 2026 Bureau Head's approval. The cell of a state's great matters
The seat that fed one gu. The living-sphere cell
One station, one sluice. The stronghold cell
A seat with no land and a signature only. The working-rank cell
B. The Joseon Six Ministries and the division of duties

The names of the Six Boards were Joseon's Personnel, Taxation, Rites, War, Punishments, and Works. What actually moved at the opening remained four matters: water and rations, escort and the muster registers, accreditation and punishment, repair and standards. The personnel database had died with the call mesh, and the rites went to the churches, the temples, the shrines, and the chapels. The 2026 HR and general-affairs teams were not laid onto those seats.
In 2126, the leaders at Gwanghwamun, Yangpyeong, Yongsan, Amsa, and Samseong were respectively president, lord, stationmaster, commander, and church chair.
A. Keeping rank and livelihood apart
The sixteen states used their own institutional titles for their rulers.
B. Station titles and the Goryeo grade ladder

A title took a station name plus senior or junior, and its grade followed the Goryeo ladder of state duke, commandery duke, county marquis, county earl, founding viscount, and county baron. A ruler kept the country's own office title and was not called king. Land without a station remained a holding, while a station was the strategic strongpoint. Inside one realm the ruler granted only lower titles, and a king-rank ruler held at most two duke-rank titles directly.

The Sluice elected its ruler at a meeting of water-contract families. The Central Technology Preservation Office selected its director by examination. Myeongbu Church appointed its chair after elder approval.

leaves.text: At about 21:47 on October 14, 2026, remote control failed at the Yeongdeungpo waterworks. Duty officer Han Jeonghun operated the valves manually and entered the failure in the first line of a paper operations log.

At about 21:47 on October 14, 2026, district indicators went dark in sequence at the Blue House crisis center. Night officer Yun Taesik tried to report to the National Security Office and Joint Chiefs, but the lines did not connect.

On October 15, 2026, the president wrote and signed an emergency order under Article 76 of the constitution. The prime minister countersigned it. Designated facility emergency officers received on-site authority during the communications outage.

On November 6, 2026, two Yeouido vault representatives visited the Yeongdeungpo waterworks. Han Jeonghun agreed to open the valve toward Yeouido from 06:00 to 12:00 daily in exchange for two emergency generator parts.
Han Jeonghun entered the exchange in the operations log. The Yeouido vault also entered the parts and water exchange in its inventory under the same date.

On March 14, 2053, waterworks head Han Seokjin and six water-receiving family representatives met seven Yeouido family representatives. Fourteen representatives signed an agreement transferring management of eleven water facilities near Yeouido and Yeongdeungpo Station to the Yeouido families.
From March 20, 2053, the Yeongdeungpo waterworks staff moved their base to Yangpyeong Station underground. Forty-five volumes of Han Jeonghun’s logs moved there. The waterworks continued operating.
In June 2097, Sumunguk contracted with waterway workers in Yangpyeong and Chuncheon. They were entered in the Yangpyeong Station ration register in return for managing the waterways.
In winter 2120, Dongbangsa demanded registration of reconstruction workers from Gyugyeokmaeng in exchange for pump parts. Gang Minseo placed workers who refused in the civic register.
In 2123, a refugee procession from Bukhansan Bogukmun descended toward Anguk. Before its arrival, Baek On moved empty spaces in the refugee register to the citizenship column.
In 2123, Sumunguk, Gyugyeokmaeng, and Hwanjeokguk sent separate water, parts, and transit contracts to the minor states in the same week. Jeong Yura copied their end conditions into one document.
In November 2125, the records office compiled a power ranking of sixteen states.

leaves.text: A. How people and machines are placed

In the Seoul of 2126, at the opening, the bodies that founded states remained human. They slept in the concourses of Yeongdeungpo, Seoul Station, and Amsa, stood sluice watch, and lined up at the ration windows. In the same graph, stopped arms mixed with machines that still walked, and raptors, feral dogs, and rat swarms clung to the rations, the heat, and the wetlands. This was not a list that tried to revive in numbers the density of the years when the call network lived; it was a compendium that recorded what the Great Blackout cut off and what remained inside the stations.

On October 15, 2026, the president signed an emergency order authorizing designated facility officers to act on site during the communications outage. Yeongdeungpo waterworks staff manually operated valves that day.

On October 14, 2026, Yeongdeungpo waterworks officer Han Jeonghun started a paper operations log after remote control failed. In 2053, forty-five volumes of his logs were moved to Yangpyeong Station underground.
In 2106, the Republic of Korea required a Government Seoul Complex stamp on Jongno and Junggu passes. Commercial contracts needed that stamp for registration.

In winter 2120, Dongbangsa demanded registration of reconstruction workers from Gyugyeokmaeng. Gang Minseo entered those who refused in its civic register. In 2123, Baek On moved blank spaces in a refugee register to the citizenship column.

When the water was cut, labor folded first. Even when food ran short, the next day's hands slowed, and without medicine the act of treatment itself did not open. The way the illnesses of people and of the tanks overlapped at one window was covered by Ailments and Symptoms.

The robot density of Korean manufacturing in 2026 was recorded as 1,012 units per 10,000 workers, and the model field humanoid was Boston Dynamics' Atlas. Material transport with minimal supervision and trials on Hyundai Motor sites were that year's starting point (Atlas, accessed 2026-09-17; IFR 2024-11-20, accessed 2026-09-17). After the calls were cut, there was no foundry to lay the same line anew.

The bodies that remained at the opening fell into two kinds: remnants standing with frozen joints at their charging terminals, and remnants repeating only their last transport order. The maintenance sheds of the Guro complex blocks and the Cheonwang depot side, and the sealed cells of the Magok test section, were often named as their places. Mechanics swapped hoses, terminals, and lenses to make pumps and watch stoves, but they could not repair the neural-network weights as a whole. The lock that kept knowing, holding, repairing, and manufacturing out of a single sentence was in Lost Technology.
After the Great Blackout cut machines off from the upper control network, they repeated their last assigned search and guard tasks.

At the opening, Lee Yeon is a biological synthetic humanoid in Jo Jaepyo's company. The H01–H16 register instead records mechanical humanoids under house custody. Neither the kind of body alone grants nor denies personhood or citizenship. Each individual is assessed for expressed will, continuity of memory, and consent. A custody record can document maintenance and responsibility, but its transfer clause cannot govern someone recognized as a person. Lee Yeon signs her own courier judgment and can refuse an order that would sacrifice civilians. No such individual determination is recorded for the H01–H16 actors.

There were bodies that overlapped with the logistics humanoids but did not stand in the same line. They were machines that pre-collapse disaster agencies had meant to use for search, reinforcement, and pipe inspection, and when the upper control network fell away, they endlessly repeated the search, guard, and transport routines they had last received. Small swarms that glowed like lanterns, heavy machines that pushed rubble with hydraulics, and flat underwater shells were those three lines. The line names and seal coordinates were a creative layer, and this page did not prove any list of real 2026 deployments.

The triggers for restart were voltage, water level, and authorization signals. Stations with attached depots such as Sinjeong, Gunja, and Godeok, water treatment with attached sluices such as Yeongdeungpo, Ttukseom, and Amsa, and the galleries of the deep tunnels provided that stage. When a scout thrust a protocol card forward, only that line, that trigger point, and that command bundle could be paused for a while; there was no universal control. The detailed modules and the salvage economy were recorded by Lost Technology, and this compendium fixed only which mission's echo the machines still walking beside people were.

Capacitor modules only used the charge already stored and could not replace generators; cells aged, and without charging terminals the repetition broke off too. A workshop repairing hydraulics did not make it look as if the fabs had returned.
Raptors, Feral Dogs, and Rat Swarms

The more stable human rations became, the more animal density followed those windows. At dusk, flocks of crows settled on the transmission towers of Sangam and Nanji, the cables of the Han bridges, and the Yongsan catenary, while the waste heat of factory roofs and the sparks of overhead lines drew insects. People called them the Large-billed Crow, but the flock did not read the content of the radio waves; it learned only the order of sparks, work noise, and food. In the spring breeding season, the bridges, school passages, and the tops of evacuation stairs became circles of diving attacks. The index was the Large-billed Crow in the Bestiary of Ecology and Variants, and the field page was G02.

Feral dogs formed families along the walls of the Magok laboratories, in closed security passages, and on weedy lots, and at night they went down as far as the Noryangjin fish docks. Their rusted collar rings made a clinking of iron, so they were named the Feral Dog. They were closer to the result of the habits of 2026, when private shelters closed their doors and construction-site guard dogs lost their people in the evacuation columns, clinging for a century to dock leftovers and the sound of ration-cart wheels. The leader was not fixed. The coexisting kind that walked beside the ration carts was a learning of the same pack. G03.

Rats made states at the transfers. Where crumbs and the heat of insulated pipes overlapped at the junctions where the Gangdong-Amsa ration passages met the Eunpyeong-Seongbuk evacuation stairs, two or three core nests formed under the cable trays. The colonies were not locked as hosts of any special plague. They were only a density of food, warmth, and shelter. When their droppings damaged wire insulation, the guidance displays went dark, and in the dark passages people thought of contagion first. G05.

On the wetlands of the Han, Nanji, and Amsa and the drainage ponds of the Changdong depot, waterfowl and waders settled first, and when the food rose, raptors followed onto the wires. When the sluices were lowered unilaterally, the flocks shot up over the depot tracks and blocked the train movements. The name binding migratory birds and predatory birds into one colony was creative, but the stopovers of the Han and the depot ponds were places that existed in 2026 as well. G06.

Sweeping up the swarms with firearms was left as a last resort. Sealing, ration detours, and the collection of leftovers were closer to what guarded the human windows. Why the stations, tunnels, and depots were the skeleton of those windows was connected by The Structures Compendium.

Search and guard routines in sealed galleries stop when batteries fail or charging is lost. Lost Technology

leaves.text: The years of the Great Blackout
The emergency decree, the manual watches, the first casualty, the underground rolls. Outskirts unloading markets, Gangwon winter passes, and Daejeon fields.
Plant recovery, the gauge sheet, the track families, the church, temple and cathedral rolls, the debt. Imjin letters, Honam seed grain, Jeju boat repairs, and Taedong crossings.
The Yeouido deed, the certificate, the contract council, Yangjae and Gangnam, Jeong-dong and the government complex. Busan coastal sailings, northern freight handoffs, and the rotating Dokdo watch.
The Holy Assembly, the Orthodox Council, the Janggyeong order, the Preservation Office, the gut and the rolls. Honam producers refusing exclusive grain contracts.
The age of the line ends
State names, the vassal posts, the Guui clash, the records-office ledger. The Sluice’s contract name and Chuncheon’s market name.
The successions, the opening rulers, the strength ledger of 2125. The Tsushima expedition and withdrawal, and reports and confirmation of the Dokdo watch.

In 2126 O Gyeongjae took office as moderator of the Myeongbu Church. Confirmed by the elders, O Gyeongjae opened Im Hajun's will of three sheets to the general assembly's meeting room, but did not approve Han Jaemok's western expansion plan. Instead he agreed with the Sluice to seal jointly the original box of the pump maintenance process.

Im Hajun disappeared in the winter of 2125. The night before his disappearance Im Hajun sealed the copy box of the pump-cleaning process. The key to the sealed box was received by the board of elders together with the will of three sheets. At the next shift Im Chowon, Im Hajun's adopted child, confirmed the seal of the original box, and the fact was entered in the witness column of the three sheets. Yun Seorin, president of the Government of the Republic of Korea, withheld approval of the will and confirmed only the seal of the box.

In 2124 a box of counterfeit medicine came up at the Seoul Station auction. Ryu Eunbi, director of the White Cross, cut off all of the White Cross's dealings in that auction, and the same day Jeong Hojun, life-safety research chief of the Taeuk Group, broke the seal of the counterfeit specimen arrived in the Yangjae stacks.

In the Jeongdong Federation chair's direct vote of spring 2125 Jeong Yura was reelected. When the Seongnam Works and the Second Branch Workshop stopped work for ten days that autumn, Jeong Seoon, chair of the Taeuk Group, visited the Seongnam Works on the ninth day of the strike. When rumors of a bad harvest went round in 2124, Nam Yungyeong, archbishop of the Myeongdong Archdiocese, opened the emergency-ration car, and the public auction was put off one day.

In the autumn of 2125 turbidity in the western mains passed the standard. When Park Nuri, the purification supervisor, closed the western main valves and Han Jaemok, head of the Sluice, withheld his signature from the document restarting supply, I Seodam, chief of the Yangcheon district, claimed Yangcheon's veto at the contract council on the ground of that withholding.

In the winter of 2125 three states asked Jo Jaepyo's party at the same time to escort the same passage. I Yeon, the party's attending courier, had signed the scouting and escort reports in her own name since 2123. In 2124 the return net joined twelve living spheres from Gangnam-gu Office to Seolleung and Suseo, and Shin Jongmok recorded the list. The 2125 Yongsan transshipment contract went to one merchant house carrying Seo Hajin's guarantee. Junction stationmaster Park Taegyeom signed the contract.

When the return rosters of the Imjin temporary quarantine post are damaged and the Anguk reissue demands and the Gwanghwamun authenticity hearings open at the same time, the demand to open the family waiting lists first clashes with the demand to finish the roster check first.

When a change of Yellow Sea tides shifts the Yeouido sluice drainage schedule and the estuary wharf loading order at once, the duty side's demand to secure the sluice gates first clashes with the wharf side's demand to cut the loss of frozen freight.

When one of the three relay legs closes at the Yongsan transshipment shed and a substitute turnback line opens at Suseo, the records side, which would untangle the mismatched relay tables first, clashes with the escort side, which would use the limited turnback line first.

When a wagon weight record at the Amsa storage yard shows an anomaly in one car and Sinnae reassigns the transfer cars, the demand to publish the weight anomaly at once clashes with the demand to avoid delay in the winter fuel order.

When the public drawing of the Sangam transmission's residual bands and the Yeouido water-supply duty's pump hours fall in the same hour, the demand to secure the bands first and save the communications clashes with the demand to record the citizen-witnessed hash first and keep the receipt ledger's trust.
When a late reply reaches the contact records Min Woonggi left in the Gangnam District Office area, residents seeking to reopen contact and residents conserving power contest the next relay time.
When Shin Jun points to a route after hearing old call rhythms and vehicle vibrations, Shin Jongmok divides care between checking field records and preserving the child’s consent and rest.

If parts for the mobile return relay are recovered from a closed depot, Shin Jongmok and residents who need those parts for power must negotiate quantities. Min Woonggi's earlier maintenance records remain in Gangnam, but he is in Daejeon at the opening.
When first relay power competes with medical refrigeration, families awaiting contact and medical workers must decide the order of use.
After checking Shin Jun’s fragments against field records, node delegates weigh capture of a centralized relay, distributed maintenance and delayed contact if completion is postponed.

If a device entry with missing costs is found in the old relay records, demands to investigate past costs conflict with current relay power allocation. Min Woonggi's earlier work remains in those records, not at the opening-day Gangnam site.

In 2126 merchants and couriers entering Seoul bring accounts from across the peninsula. Seoul’s sixteen states negotiate passage and trade at their own gateways, but cannot decide whether people at the far ends of those roads will return or what they will sell. Arriving letters and recovered goods can open the following disputes.
A reply from Daejeon · Gangnam-gu Office

If contact is made after the opening and Min Woonggi’s reply reaches Gangnam-gu Office, the contact worker brings it to the residents. Min farms and repairs equipment in Daejeon and seeks parts, but makes no promise to return to Seoul. Seoul maintenance workers short of hands ask him to come back, while Shin Jongmok and the residents dispute whether maintaining contact should mean pressing for his return.

If the player sends parts and a reply, Seoul’s repairs are delayed but contact with Daejeon can continue. Min can refuse even an improved offer to return. Delaying this delivery keeps the parts in Seoul but leaves the next contact time uncertain, along with the dispute between residents seeking renewed contact and those conserving power.
The owner of the recovered ship · Yongsan

If an escort claiming to have joined the Tsushima expedition and a local collaborator bring the same recovered cargo to Yongsan, a dispute over shares begins. The escort cites the shipowner’s commission; the collaborator cites promises made during the 2118 landing. Shares left unsettled when the main force withdrew in 2119 confront a new sale in Seoul.

The player can seek witnesses to mediate, escort one claimant, or become involved by buying the goods. Failed negotiations can halt delivery or drive a claimant to another buyer; they need not end in a fight. Returnees’ testimony, injuries, and belongings reveal what happened at the port.
A request to light the lamp · A courier from the east coast

If a courier who says they were rescued on Dokdo arrives in Seoul asking to tell their family they survived, their former shipowner claims a living sailor must return to the ship. Revealing the post’s contact point makes aid easier to find but also lets the shipowner send people there. The watchkeepers want the sailor’s skills too, so the courier seeks to decide who may learn their name and meeting place.

If carriers taking cargo toward the east coast are about to leave Seoul, the courier seeks to load a reply without exposing the meeting place. As the shipowner’s pursuer follows the letter’s recipient, the player can escort the courier within Seoul, lure the pursuer onto another route, or divide the letters among other carriers. Before departure they decide whether to conceal identity in the letter or name the sailor with consent. Missing the deadline loses this delivery opportunity and requires finding another carrier. The courier’s testimony and checks on the ground can carry the work forward even without Shin Jun’s help.
Government of the Republic of Korea
Elected in the 2121 duty-house election. Read the original emergency order on inauguration day.
Elected by the contract council in 2119. Appointed I Seodam chief of the Yangcheon district the same year.
Elected by the council in 2121. Listed the technicians who refused registration on the citizenship roster in 2120.
Succeeded as stationmaster as eldest son after the death of the track house head in 2122.
Took office as commander in 2118. Put the restoration-service register in the military affairs box in 2123.
Approved by the shareholders' meeting in 2112. Two cadet-branch representatives unsigned. Entered in the genealogy without the generation character.
Elected by the investing houses in 2120. Stopped the Association channel's bulletins in 2123.
Named successor by the previous director in 2116. Cut off the Seoul Station auction dealings in 2124.
Elected in 2115. Signed the first joint order with Guui Defense Unit captain Tak Seoyun in 2121.
Succeeded to the presidency in 2118. In 2125, set seasonal departure times for ordinary and medical trains on the dispatch sheet.
Took office by the elders' confirmation in 2126. Opened the will of three sheets to the general assembly's meeting room.
Elected by the priests' private ballot in 2113. Opened the emergency-ration car in 2124.
Elevated by the mountain assembly in 2122. Moved the refugee roster's blank lines into the citizenship lines in 2123.
Took the chair after the succession examination in 2114.
Top of the director's examination in 2119. Took office March 1 the same year.
Elected by direct vote in 2120, reelected spring 2125. Jeong Seoon visited Seongnam on the ninth day of the strike.

Im Chowon is Im Hajun's adopted child. After Im Hajun disappeared in the winter of 2125, Im Chowon checked the seal on the original document box at the next shift. The confirmation was entered in the witness fields of the three wills.
Han Somi is a workshop representative at the opening.

Jeong Hojun is the life-safety research director at the Taeuk Group. In 2124, on the day a box of counterfeit medicine was offered at the Seoul Station auction, he opened the seal on a counterfeit medicine sample that had reached the Yangjae archive.
In November 2125 the records office entered the Government of the Republic of Korea, the Sluice, the Gauge, the Junction, the Eastern Command, and the Taeuk Group in the column of major powers.

The records office entered the Yeouido Investment Federation, the White Cross, Agwansa and Sinnae Transport in the column of lesser powers. The Yeouido Investment Federation issued the common currency, the White Cross held medicine, Agwansa held the Achasan gate and the water of the Guui sluice, and Sinnae Transport escorted freight for any side.

The records office entered the Myeongbu Church, the Myeongdong Archdiocese, the Anguk Order, the Seongha Group, the Central Technology Preservation Office, and the Jeongdong Federation in the column of minor powers.

The Government of the Republic of Korea rules Jongno and Jung-gu directly from Gwanghwamun. When it drew up the roster of Jongno and Jung-gu residents in 2069, the ration counter of the Government Complex Seoul issued food against that roster. In 2070 the complex standing guard corps drew up muster rolls for Gwanghwamun, Jongno 3-ga, and Euljiro 1-ga stations and took the rotating guard at the three stations. In 2106 it required the passes of Jongno and Jung-gu to carry the Government Complex Seoul stamp. Commercial contracts were entered in the records office only if stamped, and passes and contracts carried stamp taxes. From March 2111 the Sluice, the Eastern Command, the Achasan Gate, the Junction, Sinnae Transport, the Gauge, and the White Cross submitted originals of their heads' successions and treaties to the records office, and the records office returned stamped copies.

In June 2121 the Myeongdong Archdiocese, the Anguk Order, and the Jeongdong Federation renewed the complex stamps on the Jongno and Jung-gu passes and drew up the rosters for the downtown ration counter in records office forms.

In June 2123 the Onmin Council demanded that the Sluice submit a renewed declaration of obedience to the emergency order, but the Sluice did not sign the declaration. The Junction, Sinnae Transport, the Gauge, and the White Cross suspended their entries of successions and treaties with the records office, while the Eastern Command and the Achasan Gate kept registering. President Yun Seorin withdrew the demand. The eight states outside the succession registry owe the records office no duty of entry.

In December 2125 the Sluice, the Gauge, the Junction, the Eastern Command, and the Taeuk Group submitted documents to the records office mustering their own and their vassals' troops, and the complex guard corps kept the rotating guard at Gwanghwamun, Jongno 3-ga, and Euljiro 1-ga stations. The records office drew up no expeditionary muster document for the complex guard corps.

The duty houses contend over the presidential election, the confirmation of the records commissioner, the placing of the complex guard corps, and the stamp tax income. In May 2122 Kim Yeongyu gathered nineteen records clerks and formed the Onmin Council (穩民議). In August 2122 the Onmin Council submitted to President Yun Seorin a proposal to send the complex guard corps to the Sluice's border, but Yun Seorin did not sign the deployment proposal. In January 2123, when two groups of duty houses put forward different records commissioner candidates, Yun Seorin left the confirmation unstamped for three months. In April 2123 three groups of duty houses each submitted plans for dividing the stamp tax, and Yun Seorin ordered the stamp tax ledgers kept separately by the guard corps, the records office, and the ration counter.

leaves.text: Sindorim is the bottleneck between Yeongdeungpo and Guro. Loads bound from one to the other pass through a junction there.
The junction runs from an outer waiting point through the main cargo gate to an inner assembly point. A separate maintenance passage beside it admits only people and back loads.
A load of filter media can be split across several backs, so it can go through the maintenance passage.
A load of copper parts cannot be broken down or carried without equipment. It moves only through the main cargo gate.

leaves.text: In 2126 Seoul had sixteen states. In November 2125, the records office listed six major powers, four lever states, and six minor states.
The Sluice made Yangpyeong Station its capital, the Gauge made Guro Station its capital, and the Taeuk Group made Yangjae Station its capital.
On 14 March 2053 the Yeouido families posted the name Yeouido Investors Association. In October 2079 a sign for the Central Technology Preservation Office appeared near Heukseok Station.
Two states kept their names: the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Yeouido Investors' Association.

Nine states changed their names and kept the old ones as origin labels: the Sluice, the Gauge, the Junction, the Eastern Command, the Taeuk Group, the White Cross, the Achasan Gate, the Sinnae Transport, and the Seongha Group.

Five states had not existed in 2026. The Myeongbu Church, the Myeongdong Archdiocese, the Anguk Order, the Central Technology Preservation Office, and the Jeongdong Federation held a state name for the first time in 2126.

Major Powers, Lever Powers, and Minor Powers
In November 2125 the records office classified the states by vassals, control of essential services, and standing forces.
A major power had two or more vassals or ruled a district block directly, held a monopoly on a core function, and kept a standing armed force.
A lever power had at most one vassal but held an irreplaceable lever, such as currency, medicine, the Achasan gate and the Guui water, or the neutral convoy.
A minor power kept one station and one institution, with neither vassals nor an independent force.

The Government of the Republic of Korea (S06) was first. It held one vassal, Gyeonggi (Goyang), and ruled the downtown block of Jongno and Jung-gu directly. It monopolized the downtown ration, the rolls, the seal, and the stamp tax, and kept the office guard as a standing force.
The Sluice (S01) held two vassals, the First Sluice and the Second Sluice, monopolized the western water supply, and kept a sluice guard as a standing force.
The Gauge (S02) held two vassals, the First Branch Workshop and the Second Branch Workshop, monopolized the bolt gauge, and kept a workshop guard as a standing force.
The Junction (S07) held two vassals, the First Terminus and the Second Terminus, monopolized the Yongsan transshipment, and kept a track guard as a standing force.
The Eastern Command (S05) held three vassals, the First, Second, and Third Guard Districts, monopolized the eastern defense, and kept the Amsa guard as a standing force.
The Taeuk Group (S03) held two vassals, the Seongnam works and the Suwon works, monopolized the Yangjae machining, and kept a headquarters guard as a standing force.
The Yeouido Investors' Association (S09) held one vassal, the Yeongjong branch, and monopolized the issue of the common currency.
The White Cross (S13) had no vassal and monopolized medicine.
The Achasan Gate (S14) had no vassal and held the Achasan gate and the water of the Guui sluice.
The Sinnae Transport (S12) had no vassal and monopolized the neutral convoy that took no side in any war.
The Myeongbu Church (S04) kept the one chapel at Samseong and had neither vassals nor an independent force.
The Myeongdong Archdiocese (S15) kept the one cathedral at Myeongdong and had neither vassals nor an independent force.
The Anguk Order (S10) kept the one order at Anguk and had neither vassals nor an independent force.
The Seongha Group (S11) kept the one headquarters at Gangnam and had neither vassals nor an independent force.
The Central Technology Preservation Office (S08) kept the one copying seat at Heukseok and had neither vassals nor an independent force.

The Jeongdong Federation (S16) kept its capital and strike roll at City Hall Station. The Government Complex Seoul guard took priority for security and passage there. The station was shared by S06 and S16, while the surrounding dong remained under S06. S16 had neither vassals nor an independent force.
The Government's Central Base, Its Relations, and Its Internal Strife

The Government of the Republic of Korea was the first power. It held many technical assets and combat troops and ruled downtown Jongno and Jung-gu, around Gwanghwamun, directly. That strength stood on four grounds.

The authority of the emergency order. The Eastern Command and the Achasan Gate were subject to the government in the form of registering successions and treaties with the records office. The Sluice, the Junction, the Sinnae Transport, the Gauge, and the White Cross also registered successions and treaties there. A succession not registered was not recognized as a state within the order lineage.
The downtown ration and rolls. The government ran the resident rolls and the ration windows of Jongno and Jung-gu. A person absent from the rolls received no ration downtown.
The seal and the stamp tax. Passage, trade, and contracts downtown stood only with a government seal and paid the stamp tax. A document without the seal was waste paper downtown.
The office guard. A standing guard with muster rolls held the downtown stations. The guard kept the office, the ration windows, and the seal windows at once.
In June 2121, the Myeongdong Archdiocese, Anguk Order, and Jeongdong Federation renewed government stamps on passage permits and prepared distribution registers in the records office format.
In March 2111, seven states submitted succession and treaty originals to the records office.
In May 2122 Kim Yeongyu gathered nineteen records officers and formed Onminui.

The Eastern Command and the Achasan Gate were independent commands that were also subject to the government. States that registered successions and treaties with the records office or used the government stamp and roll supported the government. States with no such tie were independent.

The thirteen vassals were not among the sixteen states. Five major powers divided eleven of them, while the Government of the Republic of Korea held Gyeonggi (Goyang) and the Yeouido Investors' Association held the Yeongjong branch.

The other nine states had no vassals: the White Cross, the Achasan Gate, Sinnae Transport, the Myeongbu Church, the Myeongdong Archdiocese, the Anguk Order, the Seongha Group, the Central Technology Preservation Office, and the Jeongdong Federation.

The states without a state religion were the Yeouido Investors' Association, the Government of the Republic of Korea, the Jeongdong Federation, Sinnae Transport, and the White Cross. The Central Technology Preservation Office leaned on the Sutra School only outwardly and had no state religion.
Diplomacy followed three religious blocs and secular neutrality. Water, parts, rail, and money crossed those blocs, so faith and interests diverged.
The Holy War Assembly bloc comprised the Myeongbu Church, Eastern Command, Achasan Gate, and the Seongha Group.
The Orthodox Assembly bloc comprised the Myeongdong Archdiocese, the Junction, and the Taeuk Group.
The Sutra School bloc comprised the Anguk Order, the Sluice, the Gauge, and the Central Technology Preservation Office. The Preservation Office belonged only outwardly.
The five without a state religion—the Yeouido Investors' Association, the Government of the Republic of Korea, the Jeongdong Federation, Sinnae Transport, and the White Cross—were secular neutrals.
Three tensions were visible at the opening.
The Sluice bore a grudge against the Yeouido Investors' Association over reclaiming Yeouido.
In February 2114 the Taeuk Group asked the Orthodox Assembly to confirm Jeong Seo-on's succession as legitimate inheritance. The Orthodox Assembly received the request but did not answer.
The Holy War Assembly persecuted shamanism.
The sixteen states were read as living areas that linked waterworks, depots, headquarters, assemblies, transfer stations, and mountain-refuge corridors. Their capitals were subway stations.

The sixteen states were not a flat partition of Seoul. Waterworks, rail yards, headquarters, assemblies, transfers, and the fortress corridors were read together as living zones. This placement was the creative control at the opening, and only the locations of public facilities were marked as measured. A capital was a subway station, and a state name was not a station name.

Migrant settlements continued in Daerim and Garibong, Itaewon, Dongdaemun, Guro and Gasan, and Yongsan. The Yongsan fence workers served inside the Junction.

The Government Complex Seoul main building handled security and passage at Gwanghwamun, Jongno 3-ga, and Euljiro 1-ga. Jogyesa, Myeongdong Cathedral, and the Jeongdong union office were facilities held by their respective states inside Government-held dong.

leaves.text: In Seoul subway stations, concourses, platforms, passages, and tunnels join at different levels. Waterworks, depots, and markets stand by the stations.
Concourses and platforms open in stages under the residents' rules. Changes to underground facilities and the surface surroundings shape each stronghold.

After the encounters and the combat, seizing the initiative in a station was only the beginning. This stronghold, where fates, goods, and reputation crossed, showed its true face only when the door was opened and the party stepped in.

The strongholds recorded in the Seoul station catalog held multi-story structures and convenience-facility sectors of their own. Whether a station was a transfer station or an ordinary one changed the scale of facilities it could seat. The Yeongdeungpo, Ttukseom, and Guui treatment plants, the Sinjeong and Cheonwang depots, Garak Market, and the Noryangjin Fisheries Market stood beside stations, forming vast infrastructure to meet the survivors.

Stations have different rooms on each level. Ordinary stations have smaller facilities, while transfer stations have larger ones. Markets, aid stations, repair workshops, generators, water-supply facilities, warehouses, and signal stations can occupy them. A nearby waterworks or depot changes how the station is used as a stronghold.

The station interior was a many-layered battlefield. The battlefield was a three-dimensional space that had to be scanned and commanded freely up, down, left, and right, and the commander could at any moment read the situation and tune the units' positions and formations precisely.

A small station house, a tangled transfer station, a terminal where the tracks ended, a collapsed tunnel, surface ruins, a vast depot, a rail bridge crossing the Han — the shape of the battlefield changed with each stronghold's character.
Facilities and the Distribution of Goods
Each facility devoured labor, power, and raw materials to keep turning. A facility cut from power stopped in its tracks, and a stronghold grown past its reach met the limit of its management.
The Structure of the World Map

leaves.text: A. How stations and tunnels are laid out

The Seoul of the time was not a flat administrative map but a graph of stations, tunnels, and sluices. Even in 2026 people crossed gu by subway, and the treatment centers and depots sat as the heavy nodes of that graph. On the night of the The Great Blackout, when remote control died, stations became fortresses and the centers of states, tunnels became licensed passage, and treatment plants and sluices became lock gates that opened only under signature. A century on, the sixteen states of 2126 read those points and lines as living spheres and never changed gu names into state names.

The Seoul Station Catalog records 334 observed-name rows for 315 stations. The Structure of the World Map records 25 gu and their assembly order; Seoul and the Subway Layers records six layers. Building use is recorded in River, Gu, and Dong Building Reuse.

A station brought people, facilities, and connections back into use. In a dong with a subway station, the station building was the core facility; distribution, passage tolls, lodging, and refuge were handled there. Schools, community centers, and hospitals supported it. After the March 14, 2053 agreement, the Yeouido houses managed eleven water facilities around Yeongdeungpo Station. From 2106, passes for Jongno and Junggu carried the Government Seoul Complex stamp from Gwanghwamun. Amsa Station administered water and escort protection from its platform. Sindorim was the bottleneck between Yeongdeungpo and Guro, while Suseo held a southern depot and contract administration. The parties and signatures of the 2053 agreement were recorded in the oral records.

A station has six layers: surface ruins, the concourse, platforms and tracks, transfer corridors, deep tunnels, and depot adjacency. Markets, homes, and offices occupy the concourse; people and freight move through the platforms; toll collectors hold the transfer corridors. The facilities adjoining each station are recorded in Entering the Station Interior. The terms by which a stronghold holds its territory are recorded in Strongholds and Territory.
In 2106, Jongno and Junggu passes and commercial contracts received a Government Seoul Complex stamp. A counterfeit medicine box appeared at a Seoul Station auction in 2124.

Between station and station lay lines that were never erased. Only the states changed — normal, hazardous, controlled, blockaded, flooded, collapsed, provisional repair — and cause and repair conditions followed. Yeongdeungpo–Sindorim and Sindorim–Guro were adjacencies the current map already knew, and no line skipped Yeongdeungpo–Guro in one cell. The full catalog's adjacencies went up as design data as 435 drawn from map points.

A transfer station cut from power stopped the traction freight flow even with both tunnels sound. Provisional repair passed only foot and light freight; heavy freight and armed passage took separate approval. The deeps were the seat of covert movement and maintenance, but flooding and communications loss came first. The formulas of throughput, isolation, and overreach were locked in Logistics and Infrastructure.

Since 2026, machines have repeated their last search and guard routines on surviving tracks, while rat colonies nest in cable trays beneath the transfer shops. Machines working or moving beside people are recorded in People and Machines. The tracks retain their 2026 connections.

Depot area reflects the rolling-stock storage and maintenance scale of 2026; post-collapse operations are fictional. Eight depots lie within Seoul: Sinjeong, Cheonwang, Banghwa, Gunja, Godeok, Changdong, Sinnae, and Suseo. Sinjeong corresponds to the Sluice, Cheonwang to the Gauge, Godeok to Eastern Command, and Sinnae to Sinnae Transport. Banghwa, Gunja, Changdong, and Suseo are unclaimed or edge corridors. No capital depots are assigned to Magok research, Ttukseom workshops, Changdong wheels, or Suseo protection. Jichuk, Dobong, Moran, and Gimpo lie outside the Seoul slots.

A depot was the seat of repair, bulk storage, and siege. Sinjeong's unloading and Godeok's train maintenance became a state's arms of legitimacy because the hands that moved a stopped train again or sent a convoy were there; Changdong's wheels and brakes lost their owner and remained only as leases in neighboring heads' ledgers. The drainage ponds became the water surface where tank aquaculture and migratory birds overlapped, and in the deep bays of maintenance sheds the sealing of looping chassis attached as a creative layer. The charging terminals and hydraulic hoses were the repair layer of Lost Technology.

The industrial blocks of Guro and Geumcheon clung to the depots and used schools for drying parts, and the residential shells of Dobong and Nowon could not hold water without Changdong. Depot names were not raised to state names. The wheels and dispatch that people watched over became the state names.
A. Water plants and their watches

On October 14, 2026, Yeongdeungpo waterworks officer Han Jeonghun operated valves manually after remote control failed. Under the March 14, 2053 agreement, Yeouido families took management of eleven water facilities near Yeongdeungpo Station. The waterworks staff moved their base to Yangpyeong Station underground on March 20.

On November 6, 2026, Han Jeonghun received two emergency-generator parts and agreed to open the water-pipe valve toward Yeouido every day. The transaction was recorded in the oral records. Representatives of both sides also signed the March 14, 2053 transfer of water-facility management rights.

The first floors north and south of the Han, and the tributaries Jungnang, Anyang, Tan, Cheonggye, and Hongje, decided which dongs got wet. Yeouido, Ichon, Banpo, Jamsil, Mangwon, Hapjeong, Amsa, Guui, and Jayang were read as main-channel waterfront. Habitation pushed above the third floor and the ration windows sat inside the embankment. The details of the waterfront rules were already written by River, Gu, and Dong Building Reuse.

Passages were the narrow lines where transfer, maintenance, and refuge overlapped. The transfer corridors were the hubs of politics and logistics between lines, and blockades, transit tolls, and congestion came first. The junctions where the Gangdong and Amsa ration corridors met the Eunpyeong and Seongbuk evacuation stairs became the warm nests of the rat colonies, and the fictional Sindorim junction split the main freight door from the maintenance passage that took only people and packloads, using siege as its stage. This junction is not among the catalog's 334 observed-name rows. The Sindorim incident's location is recorded in the Scenario Timeline.

The vertical connections were stairs, elevators, and ventilation shafts. Flooded floors showed cause and repair conditions and kept people out — that was the design. The Bukhansan Bogukmun mountain refuge roads, the Jegi-dong herb unloading, and the lower passages under the Noryangjin elevated joined the same graph from outside the stations. Connections were never deleted. Their states changed, and those states changed the times of rice, medicine, and convoys.

Garak Market, Gangseo Market, Yanggok Market, and Noryangjin Fish Market are facilities around station hubs. Garak handles price discovery rather than production. Noryangjin relies on refrigeration and ice credit, so it cannot keep goods frozen when power fails. Convenience stores and clinics remain trades around the stations.
Fortress, ration windows, the centers of states
Adjacent lines drawn from map points, transfers
Licensed passage, the states of flooding and blockade
Repair, rolling stock, wheels and convoys
The Structure of the World Map
Transit tolls, leftovers and heat, detours

DOC:Values-and-Policy-Scales.selector: p, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, blockquote, pre, li, th, td

leaves.text: A. Purpose of the Values Scale

What moved a person was not only temperament, ambition, and fear. Faced with the same issue, the means chosen diverged according to ten values cells. Organizations likewise took no eternal national personality; they stood on the values of the current charter and policy slots. When a leader was replaced, the numbers engraved in the charter went through a natural re-review, in the same vein as the "no fixed national personality" principle mentioned in Ambitions.

The scale ran from −100 to 100. Zero meant only that the axis had not yet tipped; it did not stand for the virtue of indifference. The axes of desire and preference were recorded separately. The numeric ledgers were values-cast.json and values-orgs.json.
Left is negative, right is positive.
Emergency powers, water cutoffs, protection governments

If values were the gradient on public issues, desire worked as the axis on which with whom and how one wanted to entangle shook decisions. It was read together with ambition and fear. Bonds made without the counterpart's consent, abuse of office, and material involving minors did not go into these cells.
Orientation: opposite sex / same sex / both sexes / none / fluid. Bonding: monogamy / multi-partner / contract cohabitation / non-exclusive / none.
Desires: longing _ | possessiveness _ | risk _ | display _ | duration _ | orientation _ | bonding _

Organization values were likewise built on the same ten axes as persons. The numbers were scored against the current charter, council majorities, and ledger practice. The authority number Han Jaemok carried as an individual could differ from the authority number of the Water Compact he belonged to, and it was precisely in that difference that issues budded.
As in the Stellaris policy system, each slot was given choices. The numbers here were not slot strength but simple choice codes.
What it looked like in Seoul
Garrison only / protection army / preemptive occupation
House secret / licensed sharing / joint ledger
Monogamy license / contract cohabitation / house bonding / military-register bonding / open bonding
Marriage and cohabitation ledgers. Organizations did not assign sexual taste
Operating houses HC and HP and external theaters XT use the same fields. House records appear in the world narrative atlas.
Seventeen Key Persons at the Opening

A positive qualification value meant proximity to examinations and apprenticeship. Im Chowon and I Hongwon stood high on this number, and Bae Ujin showed steep gradients on the force and authority items.
Values stood for the practice the current majority followed.
