leaves.text: An administrative map lays out Seoul from Jongno-gu to Gangdong-gu. The rail network has 315 stations reconciled from 334 observed name rows and the tunnels connecting them. Seoul Station, Sindorim, and Yeongdeungpo are major strongholds.

The geography that grounded the new age consisted of the 25 autonomous districts, the principal stations within them, the key facilities at their sides, and the spheres of the sixteen states. How buildings and facilities found new uses after the collapse was an important key to understanding the survivors' lives.
Related documents: Seoul and the Subway Layers, the Sixteen States of Seoul, Seoul region-setting data, the Seoul Station Catalog, Entering the Station Interior, Travel and Encounters.
The district names used the KOSTAT GeoJSON properties.name as they stood, and all twenty-five were present without omission.

Jongno-gu, Jung-gu, Yongsan-gu, Seongdong-gu, Gwangjin-gu, Dongdaemun-gu, Jungnang-gu, Seongbuk-gu, Gangbuk-gu, Dobong-gu, Nowon-gu, Eunpyeong-gu, Seodaemun-gu, Mapo-gu, Yangcheon-gu, Gangseo-gu, Guro-gu, Geumcheon-gu, Yeongdeungpo-gu, Dongjak-gu, Gwanak-gu, Seocho-gu, Gangnam-gu, Songpa-gu, Gangdong-gu.

These twenty-five remained the world map's core sectors, and the sixteen states laid their spheres over these districts. Yeongdeungpo-gu was not renamed the Water Compact, nor Jongno-gu the Republic of Korea Government.

The Seoul station catalog records 334 observed-name rows. The wiki map displays 315 stations after joining official subtitles and spelling variants. The outer metropolitan network extends beyond them. Names such as Seoul Station, City Hall, Gangnam, Jamsil, and Yeouido are still used for their strongholds.
Among the 315 Seoul stations on the wiki map, Gangnam-gu and Songpa-gu each have 23, while Geumcheon-gu has four. Major movement routes cross around Yeongdeungpo, Sindorim, and Guro.
The vast infrastructures essential to the survivors' maintenance of their spheres sat beside the stations.
The water-treatment plants stood at Yeongdeungpo, Ttukseom, Guui, and Amsa, and Gangbuk (Namyangju) and Gwangam (Hanam) also worked as principal water-pressure sources.
The depots lay at Sinjeong, Cheonwang, Banghwa, Gunja, Godeok, Changdong, Sinnae, and Suseo, and the outer depots at Jichuk, Dobong, Moran, and Gimpo were also key strongholds.

The principal markets where bulk goods moved — Garak Market, Gangseo Market, Yanggok Market, and the Noryangjin Fisheries Market — formed the skeleton. Beyond them, hospitals, fire stations, police stations, substations, and rail marshaling yards remained beside the stations, backing each stronghold's role.
Laying the Sixteen States Over the Districts

The states did not replace the districts. Sixteen-States.md was the standard for the spheres' arms and key infrastructure. The Yeouido waterfront and the Ttukseom workshops, the Amsa treatment plant, and the Seoul Station records were read as the skeleton of the spheres.
Yeongdeungpo treatment plant, Sinjeong depot, rail and Han River bridges
Manufacturing and repair, Cheonwang depot, southwestern outskirts
Depot car bodies and rigging at Yangjae, surviving field humanoids, southern perimeter and outer links
Samsung Station megachurch southern pulpit axis
Samsung Station church real estate, Yeonji-dong General Assembly registers and relief
Amsa treatment plant, Godeok depot, eastern bridges
Government of the Republic of Korea
Administrative records, the Seoul Station emblem, central disaster medicine
Central rail transshipment, garrison-fence labor contracts, strait and beyond-the-fence outside links
Fisheries wholesale, cold storage, southern gate and medicine
The Yeouido hall, investment ledgers and the cooling key, West Sea and financial outside links
Anguk Station Jogyesa central tablet axis
Jogyesa and General Directorate tablets, temple rolls, rite calendar and relief
Gangnam Station intersection southern commercial axis
Samsung Town, the Gangnam cooling key, southern-outskirts memory
The medicinal-herb market, eastern medicine, rail
Guui treatment plant, Achasan, eastern bridges
Myeongdong Cathedral altar, accreditation of marriages, adoptions, and memorial rites, diocesan registers
City Hall Station Jeongdong central register axis
Strike rolls, City Hall Plaza gatherings, Jeongdong offices

The opening map derives surface control at 311 stations from the territory register. City Hall has a separate shared-control record for the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Jeongdong Federation, with government security taking priority. Gwangmyeong Sageori, Daechi, and Seoksu lie outside the mapped surface regions; each station's interior has its own control record.
The single stronghold called a station divided into several vertical layers. Concourse, transfer corridors, deep tunnels — each layer carried its own role and its own lurking dangers.

The passages joining layer to layer and station to station changed state without pause as events — collapse, flooding, control, blockade — passed over them, and this bore directly on logistics and on the survivors' movement.

DOC:World-Unbinding.selector: p, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, blockquote, pre, li, th, td

leaves.text: At about 21:47 on October 14, 2026, district indicators went dark in the Blue House crisis center. Remote control and external power also failed at the Yeongdeungpo waterworks. This event was the Great Blackout.

In 2026, humanity ran factory robots, logistics humanoids, orbital relays, mobile networks, semiconductor fabs, and grid SCADA on one chain of command. When the authority that had called the fleets fell out of that network all at once, the machines carried no malice; they repeated the last search, patrol, and transfer orders they had received. The week in which factories could no longer remake the same goods opened in the manner of a severed call. The opening of the game fell one hundred years after the Great Blackout, in 2126, because the clock on which manufacture died and the clock on which society changed overlapped.

The opening campaign centered on Seoul's sixteen states and subway routes. Beyond Seoul, settlements across the Korean Peninsula rebuilt parts of their roads and waterways. Letters, goods, and people reached Seoul through successive handovers. Returnees from the Tsushima expedition described the harbor where they had fought; their accounts did not establish the state of the Japanese mainland. News from China and the United States remained fragmentary.

On October 15, 2026, the president signed an emergency order and the prime minister countersigned it. Designated facility emergency officers received on-site authority during the communications outage.
A. Halted manufacturing and the change of generations

High-density batteries, authorization chips, and the weights held in the cloud could not be made again within one generation. That single limit ruled out an opening only six years later. In 2032, adults who had survived the Great Blackout would still have opened the sluices. While hands that remembered when emergency authority was supposed to be returned were alive, a state would not have hardened into a feudal order. Markets, district mayors, and boards of directors did not die merely because people told their story aloud.

On March 14, 2053, Han Seokjin and six family representatives met seven Yeouido family representatives and signed an agreement. After the transfer of management rights, the waterworks staff moved their base to Yangpyeong Station underground.

At about 21:47 on October 14, 2026, district indicators in the Blue House crisis room went dark one after another, beginning with Ulsan.

That day remote control and outside power failed at Yeongdeungpo waterworks. Staff started the emergency generator and operated valves manually. Han Jeonghun entered 21:47 and the control failure in the first line of a paper log.
On October 15, 2026, Government Seoul Complex staff copied the emergency order eight times and sent copies to designated facilities, including the Yeongdeungpo, Amsa, and Guui waterworks.

Seoul's States and the Peninsula Beyond
A. Water supply and the neighboring regions

After the Great Blackout, Seoul retained a network of stations where signatories managed water. Stations maintained tanks and temperature. Seoul and the Subway Layers described the grid itself. Han River treatment works and sluices endured through human duty shifts; that duty became the legitimacy of the Water-Supply Covenant Court.
In 2100 Hwanjeokguk collected tolls at rail termini in Incheon and Paju. In 2102 Gyugyeokmaeng incorporated workshops in Cheonan–Asan and Siheung as branch workshops.
A. The outside as seen from Seoul
Factory physical-AI density was lower than in South Korea and China; labor and artillery were substantial.

Letters from Kaesong and Hwanghae reached the Imjin return corridor. Residents around Pyongyang maintained sections of the Daedong crossings, while northern east-coast settlements passed goods along shorter surviving links. These local ties established neither a single northern government nor modern nuclear force projection into Seoul. The survival of twentieth-century firepower remained undecided.
Robot density in 2023 was 470. The coastal export and automation belt depended on the stack.
The coast died first. The inland grain belt was a rumor. The People's Liberation Army had no modern projection at the opening.
Atlas-type machines and cloud logistics had already reached Korean worksites.
With the same stack undone on the mainland, there was no Pacific rescue of the 2026 kind. The Incheon trust was a lottery for the remaining orbital resources.
